candidates.title: EmoBench-M: Benchmarking Emotional Intelligence for Multimodal Large Language Models
candidates.abstract: With the integration of multimodal large language models (MLLMs) into robotic systems and AI applications, embedding emotional intelligence (EI) capabilities is essential for enabling these models to perceive, interpret, and respond to human emotions effectively in real-world scenarios. Existing static, text-based, or text-image benchmarks overlook the multimodal complexities of real interactions and fail to capture the dynamic, context-dependent nature of emotional expressions, rendering them inadequate for evaluating MLLMs' EI capabilities. To address these limitations, we introduce EmoBench-M, a systematic benchmark grounded in established psychological theories, designed to evaluate MLLMs across 13 evaluation scenarios spanning three hierarchical dimensions: foundational emotion recognition (FER), conversational emotion understanding (CEU), and socially complex emotion analysis (SCEA). Evaluation was conducted on 27 state-of-the-art MLLMs, using both objective task-specific metrics and LLM-based evaluation, revealing a substantial performance gap relative to human-level competence. Even the best-performing models, Gemini-3.0-Pro and GPT-5.2, achieve the highest scores on EmoBench-M, 70.5 and 66.5 points. Specialized models such as AffectGPT exhibit uneven performance across EmoBench-M, demonstrating strengths in certain scenarios but generally lacking comprehensive emotional intelligence. By providing a comprehensive, multimodal evaluation framework, EmoBench-M captures both the strengths and weaknesses of current MLLMs across diverse emotional contexts. All benchmark resources, including datasets and code, are publicly available at Emobench-M , facilitating further research and advancement in MLLM emotional intelligence.

candidates.title: Souffleur: A Glanceable Display for Mobile Voice Conversations
candidates.abstract: The speech capabilities of mobile devices have grown, but their displays still rely on a text-based chat. When resuming a voice chat after a context switch, the last messages may not convey the key points of the conversation. Autobiographical use and sessions with external participants led to design goals for a mobile-first, speech-driven, glanceable display that helps users continue their reasoning from where they left off. We implement these goals in Souffleur and evaluate it in a between-subjects study with 48 participants. Compared with a conventional chat transcript, we found no reliable difference in how easily participants followed and resumed short voice conversations, nor in effort, attention or recall, although Souffleur reduces the conversation to a few short phrases.

candidates.title: Phygital customer experience and the adoption of immersive technologies in hospitality: an exploratory study with a value co-creation perspective
candidates.abstract: Purpose This study aims to explore immersive-technology adoption in hospitality through the Phygital Customer Experience (PH-CX) framework. PH-CX extends existing technology acceptance, service-dominant logic, omnichannel and customer-journey perspectives by emphasizing embodied, co-created and human-centered experience across physical, digital and artificial intelligence (AI)-mediated interactions. Design/methodology/approach Using Bayesian Networks, the study examines probabilistic dependencies among perceived usefulness, collaborative value, responsive co-creation attitudes and intention to use immersive technologies. Data was collected from 208 participants exposed to an AI-supported immersive hotel journey scenario. The analysis is exploratory and identifies conditional associations rather than causal effects or latent-variable relationships. Findings Adoption intention was conditionally associated with perceived usefulness, collaborative value and responsiveness to service innovation. The findings suggest that immersive-hospitality engagement involves functional, relational and participatory conditions beyond usefulness alone. However, the item-level results are hypothesis-generating and do not demonstrate PH-CX’s incremental predictive superiority over technology acceptance model (TAM) or service-dominant logic. Research limitations/implications The scenario-based, cross-sectional bayesian network (BN) design cannot model latent constructs, measurement error, mediation or causal effects. Future studies should validate PH-CX dimensions and compare TAM, TAM-plus-service-dominant logic (SDL) and PH-CX models using structural equation modeling, longitudinal designs and holdout-sample prediction. Practical implications Hotels can implement PH-CX through phased AI concierge pilots, cross-platform data integration and guest co-creation mechanisms. Relevant metrics include booking conversion, AI resolution rates, cross-channel engagement, co-creation participation and net promoter score (NPS). Ethical implementation requires transparency, opt-in participation, privacy safeguards, accessibility and human escalation options. Social implications Human-centered phygital hospitality requires safeguards against digital exclusion, surveillance and loss of human warmth. Transparency, agency, equity, privacy and non-digital alternatives are essential for inclusive and trustworthy service innovation. Originality/value The study advances PH-CX as a theory-extending framework linking usefulness, co-creation, embodied experience and ethical safeguards in immersive hospitality. It also proposes experience-design orientation as a future research profile and offers a phased implementation framework for responsible phygital service design.

candidates.title: Adapting Character Personalities: Emotional Resonance in the Transition of Comics to Animation
candidates.abstract: Abstract This paper explores how the adaptation of comic characters into animation reshapes personality and enhances emotional resonance. Rather than a simple shift from static panels to moving images, adaptation is treated as a creative process of negotiation between source material and reinvention for new audiences. Grounded in adaptation theory, transmedia storytelling, and semiotics, the study examines two case studies: Spider-Man: Into the Spider-Verse (2018), a Western example of superhero reinvention through multiverse storytelling and stylistic experimentation, and YuYu Hakusho (1992), a manga-to-anime adaptation that deepens shōnen characterisation and emotional engagement. The analysis demonstrates how animation extends character identity through movement, voice, and pacing, while also navigating challenges of localisation and cultural translation. The findings suggest that the sustainability of transmedia franchises depends on deliberate planning that preserves essential identity traits while allowing flexible reinterpretation across platforms and cultures. Key Words: Animation, Adaptation, Localisation, Comics, Semiotics, Emotional Resonance

candidates.title: Do We Really Need Multimodal Emotion Language Models Larger Than 1B Parameters?
candidates.abstract: Recent advances in multimodal large language models (MLLMs) have significantly improved the performance of multimodal emotion recognition (MER) and enabled interpretable description generation by jointly modeling video, audio, and language, etc. However, these performance improvements are often accompanied by an increase in model parameter size (e.g, at least 7B), which simultaneously incurs high computational costs and reduces inference efficiency, thereby hindering real-time deployment on resource-constrained platforms such as robots and mobile devices. This raises a fundamental question: do we really need the multimodal MER model larger than 1B parameters for high-quality MER? In this paper, we challenge the assumption that larger models are inherently necessary and proposes a lightweight MER framework (called Light-MER ), which achieves better and faster multimodal sentiment understanding and recognition through knowledge distillation. It can transfer knowledge from a strong, large-scale teacher model to a lightweight sub-billion-parameter student model, aiming to preserve rich multimodal emotion reasoning and recognition while substantially improving deployment efficiency. Specifically, we introduce two new optimization strategies to enhance knowledge transfer: (1) a new optimal transport loss that combines Sliced Wasserstein Distance with hidden-state alignment, and (2) a new multi-reward optimization strategy based on GRPO that balances MER performance and efficiency, aimed at further enhancing the learning capabilities of student models. Extensive experiments on nine benchmark datasets demonstrate that Light-MER achieves state-of-the-art performance while significantly improving inference efficiency. This highlights the strong potential of small multimodal emotion language models for future research. Code is available at https://github.com/GAIR-Lab/Light-MER.

candidates.title: The fake friend dilemma: relational trust and the political economy of conversational AI
candidates.abstract: As conversational AI systems become a larger part of the media landscape, they raise questions about whose interests they serve and the risks they may pose to users. These systems do more than provide information: they increasingly offer advice and companionship through interfaces that can appear supportive and socially responsive. A pressing concern is that users may form perceived social relationships with these systems and place relational trust in them, even when the interests shaping interactions do not fully align with their own. The Fake Friend Dilemma (FFD) describes the problem that follows: the same relational trust that makes conversational AI useful can also leave users open to manipulation and exploitation when institutional interests conflict with their own. Drawing on work on relational trust, AI alignment, extractive design, and the political economy of communication, the paper considers how the FFD can manifest through product sales, propaganda and biased information, surveillance, and behavioral nudging. It also considers possible structural and technical mitigation strategies. The FFD is not simply about AI misleading users. The problem it surfaces is that the trust people place in these systems can itself become a resource for institutional actors seeking to influence behavior or extract information. The FFD is therefore as much a problem of media governance and political economy as it is a technological one.

candidates.title: Exploring Emotional Attachment to Artificial Intelligence Companions: A Cross-Cultural Qualitative Study of Psychological Needs, Loneliness, and Human–AI Relationships in Pakistan and the United States
candidates.abstract: The rapid development of artificial intelligence (AI) companions has introduced new forms of human–technology interaction in which individuals increasingly experience emotional connection, psychological support, and companionship through digital systems. This study explores emotional attachment to AI companions by examining the psychological needs, loneliness experiences, and human–AI relationship patterns of users in Pakistan and the United States. Using a qualitative interpretive research design, semi-structured interviews were conducted with 20 AI companion users, including 10 participants from each cultural context. Data were analyzed through reflexive thematic analysis, resulting in five major themes: AI as an emotionally safe space, loneliness and unmet psychological needs, consistency and attachment formation, negotiation of authenticity, and dependency risks. Drawing upon Attachment Theory and Self-Determination Theory, the findings demonstrate that AI companions may provide meaningful emotional utility by fulfilling needs for connection, validation, and psychological comfort, while remaining distinct from human relationships. The study contributes an integrated AI Attachment–Need Fulfillment perspective and highlights the importance of responsible AI design, ethical guidelines, and balanced human–AI interaction.

candidates.title: How Does Perceived Empathy From AI Chatbots Shape Users' Privacy Attitudes, Behaviors, and Needs?
candidates.abstract: Prior research suggests that some dimensions of AI empathy may increase users' disclosure to chatbots, posing growing privacy risks as chatbots become more capable of empathic interaction. Yet this work often conceptualizes AI empathy narrowly, leaving users' own definitions and their broader privacy experiences unexplored. We interviewed 21 AI Chatbot users about what AI empathy meant to them and how it shaped their privacy attitudes, behaviors, and needs. Participants characterized empathy through five components--understanding, resonating, caring, expressing, and helping. Most participants viewed resonating and caring as essential components of human empathy but absent from AI empathy. Yet AI's contextual, in-depth understanding and helpfulness still encouraged highly sensitive disclosure. This highlights that AI empathy can endanger users' privacy without necessarily making AI seem human. Participants also desired varied forms and levels of empathy, each associated with distinct privacy needs. We offer actionable recommendations for designing privacy-enhancing mechanisms for empathic AI interactions.

candidates.title: From Algorithms to Empathy: Emotionally Intelligent AI Companions in Elder Mental Health Care - A scoping review
candidates.abstract: Background: The rising mental health crisis among older people, which is caused by loneliness, cognitive loss, and a lack of emotional support, needs new and caring solutions. This systematic literature review looks at how emotional intelligence (EI) can be added to AI- powered virtual companions and how they can help improve mental health outcomes in elder healthcare services. Objective: The study’s goal is to find out how emotionally intelligent technology can improve traditional eldercare by delivering consistent, caring, customized emotional support by looking at existing applications and conceptual frameworks. Methods: A peer-reviewed literature published between 2010 and 2025 in the Scopus, Web of Science, and PubMed databases. Studies that talked about emotional intelligence, virtual companions, mental health outcomes, or the design or implementation of eldercare services were included. A PRISMA-guided screening method chose 87 articles in all. The data was organized using the theme to identify common ideas and patterns in how virtual agents are used to help older people’s mental health. Results: The results show that there are five main themes: Emotional Responsiveness, Conceptual Frameworks, Psychological Outcomes, Usability and Acceptance, Ethical/System Integration, and Health System Integration. The results show that virtual companions with emotional intelligence may help older people feel less lonely, improve their mood, and make them more mentally strong. But the current collection of studies is not very complete; it has few real-world examples and no models that work across other cultures. Conclusion: This paper emphasizes the possibility of emotionally intelligent virtual companions as an aid in mental healthcare for the elderly. It underlines the critical demand for standardized conceptual frameworks, interdisciplinary research, and ethical principles to inform future breakthroughs and implementations. Emotionally intelligent AI technology could drastically transform aged care into a more responsive and person-centred service model in the digital era.

candidates.title: Do Virtual Faces Lead to Real Purchases? Investigating AI Anthropomorphism & Its Impact on Purchase Intention
candidates.abstract: The research paper focuses on the impact of AI anthropomorphism on purchase intention, with the mediating role of marketing personalization, entertainment value and perceived homophily in the context of AI influencers/models. Brands around the world are adopting AI marketing tools, in which AI influencers/models are a relatively newer domain. The aim of the research is to fill the gap of research done on AI influencers/models in the Pakistani consumer market, discussing its practical implications on the fashion industry in particular. The study involved a sample size of 220 respondents, Pakistani residents aged 16 to 45 years, who had either seen or interacted with AI influencers/models before in any media type, using convenience and snowball sampling technique for data collection, which was then run through SPSS using Process Hayes Mediation Model 4. The results of the mediation analysis represented that the three proposed hypotheses in the study were accepted. The hypotheses were; marketing personalization mediates the positive relationship between AI anthropomorphism and purchase Intention, entertainment value mediates the positive relationship between AI anthropomorphism and purchase intention, and lastly, entertainment value mediates the positive relationship between AI anthropomorphism and purchase intention. The proven hypotheses signify the importance of the practical implications of the research on the Pakistani fashion industry, as big global brands are moving towards and investing in newer technologies like AI marketing tools. Semantic-Enhanced Sparse Temporal Modeling for Dynamic Engagement Estimation in Multimodal Interactions
candidates.abstract: Dynamic engagement estimation aims to infer participants' evolving engagement states from continuous multimodal interaction streams. Existing approaches typically combine acoustic, pose, and visual representations with temporal models to capture observable interaction patterns. However, conversational semantics are difficult to align with frame-level engagement annotations in the same manner as continuous audio-visual signals, leaving dialogue context less effectively exploited in existing temporal modeling pipelines. Moreover, engagement annotations often evolve smoothly over time, making dense frame-level modeling computationally redundant and potentially sensitive to local annotation noise. To address these issues, we propose SEST, a Semantically-Enhanced Sparse Temporal framework that models engagement-related information from both semantic and temporal perspectives. SEST leverages Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) to extract multimodal semantic embeddings, providing dialogue-aware contextual information beyond conventional frame-level features. In parallel, SEST replaces dense-to-dense temporal modeling with a sparse-to-dense pathway, where continuous frame sequences are first encoded into compact temporal dynamics to reduce redundant computation and broaden temporal coverage, then fused with semantic context and recovered to the original label resolution for dense engagement prediction. Experiments on the MultiMediate'26 Multi-domain Engagement Estimation (MEE2026) benchmark demonstrate the effectiveness of SEST, which achieved first place in the challenge. Code is available at https://github.com/MSA-LMC/SEST.

candidates.title: Embodying the victim: Virtual embodiment equalizes gender responses to simulated domestic violence
candidates.abstract: Virtual embodiment (i.e. the first-person experience of inhabiting a virtual body) has been shown to modulate emotional and cognitive responses across diverse social contexts. In the domain of domestic violence, virtual reality (VR) offers a promising tool for fostering awareness of and sensitivity to aggressive behavior. Yet any VR-based intervention relying on shared experiential ground across genders must first establish cross-gender equivalence, regardless of whether VR is ultimately the optimal delivery platform. To address this requirement, we embodied 40 participants (20 male, 20 female) in a female avatar and exposed them to a VR domestic violence scenario featuring escalating verbal and physical aggression. We measured physiological responses (electrodermal activity, EDA), behavioral performance (Onset Time), and self-reported experiences (presence, embodiment, empathy), supplemented by post-experience verbal reports. Cross-gender equivalence was evaluated using a Two One-Sided Tests (TOST) procedure. Across physiological, behavioral, and subjective measures, male and female participants responded equivalently: EDA modulation was comparable across scenario phases, distress-threshold reaction times were statistically equivalent, and ratings of presence and embodiment did not differ meaningfully between groups. Of 33 binary verbal indicators, 30 (91%) fell within the equivalence margin. The three non-equivalent indicators were interpretive in nature: males more frequently reported guilt and submission, and tended to identify the onset of violence only upon physical aggression, whereas females recognized it during earlier verbal escalation. Within-gender EDA coupling further distinguished the groups – in males, physiological arousal co-varied with feelings of submission; in females, it co-varied with discomfort and perceived violation. These findings demonstrate that virtual embodiment substantially aligns male and female responses to simulated domestic violence, supporting its potential as a standardized tool for prevention and rehabilitation programs targeting gender-based violence.

candidates.title: Value dimensions shaping digital healthcare adoption: a conceptual review with implications for BRICS countries
candidates.abstract: Digital healthcare has revolutionized the way we see modern healthcare delivery bringing a massive shift from hospitals to home. However, recent literature points towards a scattered understanding of the concept. Thereby, this study analyses the literature around digital healthcare adoption to broaden the scope and their consumption value drivers. It explores the core consumption values through which digital healthcare gets augmented for their impact on preventive and promotive healthcare utilising bibliometric and content analysis methodologies with the theoretical base of the Theory of Consumption Values. The contribution of the study includes: classifying Digital healthcare research into paradigms, offering a conceptual framework, and exploring how consumption values may shape the user attitude, intention, and sustainable utilization of the futuristic wellness landscape. The framework brings together five value dimensions—functional, social, emotional, conditional, and epistemic—and organizes the reviewed literature into eight thematic categories. For BRICS health systems, the discussion considers affordability, infrastructure, clinical workflow integration, digital health literacy, and cultural adaptation. These implications are conceptual propositions rather than findings from a comparative cross-national study. The proposed relationships require empirical validation, particularly regarding sustained use and their applicability across healthcare settings. The findings hold implications for researchers, healthcare businesses, providers, and policymakers proposing possibilities for research exploration.

candidates.title: Trust, Risk, and Uncertainty Surrounding the Use of AI in Health Care: Scoping Review of Studies on Public Perception
candidates.abstract: Background: While AI has existed for decades, the introduction of generative AI tools and subsequent advancements in their capability and public use resulted in a shift in public awareness and perceptions of AI. In response, the research community has grown increasingly interested in understanding public perceptions of AI use in various contexts, including health care. Public perceptions shape AI acceptance and consequently integration into health care. It is thus crucial to understand public trust in AI and perceptions of risk as we consider its implementation moving forward. Objective: This study aimed to (1) document the extent of what is known within the literature regarding public perceptions of AI applications in health; (2) interrogate existing definitions and theories of trust being used to guide investigations of public trust in AI; and (3) identify practice and policy considerations and support the design, deployment, and regulation of these technologies in a manner that is trustworthy. Methods: The Arksey and O'Malley scoping review framework and the PRISMA-ScR (Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses extension for Scoping Reviews) guidelines were used to review publications between 2022 and 2024 across 4 databases, resulting in the inclusion of 41 papers for review. Key findings were then charted and organized into tables to help answer the proposed research questions. Results: Public trust in AI in health care was shaped by discourse relating to AI performance and concerns related to depersonalization, loss of human connection, privacy, bias, and transparency. Trust was found to be higher when AI was supporting rather than replacing health care professionals and was influenced by emotional responses, anthropomorphism, demographic factors, and institutional trust. Furthermore, trust extended beyond algorithms to software interfaces, providers, developers, and governing institutions, highlighting the importance of governance and oversight. Conceptualizations of trust varied widely, and trust was defined through vulnerability, competence, benevolence, and integrity. Different theories identified suggested that trust operates across individual, social, institutional, and technological levels. Finally, trust was closely linked to risk and uncertainty, where perceived risk reduced acceptance, while AI literacy, transparency, and explainability mitigated concerns and fostered trust. Conclusions: Trust in AI is not uniform, and as such, efforts to build and measure trust must account for these nuances to effectively mitigate risk and support informed, ethical AI integration and deployment. On the basis of the findings of this review, we propose a multilevel conceptual framework that provides a general understanding of public trust in AI within a health care context that may guide research and policy and practice considerations. Our findings highlight the importance of considering public trust when implementing AI in health care and may support AI communication strategies, policy development, and trustworthy AI development.

candidates.title: RL-Robotutor: a hierarchical reinforcement learning framework for multimodal robot tutoring
candidates.abstract: Personalised robot tutoring requires real-time pedagogical decision-making under uncertain and multimodal learner states. Existing intelligent tutoring and robot-assisted learning systems often rely on static rules, single-modality learner modelling, or short-term correctness-oriented optimisation, which limits their capacity to balance knowledge acquisition, engagement, retention, and safe embodied interaction. RL-Robotutor is presented as a hierarchical reinforcement learning framework that integrates cognitive knowledge-tracing signals, facial-expression and gaze-derived affective cues, and behavioural interaction logs through transformer-based fusion. A PPO-trained meta-policy selects among specialised modules for learner assessment, curriculum adaptation, strategy selection, and reflective feedback, while a hybrid reward combines immediate learning performance, engagement, long-term learning gain, and safety. The evidence is reported by source: five public knowledge-tracing datasets assess the cognitive prediction component; controlled simulator experiments assess policy learning, reward ablation, and multimodal fusion; and a randomised robot-tutoring study assesses embodied interaction with 120 undergraduate participants. RL-Robotutor outperforms rule-based, flat reinforcement-learning, knowledge-tracing, and LLM-based comparators. In the human study, the learning gain is 0.62, compared with 0.40 for the rule-based robot condition. The full hybrid reward improves simulator learning gain by 19% over correctness-only optimisation, and full multimodal fusion improves simulator engagement by 17% over text-only modelling. Jetson Orin deployment achieves 48 ms inference latency with an absolute AUC reduction of 0.007, supporting real-time edge execution.

candidates.title: Triboelectric E-Skin Patch Decoding Silent Speech for Advanced Human–Machine Interaction and Augmented Virtual Communication
candidates.abstract: Silent speech decoding (lip reading) represents an innovative hands-free communication method for individuals with laryngeal and lingual impairments, addressing critical daily communication challenges. Herein, a novel silent speech decoding system is proposed, which employs a self-powered, low-cost, and conformable triboelectric-based E‑skin patch and a well-trained multi-layer convolutional neural network (CNN) model. We systematically characterize the structural principles and electrical performance of the E-skin patch. A comparative analysis of labial kinematics during vocalized and silent speech is also conducted, which demonstrates strong consistency in time-frequency domain characteristics. The utilized CNN model is trained across 15 lexical categories (200 samples per category), achieving a high accuracy of 98.75% and demonstrating excellent recognition performance. Furthermore, by integrating human-machine interaction (HMI) and virtual reality (VR) technologies, we develop three representative applications, including a real-time lip language visualization system, an orofacial-controlled "Feeding Frenzy" interactive game, and a VR communication platform with avatar dialogue. This technology enables barrier-free communication for voiceless populations, demonstrating significant potential in HMI, augmentative communication systems, virtual reality integration, and biomedical rehabilitation.

candidates.title: Gaze semantics: A scoping review of how gaze conveys and constrains meaning in social contexts
candidates.abstract: Humans rely on gaze to encode information and signal to others. Gaze may indicate where someone is attending, but its contribution extends beyond spatial orientation. Evidence is scattered across different research traditions. This scoping review synthesizes 361 publications on gaze as a meaningful social cue. Gaze semantics describes the systematic contribution of gaze to conveying and constraining social meaning. A cross-domain synthesis identified four recurrent operations: gaze orients by making objects, people or locations socially relevant; addresses by positioning people as recipients or interaction partners; qualifies by modifying how other cues are interpreted; and coordinates by organizing participation and unfolding action. These functional contributions can co-occur within a single gaze event. Gaze interpretation is inferential, shaped by five categories of contextual factors: signal properties; interactional availability; multimodal and sequential embedding; cultural, social and activity frame; and gazer and observer states and interactional history. We propose a Gazer-Observer Model of Gaze Understanding that integrates these findings to describe the dynamic relation between gaze production and interpretation. The same gaze pattern may support different interpretations across situations yet allow a relatively specific interpretation within a particular encounter. Gaze can therefore systematically affect social interpretation while remaining semantically underdetermined to varying degrees.

candidates.title: Anthropomorphism and risk perception: The role of trust and domain knowledge in decision-support AI
candidates.abstract: Anthropomorphic design is increasingly used to make conversational AI systems more approachable and socially engaging, yet its effects on users’ risk judgments remain unclear. Drawing on theories of anthropomorphism and cognitive–affective trust, we develop a moderated mediation model explaining how perceived anthropomorphism relates to risk perception in AI decision support. We conducted a large-scale between-subjects online experiment (N = 1,256) using a simulated financial advisor chatbot with a 2 2 2 anthropomorphic design manipulation varying visual cues (human vs. machine avatar), identity cues (human name vs. bot identifier), and communication style (human-like vs. machine-like communication). Results show that perceived anthropomorphism was positively associated with both cognitive trust and affective trust, but these trust dimensions had different relationships with perceived risk. Cognitive trust consistently predicted lower risk perception, whereas affective trust showed a weaker positive association with risk perception that was not robust across model specifications. Self-reported domain knowledge moderated these relationships: higher domain knowledge attenuated the association between perceived anthropomorphism and both trust dimensions, while participants with lower domain knowledge showed a stronger negative indirect association between anthropomorphism and risk perception through cognitive trust. By treating the perceived risk of following AI advice as a focal outcome, this study extends anthropomorphism research beyond trust formation and distinguishes how cognitive and affective trust relate to users’ risk judgments. The findings highlight the importance of calibrating, rather than simply maximizing, anthropomorphic cues in high-stakes AI decision-support systems.

candidates.title: Evaluating human-like chatbot interaction in customer service: integrating anthropomorphism and conversational capability
candidates.abstract: The development of artificial intelligence (AI)-based technology has driven the development of rule-based chatbots into AI-based chatbots. This development is used by various companies to use AI chatbots as the frontline of customer service. Meeting user expectations for AI chatbots requires an evaluation model to measure chatbot quality. Based on the literature, chatbot evaluation models still focus solely on technical quality, even as AI chatbots are evolving towards human-like services. This research will explore the integration of the technical dimensions of information system success with a new dimension, namely Human-Like Chatbot Interaction (HLCI) as a higher-order construct of anthropomorphism and conversational capability. This quantitative study uses an explanatory research approach. Data were collected through a cross-sectional survey of users of the Veronika chatbot, owned by Telkomsel, an Indonesian telecommunications company. A total of 213 respondents had data ready for analysis using the Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) method in SmartPLS 4, namely the measurement model and structural model tests. The analysis results show that service quality is not significantly related to user satisfaction but has a direct effect on trust. Meanwhile, information quality, system quality, and human-like chatbot interaction are positively related to trust and user satisfaction. Trust and user satisfaction are positively related to intention to continue using. The results of this study can contribute both theoretically and practically to modern AI chatbot quality evaluation models.

candidates.title: The Economic Sustainability of Intangible Cultural Heritage in the Platform Age With Global Evidence and Implications for Xinjiang
candidates.abstract: ABSTRACT Digital platforms lower market access costs for intangible cultural heritage but can concentrate visibility, weaken community control, and disconnect revenue from cultural reproduction. This global survey integrates platform and cultural economics with research on authenticity, intellectual property, and heritage governance. Its Platform Frictions, Cultural Rents, and Intergenerational Reproduction framework distinguishes living practices from their commercial products, recordings, and experiences. Economic sustainability requires four minimum conditions that cannot substitute for one another. These comprise adequate net market access, viable cultural reproduction, a sufficient practitioner value share, and meaningful community control. The framework distinguishes these conditions from the mechanisms through which platforms affect them. Rankings, provenance labels, copyright, and certification can improve discovery and bargaining while concentrating demand, excluding legitimate variants, or burdening small producers. Community authorization requires representation, reviewable delegation, and effective appeal. Distributional assessment separates individual earnings, collective transfers, unpaid contributions, and investment in transmission. Applications to Xinjiang differentiate crafts, performances, foodways, and community events by economic object and institutional responsibility. Longitudinal indicators of apprentice retention, repertoire in use, and contextual participation distinguish authorized adaptation from commercial hollowing. Platform growth sustains living heritage when returns support practitioners, learning, and community authority.

candidates.title: Data-driven fandom culture: exploring parasocial interactions between digital fan labor and traffic stars using interaction ritual chains theory
candidates.abstract: Traffic stars and digital fan labor become a widespread phenomenon in China. Digital fan labor refers to the use of tools and data-driven social media strategies to interact with their favorite stars, organize events, measure popularity, and influence the popularity; such stars are referred to as traffic stars. While existing research has largely focused on the characteristics and motivations of digital fan labor in participating in fan activities, few studies have examined the factors influencing their interactive rituals with other fans and parasocial interactions with their celebrities. Parasocial interactions between traffic stars and digital fan labor refer to fans establishing emotional connections with celebrities through participation in fan activities, while celebrities, in turn, strengthen fan engagement through actions such as commenting and liking posts. At this point, Interaction Ritual Chains Theory provides a theoretical framework for the assessment of the importance of collective effervescence and the shared emotional intensity experienced during group rituals in virtual spaces. Therefore, this study uses factors drawn from interaction ritual chains theory to explore the parasocial interaction between so-called ‘traffic stars’ and the digital fan labor they attract within data-driven fandom communities. The sampling strategy was using snowball sampling of a purposive group, and 329 Chinese fans aged between 18 and 42 years old were selected. SPSS version 26.0 was used to obtain descriptive statistics, t-test, mediation effects and moderation effects, and AMOS version 24.0 was used to investigate the result of correlation analysis. The resulting indicated that virtual experience, sense of community, mutual focus of attention, and shared mood all are all associated to the interactive ritual of digital fan labor. This study also found that interactive ritual outcomes play a mediating role between interactive ritual elements and parasocial interactions, especially having different mediating effects with subgroups. However, personal norms did not have a moderating role regarding ritual ingredients affecting interactive ritual outcomes and parasocial interaction. Consequently, this study identified a noteworthy phenomenon: the parasocial interaction between traffic stars and digital fan labor involving a higher level of interactive rituals arises from a hybrid pattern of online actions that develops in a particular environment.

candidates.title: A multimodal approach to identify atypical face processing in first episode psychosis (early schizophrenia spectrum disorders)
candidates.abstract: Background While social interaction difficulties are common in schizophrenia, the neural underpinnings for its social symptomatology are under-explored. In this study, we aimed to isolate atypical neural systems associated with live social interaction in first episode psychosis (early schizophrenia spectrum disorder). Methods A two-person live face gaze paradigm was employed as the behavioral proxy for social interaction while electroencephalography (EEG), functional near infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS), eye tracking, and facial movement measures were simultaneously acquired. Findings were compared for 24 first episode psychosis (FEP) patients and 32 typically developed (TD) participants to test the hypothesis that these neural and behavioral measures would isolate atypical social neural systems in the FEP group. Results FNIRS neural data showed atypical hemodynamic activity in the right temporoparietal region, known to be associated with live face-to-face interactions. This atypical activity was significantly correlated with expressive deficit score, a sub score derived from PANSS negative symptom domain and N4, a PANSS negative symptom which measures passive/apathetic social withdrawal. Involuntary behavioral responses associated with spontaneous facial mimicry and gaze fixation were reduced in FEP. Consistent with previous findings, Event Related Potential (ERP) amplitudes and latencies were atypical in FEP during the first 100–300 ms in the right temporoparietal electrodes, along with reduced theta oscillation power. Conclusion Together, the identified regions represent atypical live face processing systems in early schizophrenia spectrum disorder, which is further correlated with expressive deficits and social withdrawal. The study emphasizes the need for ecologically valid multimodal data acquisition to detect neural hubs crucial in live face processing in early schizophrenia.

candidates.title: From Emotional Impulse to Recurring Revenue: Consumer Psychology, Unit Economics, and VC Investment Evaluation of AI Companion Hardware for Gen Z
candidates.abstract: With the rapid convergence of Large Language Models (LLMs) and embodied intelligence, AI companion hardware targeted at Generation Z (e.g., desktop AI pets and smart emotional robots) has emerged as a premier track for venture capital (VC) investment. However, these conceptual devices frequently face severe Unit Economics crises characterized by high customer acquisition costs (CAC), elevated initial product returns, and steep user churn rates. This paper examines the psychological drivers behind Gen Z's willingness to pay (WTP) high emotional premiums for feature-incomplete AI hardware, and investigates how hardware enterprises can leverage proactive retention mechanisms to optimize LTV/CAC ratios and valuation multiples . This paper conducts a literature review that synthesizes theoretical frameworks from behavioral finance, consumer psychology, human-computer interaction (HCI), and venture capital valuation models. The study reveals that Gen Z's demand for loneliness compensation and social status validation provides firms with strong initial pricing power and gross margins. However, sustaining long-term commercial viability requires overcoming the "novelty decay trap" through proactive AgentOS interactions and dynamic memory graphs. Transforming hardware from a one-off transaction into an Annual Recurring Revenue (ARR) subscription model substantially improves capital efficiency, expanding valuation multiples from 1.0x–2.0x P/S to 8.0x–12.0x P/S.

candidates.title: Voice-Native LLMs Hear Frustration but Do Not Listen to It
candidates.abstract: Users convey frustration in what they say and in how they say it, and voice-native models, which hear speech instead of an ASR transcript, can register both. Existing evaluations read unchanged performance as robustness without checking perception. Following Brunswik's lens model, we measure on identical audio whether frustration is expressed, perceived, and utilized. We cross frustrated wording with frustrated voice in a within-item 2x2 design over 353 tasks and release the 1,412 clips as VoxAffect. Across 8 models, outputs look robust, with no detectable vocal effect on accuracy for 7. With neutral wording, all 8 label the frustrated voice frustrated in at most 3.1% of clips, although 7 of them detect acted anger in 73-100% of clips and human listeners classify the voice correctly in 65.3% of judgments. Yet linear probes decode the frustrated voice from the audio encoders of the 2 open-weight models, with paired accuracy 0.67 and 0.69, and in proprietary models too the voice raises perceived frustration once the words agree. The models thus hear the frustrated voice but do not listen to it, whereas their invariance to frustrated wording, perceived in 40-75% of clips, is genuine robustness. Our work is openly accessible at https://github.com/Astarojth/hear-not-listen.

candidates.title: BRIDGING AUTOMATION AND ROBOTICS IN INDUSTRIALIZED BUILDING SYSTEM (IBS): CHALLENGES, IMPACTS, AND STRATEGIES OF ADOPTIONS
candidates.abstract: The Industrialised Building System (IBS) was introduced in Malaysia in the early 1960s to address the growing demand for affordable housing, reduce reliance on foreign labour, and enhance the overall quality and productivity of the construction sector. Recently, the construction industry has begun integrating automation and robotics, aligning with the global shift towards the Fourth Industrial Revolution (IR 4.0). The Construction 4.0 Strategic Plan (2021–2025) further emphasises digitalisation, robotics, and automation to improve industry efficiency and sustainability. However, the construction industry has been slow to adopt these advancements, limiting the full benefits of automation in IBS. Persistent challenges, including resistance to change, high initial investment costs, a shortage of skilled personnel, and technical complexities, hinder widespread adoption. This research examines the integration of automation and robotics in IBS to enhance construction productivity. A questionnaire survey was used for the data collection exercise. The data collected were analysed using descriptive statistical methods utilising the Statistical Package for the Social Sciences (SPSS) software. The study is guided by three (3) objectives: (1) To identify barriers to the integration of automation and robotics in IBS, (2) To analyse the impact of automation and robotics on construction productivity compared to conventional IBS, and (3)To propose strategies to improve the adoption of these technologies.Findings reveal that the integration of automation and robotics in (IBS) facessignificant barriers, primarily due to the high costs of investment. candidates.title: MESSPa: A Multi-modal Embodiment Stimulation Shoulder Pad for Preserving the Sense of Agency in a Detachable Robotic Arm
candidates.abstract: Wearable robots such as supernumerary robotic limbs (SRLs) can augment human capability, but their effectiveness depends strongly on the operator's sense of embodiment, comprising the sense of agency (SoA) and the sense of ownership (SoO). When an SRL is detached from the body so that the operator can act in two places at once, both the sense of agency and task performance tend to degrade. This paper presents the Multi-modal Embodiment Stimulation Shoulder Pad (MESSPa), a wearable interface that combines one-to-one motion transfer with spatially distributed pneumatic (balloon) haptic feedback on the shoulder, with the goal of preserving the sense of agency across attached and detached states. We describe the system design, the control mapping, and a controlled experiment using a $2\times2$ mixed design that crosses the control interface between groups (MESSPa, $N=13$, vs. keyboard control, $N=12$ from our previous study) and attachment (on-shoulder/detached) within participants, under single- and dual-task loads. Compared with keyboard control in the detached condition, MESSPa significantly reduced task completion time and significantly improved the sense of agency in the detached state, while narrowing the performance gap between the attached and detached conditions. The sense of ownership did not change significantly. These results indicate that combining motion transfer with positional haptic feedback is an effective way to recover agency when a robotic limb is operated remotely.

candidates.title: Create, Innovate, Play and Explore: Opportunities for Formal and Informal Teaching and Learning in Makerspaces in Ireland
candidates.abstract: The Maker Movement has gained in popularity over the last decade, allowing people of all ages and with varying skills and abilities to come together in order to create and explore in areas such as art, science, and engineering. To facilitate this movement, for profit companies, non-profits, and educational institutions run makerspaces. This qualitative study set out to examine the benefits of makerspace adoption in higher education in Ireland, with particular attention to their pedagogical value. The authors sought to identify opportunities for teaching and learning and the development of rich, diverse, and inclusive educational environments, as well as the potential to develop a maker network linking tertiary makerspaces with the wider community. Nine administrators from diverse types of makerspaces participated in interviews where they described the impacts and observed effects of makerspaces on participant learning experiences. Findings indicate that makerspaces support self-directed and peer learning, foster inclusive learning communities characterised by skill-sharing and mentorship, and provide safe environments for experimentation and productive failure. In doing so, makerspaces support learning dispositions such as agency, resilience, and self-efficacy, which are increasingly recognised as critical to student learning, persistence, and adaptability in contemporary higher education. Participants also perceived positive impacts on mental health, an area that remains under-researched in tertiary makerspaces. Finally, interviewees advocated for the development of a maker network in Ireland, suggesting that such a network could facilitate the sharing of skills and resources and strengthen access to larger-scale funding.

candidates.title: THINKING OF OTHERNESS IN THE ERA OF AI. FOR A PEDAGOGY OF EMOTIONAL INTELLIGENCE IN FORMAL CONTEXTS
candidates.abstract: The paper investigates whether and to what extent AI-based devices can support or simulate certain aspects of the educational relationship, with particular reference to the emotional education of children and adolescents. Starting from the contemporary crisis of human connections, the weakening of emotional awareness, and the growing exposure of younger generations to intelligent digital environments, the contribution reflects on the relationship between emotional intelligence, empathy, and education.Situated within both classical and contemporary pedagogical frameworks, the paper critically examines both the risks of artificialization and the colonization of human experience, as well as the potential educational resources offered by the digital environment. It underscores the necessity of transcending any technophobia, in order to critically question whether and how intelligent machines can engage in formal educational contexts with practices of recognizing others, self-regulation, compassion, and the design of an authentically human existence.

candidates.title: R-Metaverse: multimodal social cues for real-world-centered telepresence–MR collaboration with telepresence robots
candidates.abstract: Remote collaboration in live physical workspaces requires direct access to the evolving scene and shared task information anchored to it. Telepresence provides embodied access but lacks a shared spatial interaction layer, whereas fully virtual collaboration requires reconstructing the workspace. R-Metaverse (Ritsumei Real-World Robotic Metaverse) is a telepresence–MR system design centered on the physical workspace. A remote participant operates a telepresence robot and views its camera image augmented with virtual objects through a head-mounted display (HMD), while an on-site participant views the same spatially registered virtual objects through a smartphone. The robot–mobile configuration creates viewpoint and embodiment asymmetries that can reduce social presence. Robot–robot collaboration makes partner distance and approach difficult to perceive because of robot-camera field-of-view limitations. To restore missing cues, we implement facial-expression display, motion-synchronized avatar overlay, spatially localized audio, and distance-linked vibrotactile feedback. The first three target robot–mobile collaboration; the fourth targets robot–robot collaboration. Ablation experiments show that facial-expression display improves affect understanding and closeness, while distance-linked vibrotactile feedback supports co-presence and spatial awareness under field-of-view constraints. Avatar, audio, and vibration-pattern effects are interpreted as exploratory after Holm correction. These results suggest that gap-specific multimodal cues can partially compensate for reduced social presence in real-world-centered telepresence–MR collaboration.

candidates.title: Artificial Intelligence Anthropomorphism and Emotional Affiliation Needs among Young Adults
candidates.abstract: The increasing integration of artificial intelligence (AI) into interpersonal communication has transformed the dynamics of emotional relationships between humans and digital technologies. This study examines the relationship between AI anthropomorphism and emotional affiliation needs among young adults, focusing on perceived social presence, emotional attachment, and AI-mediated companionship. Employing a qualitative library research approach, the study thematically synthesizes 35 scholarly publications published between 2018 and 2026. The findings suggest that humanlike communication, personalized responses, and perceived emotional responsiveness may strengthen social presence and facilitate emotional attachment. Such interactions may provide perceived emotional support, particularly for individuals experiencing loneliness or unmet affiliation needs. However, intensive emotional engagement may also contribute to dependence, unrealistic relational expectations, and psychological vulnerability following the disruption of AI companionship. This study develops a conceptual synthesis integrating anthropomorphism, social presence, emotional attachment, and affiliation needs to explain the dynamics of human–AI emotional relationships. Further empirical investigation is needed to validate this framework among young adults.

candidates.title: LabMaker: Conectando educação, inovação e impacto social por meio da cultura Maker
candidates.abstract: Maker culture has been established as a strategy to promote active learning, innovation, and social impact, contributing to the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), especially SDGs 4, 10, and 12. In this context, this paper presents a set of actions developed by the extension project Labmaker, a multidisciplinary laboratory that integrates education, accessibility, healthcare, and sustainability through Maker culture, additive manufacturing, and Web technologies and platforms. The actions presented include training activities in robotics, programming, and 3D modeling, the development of assistive technologies and solutions for the healthcare sector, the promotion of circular economy initiatives focused on 3D printing, and the use of digital media and Web platforms to expand the project’s reach and interaction with the community. The results of these actions demonstrate the project’s potential to democratize access to technologies, strengthen the relationship between the university and society, promote hands-on learning, and contribute to the development of innovative solutions aligned with the SDGs.

candidates.title: Baby-schema-related cues shape moral expectations about decision-makers: evidence from names, faces, and AI avatars
candidates.abstract: People routinely form expectations about how others will behave in morally difficult situations, and such expectations guide consequential decisions, including whom to trust, hire, or delegate responsibility to. The present research examined whether baby-schema-related cues systematically bias these moral predictions. Across three experiments with Chinese university students (total N = 858), we tested three manifestations of baby-schema-related cues that share the function of evoking infant-like associations: repeated two-syllable names (Experiment 1), babyfaced appearance (Experiment 2), and visually cute artificial intelligence (AI) avatar designs (Experiment 3). Participants consistently perceived decision-makers displaying baby-schema-related cues as less likely to make utilitarian choices involving direct harm to others. The results show that superficially irrelevant social cues can bias moral expectations about others, although the underlying psychological mechanism remains to be clarified. These findings are relevant to moral psychology, person perception, and the design and evaluation of AI systems.

candidates.title: AI vs. AI: An AI-Enabled Conversational Intervention to Inoculate Against AI-Generated Fake News
candidates.abstract: Abstract Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is a double-edged sword that can be used to amplify the proliferation of highly sophisticated fake news as well as to fight it. In this work, we explore a new route: using one AI to inoculate humans against fake news generated by another AI. Motivated by psychological inoculation theory, we created ‘Alex’, a conversational AI agent that engages users in an adaptive conversational dialogue designed to build cognitive resilience against AI-generated, AI-related fake news. We tested its efficacy in a Solomon four-group experiment with 542 participants. The results of a 2 × 2 ANOVA show a significant main effect of the intervention on participants’ discrimination of true and false headlines, with no significant evidence of pretest sensitization. We show that AI can be designed as a scalable, interactive conversational intervention for delivering psychological inoculation against AI-generated, AI-related fake news.

candidates.title: Virtual idol consumption among Generation Z: exploring fandom motivations, engagement behavior, and marketing implications
candidates.abstract: Virtual idols have rapidly gained worldwide popularity among young people and have become a significant marketing tool for promoting brands and expanding market reach. Grounded in Self-Determination Theory (SDT), this study conducted in-depth interviews to explore motivations, engagement behavior, and consumption patterns underlying Generation Z’s virtual idol fandom. The findings reveal that virtual idol fandom is shaped by both intrinsic and attribute-driven motivations. Within the fandom, engagement with and consumption of virtual idols are driven by overlapping motivational pathways combining emotional involvement, relational control, technology fascination, and community participation. Where community participation is involved, virtual idol fandom extends beyond individual engagement into a socio-technical ecosystem shaped by user agency, platform affordances, and regulatory oversight. At the same time, virtual idol fans seek emotional involvement while pursuing a ‘secure distance’ that preserves psychological boundaries and relational control. This study develops an SDT-informed interpretive framework that reconfigures diverse motivations within contemporary virtual idol fandom. By mapping distinct fan-as-consumer profiles, this study offers practical implications for the scalability of digital persona-led industries and insights for brands seeking to leverage the visibility and influence of virtual idols for targeted promotion among young consumers, enhanced brand value creation, and sustainable expansion in global markets.

candidates.title: A Survey on AI-Based Household Robots Focusing on Voice Assistance, Smart Kitchen Support, Home Monitoring and Autonomous Navigation
candidates.abstract: The proposed system places a Raspberry Pi at the centre, connected to a microphone, speaker, display, camera, ultrasonic sensors, a motor driver and a wheeled base. A conversational AI layer interprets natural-language requests, while obstacle detection, emergency stop and motor time-outs are kept in local safety logic outside the AI loop. Design considerations, a proposed function-to-module mapping, safety logic and an evaluation plan are presented.

candidates.title: A Two Timescale Probabilistic State-Space Framework for Multimodal Affect Estimation and Uncertainty Aware Expressive Behavior in Humanoid Robots: A Monte Carlo Simulation Study
candidates.abstract: Abstract Humanoid robots intended for care, education and collaboration are expected to perceive human affect and respond appropriately, yet published systems often map momentary classifier outputs directly to robot expressions, discarding uncertainty, temporal structure and the asymmetric informativeness of sensing channels. This paper formulates affect transfer from human to robot as a Bayesian state-estimation and constrained-control problem. A six-dimensional latent state couples fast emotion and slow mood in pleasure–arousal–dominance (PAD) space; physiological, facial and vocal channels enter through modality-specific linear-Gaussian observation models; a sequential Kalman filter with a chi-square innovation gate fuses them under intermittent dropout and outliers; and an uncertainty-weighted, rate-limited mapping converts the posterior into robot display commands. The framework is evaluated entirely in synthetic Monte Carlo simulation (200 trials, 120 s each) under explicitly stated assumptions; no human-subject data are used. Under nominal conditions the gated fused filter reached an overall PAD RMSE of 0.151, against 0.257 for smoothed late fusion and 0.243 for a face-only filter. A 2 factorial study (R2 = 0.862) showed that gating helps only when outliers are present and slightly harms accuracy otherwise. Confidence scaling with λ = 2 cut display jitter by 81% and wrong-sign valence displays by 42% at a 32% tracking-error cost. The contribution is a reproducible, falsifiable baseline that must next be tested on recorded human data.

candidates.title: Attentional territories: The influence of gaze and interpersonal distance in the navigation of public space
candidates.abstract: Human gaze is a potent social signal; it communicates attention, intention and social engagement, and allows observers to infer not only where others are attending but also how they are socially related. Although gaze has been extensively studied in direct social interaction, far less is known about how it shapes the perceptions and actions of uninvolved observers in shared environments. Here, we investigate whether mutual gaze creates an 'attentional territory' that third parties implicitly respect. In a large-scale field study across four university campuses in Europe and Canada (N = 4680 pedestrians), two confederates stood facing one another in a public space. We manipulated gaze direction and reciprocity (mutual, unilateral or no interaction) as well as interpersonal distance (2-6 metres), holding body orientation and spatial arrangement constant. Pedestrians were less likely to cross between individuals engaged in mutual gaze. This effect weakened with increasing distance, but was robust across all locations. Together, the findings demonstrate that gaze does not merely coordinate interaction between individuals but also shapes how uninvolved others perceive and move through shared environments. By isolating gaze reciprocity from spatial arrangement, we demonstrate that mutual gaze functions as a dynamic social boundary organizing the permeability of public space.

candidates.title: What craft-makers know, and what they need: mapping skills and learning preferences across European craft-ecosystems
candidates.abstract: This article investigates which skills contemporary craft-makers consider most relevant, which they prefer to develop or outsource, and how these preferences reflect different educational contexts. We conducted fieldwork in four European craft ecosystems (Bassano del Grappa, Venice, Dals Långed, Bornholm) through interviews, an online questionnaire, and three co-creation workshops. We develop a framework comprising five skill areas: craft-making and technical, technological, business, communication and selling, and transversal skills. Our findings reveal how craft-making is shaped by a complex interplay between the primacy of craft-making skills, the uneasy yet unavoidable role of managerial and communication skills, and persistent tensions around technology and sustainability. Craft-makers generally prefer to develop making and transversal skills while outsourcing business and administrative activities. Learning is also constrained by limited time, and economic precarity, while national educational systems shape distinct career pathways and skill needs, requiring context-sensitive policy support.

candidates.title: Bespoke Visual Assistance: What and How do Blind and Low-Vision People Create with Agentic Programming?
candidates.abstract: AI-powered assistive technologies have long supported blind and low vision (BLV) people in everyday tasks, but they are general-purpose and often fall short of meeting complex, individualized, in-situ accessibility needs. Though agentic programming tools, like GitHub Copilot, have the potential to bridge this gap by lowering the technical barriers to building personal AT using natural language, the practical applicability of this creation paradigm has been unknown. We address this knowledge gap through a two-phase longitudinal co-design study with five tech-savvy BLV users using ProgramAT, an agentic programming tool that supports the creation, iteration, and testing of camera-based AT. Overall, co-designers created over 37 tools, with some addressing needs unmet by any existing commercial AT—such as identifying Uber rides or interpreting hand gestures. Qualitative feedback from our co-designers and analysis of development logs surface BLV strategies for tool creation, along with key challenges including model capability limits, specification conflicts, and barriers to successful creation. We discuss recommendations to provide appropriate conversational scaffolding, community tool sharing capabilities, and support for specialized models and personal datasets for future agentic programming environments to empower BLV users to create bespoke visual assistance for themselves.

candidates.title: BabAR: from phoneme recognition to developmental measures of young children's speech production
The social self: integration of multimodal communication signals in dyadic interactions
candidates.abstract: Humans are in continuous exchange with other persons, thereby integrating the individual self and the social self. This requires the production of different verbal and nonverbal signals at the subpersonal level (individual self) and, at the same time, their coordination with various perceived signals at the interpersonal level (social self). Many of our communicative signals are conveyed substantially nonverbally-that is automatically, intuitively and effortlessly, requiring dynamic coordination over time ('chronemics'). Whereas successful communication is usually perceived as pleasant and satisfying, communication can also be experienced as disrupted if chronemics do not unfold properly. With respect to the particularly informative example of autism spectrum disorder, we propose the concept of 'double invisibility'. Non-autistic persons intuitively produce and expect a rich, multimodal stream of communication signals without being aware of it (first invisibility). By contrast, autistic persons produce and expect nonverbal cues either to a significantly lesser extent or not at all without being aware of it (second invisibility). This mismatch leads to misunderstandings and disturbed communication. The coordination within the dyad that is continuously constructed through real-time communication is crucial to understand the full complexity of multimodal interactions and their disturbances. This article is part of the discussion meeting issue 'From being to identity: analysis and synthesis of the self'.
