candidates.title: Multimodal human-intent modeling for contextual robot-to-human handovers of arbitrary objects
Beyond One-Size-Fits-All: Personalized and Culturally Adaptive Emotional TTS via Interactive Optimization of Individual Emotion Perception Spaces
Editorial: Rethinking technology adoption in the age of agentic artificial intelligence
Enabling Robot Learning Through Capable Hardware: Preliminary Studies In Multimodal Tactile Sensing, Bimanual Mobile Manipulation, And Semantic Demonstration Synthesis
candidates.abstract: Physical AI is continuing to advance rapidly, but its current capabilities are limited by the underlying hardware and perception stack. Robot learning, in particular, is often bottlenecked by current sensing capabilities, which limit the amount of information available to the learning algorithm and the range of tasks that can be attempted. Most robotics operations are contact-rich, meaning it requires robotic systems to have robust tactile sensing and whole-body perception to understand the state of the world during grasping and object manipulation. In this thesis, I present how there is a need to develop more capable hardware and perception capabilities to enable robot learning in robotic dexterous manipulation and mobile manipulation. To show this, I discuss how DenseTact sensors can be improved to provide more reliable tactile sensing in robotic end effectors, how we can utilize the TidyBot++ mobile manipulator platform to enable bimanual mobile manipulation research and education, and how we can use a single RGB video of a human performing a manipulation task to generate a large set of robot demonstrations for downstream policy learning. DenseTact is an optical tactile sensor that provides high-resolution tactile sensing for robotic manipulation. It’s current capabilities include shape and force sensing. Currently, it has reliability limitations in terms of its manufacturing process, calibration pipeline, and overall hardware design. Additionally, it lacks the ability to sense vibration and temperature, which are important for many manipulation tasks. As a result, I am presenting the current progress to move DenseTact to be more antrhropomorphic, reliable in manufacturing and calibration, and to have multimodal sensing capabilities. The strategy for this is to introduce a new version of the DenseTact Mini sensor, an automated calibration pipeline that builds on TensorTouch, and prototyping hardware and software for localized vibration and distributed temperature sensing modalities co-localized with the existing shape and force channels. MR. CRABS is a holonomic bimanual mobile manipulator that is built on the open-source TidyBot++ base. It includes two Realsense D435 depth cameras, one of which has an active pan-and-tilt mechanism for near-ground perception. It also includes a top LIDAR for long-range perception. It also utilizes two Trossen Robotics Widow-X arms. MR. CRABS is designed both as a research platform for bimanual mobile manipulation and as the next-generation educational platform for Stanford’s ME 326, replacing the LoCoBots used previously. The more capable hardware proved to be essential to allow students to complete the course’s final project, allowing them to better navigate the scene and perform more complex manipulation tasks that cannot be done with the LoCoBots. I present that more teams were able to complete more of the final project, and the projects were more complex than in previous years. Finally, I present Semantics as a Present (SAP), a demonstration-augmentation pipeline that turns a single RGB video of a human performing a manipulation task into an N ×M set of robot demonstrations spanning a family of pre-scanned cousin objects, with no depth sensor, no teleoperation, and no per-object annotation. The method recovers per-frame SE(3) object pose from RGB alone via distilled-DINO and depth-ranking losses, grafts the recovered motion onto each cousin via regionweighted semantic 3D Gaussian splat alignment, and replays the grafted trajectories in IsaacLab to mint demonstrations for any downstream policy (diffusion policy, ACT, π0). SAP shares its vision front end with the first two contributions, illustrating the thesis’s central claim: that perception-grounded, capable hardware is what enables modern robot learning to translate from benchmarks to real, contact-rich, bimanual, semantically rich tasks. It is compared with human demonstrations collected with an Realsense camera and teleoperation, then trained on a VLA benchmark and evaluated on a real robot to show that it can achieve comparable performance to the human demonstrations. We evaluate SAP on seven different tasks.

candidates.title: Love to Fandom: Ethical Condition for Cosplayers Subjectivity
candidates.abstract: Abstract Cosplay is a fan production that allows its participants to express their subjective values through dressing up as characters from media products. Such phenomenon exemplifies the intricate dynamics of consumer relations since cosplay explores multiple aspects of consumer culture theory. Thus, drawing from fan studies and Foucauldian frameworks, the aim of the research is analyzing how cosplayer subjectivity is constituted. In this sense, the study performs an Ethnographic Foucauldian Genealogy, based on a corpora constituted of autoethnography, netnography, online ethnographic interviews and virtual ethnomethodology data. The results evidenced two subject-forms: Nailers, representing the position taken by cosplayers who take on the role of exemplary representing the cosplay phenomenon; and Guardians, highlighting how some cosplayers feel responsible for maintaining a community of practitioners that allows those interested in cosplay to feel comfortable. Both subjectivities share an ethic named as Love to fandom. Such ethic guide cosplayers to produce truths about the ways in which they interact or show solidarity between peers based on their own condition as fans, legitimizing autonomous and complementary subjectivities, and enhancing and ensuring experiences with cosplay practice. Thus, the study expands the possibilities of living love through consumption – here, inherent to fans. It is a love established and maintained by the consumers themselves both through the intense relationship with the products consumed and through interactions with their peers.
authors: André Luiz Maranhão de Souza Leão

candidates.title: Big Data and Predictive Analytics Capability and Triple Bottom Line Sustainability Performance: A Resource‐Based Perspective From BRICS Nations
candidates.abstract: ABSTRACT This study aims to investigate the relationship between big data and predictive analytics (BDPA) capability and triple bottom line (TBL) sustainability performance in BRICS manufacturing firms. Grounded in the resource‐based view (RBV), we conceptualise BDPA capability as a third‐order hierarchical construct comprising tangible resources (data infrastructure and technology), intangible resources (organisational culture, organisational learning and data‐driven culture) and human‐related skills (technical skills and management skills). Survey data have been used from 304 IT and analytics professionals representing different organisations across BRICS economies and partial least squares structural equation modelling (PLS‐SEM) with 5000 bootstrap samples; we test six hypotheses examining both the resource‐capability link and the capability‐performance link. Results reveal that all three resource categories significantly contribute to BDPA capability, with human‐related skills exerting the strongest influence. BDPA capability, in turn, significantly predicts environmental performance, social performance and economic performance, explaining 40%, 50% and 55% of variance, respectively. The study contributes to the literature by providing an empirically validated, multi‐level resource‐capability‐performance framework for analytics‐driven sustainability in emerging economies.

candidates.title: Dexterous Robotic Hands in the Foundation-Model Era: A Full-Stack Survey of Hardware, Data, Cross-Embodiment Transfer, Learning, and Evaluation
candidates.abstract: Dexterous robotic hands are increasingly coupled to large-scale human data and foundation models, yet progress in hardware, representation learning and evaluation is often assessed separately. This survey reviews work from January 2024 to early November 2026, with earlier studies included to establish technical lineages. We organize the literature into five interdependent layers: hardware; data collection and curation; cross-embodiment transfer; learning and foundation models; and evaluation and applications. Human hand-object understanding and tactile sensing provide two cross-cutting perspectives. A system-level architecture, comparative tables and five case analyses connect design choices across these layers. We distinguish within-study experimental comparisons from heterogeneous corpus statistics, vendor specifications and company-reported results. Three conclusions emerge. First, the value of human data depends on kinematic, visual and contact alignment, not recording volume alone. Second, shared action representations and foundation policies do not remove embodiment-specific constraints on force, latency and contact. Third, task completion is insufficient to establish physical correctness or deployment readiness. Evidence remains limited for zero-shot transfer of contact-rich skills between morphologically different hands, long-duration reliability, and cross-sensor tactile generalization. We identify eleven open problems and propose reporting interfaces and controlled comparisons that can make full-stack progress more measurable. The review is a structured narrative synthesis rather than a pooled performance ranking or an exhaustive systematic review.

candidates.title: Fans for life? Popular culture-inspired tattoos and the challenges of inscribed expressions of fandom
candidates.abstract: This article examines active practices of fandom and identity communication through the collection of fandom-based tattoos. Through an analysis of fan theory, the article argues that fans who express their devotion to media culture through tattooing engage in a distinctive act of active fandom that represents a bodily extension of Rojek’s concept of the fan reliquary, a religiously inspired repository of collected items and artefacts by which fans signify their fandom to inspiration figures (such as Taylor Swift). The article considers the critical issues relating to fans that have used their bodies as tattooed reliquaries, but for whom the designs have become problematic in the wake of negative social actions and cultural reactions towards the objects of the fandom, such as J.K. Rowling. Tattoos, therefore, signify a potent expression of fan identification, but their permanence makes them a risk in an unpredictable landscape of popular and media culture.

candidates.title: Personality expression and perception in large language models and humans
candidates.abstract: Abstract Growing numbers of people frequently turn to Large Language Models (LLMs) for concerns from various areas of life. Because its content has become ubiquitous, examining user perceptions of LLM-produced text and its distinguishability from human writing is crucial. This study investigated how seven LLMs (ChatGPT-4o, ChatGPT-3.5, Llama 3, Gemma, Gemini, Phi-3, Orca-2) describe themselves when compared to humans. LLM-generated outputs and human responses were collected using psychological questionnaires (Big Five, self-esteem, narcissism) and tailored prompts to elicit short self-descriptive texts. Six LLM and ten human judges then evaluated personality traits and text origin based on these self-descriptions (140 total, half LLM-generated). Results show that current LLM outputs can convey personality-consistent cues in questionnaires and texts. The perception of such significantly differed from that of humans. Both LLM and human judges accurately inferred personality from short self-descriptions and correctly differentiated between LLM-generated and human text. Linguistic analysis and participant feedback revealed textual cues distinguishing LLM-produced from human language and offered insights into how LLM versus human judgment and decisionmaking differ.

candidates.title: Role of AI adoption, AgriTech, and climate variability on agricultural export performance of Pakistan
candidates.abstract: Achieving Pakistan’s $100 billion export target requires a fundamental transformation of its agricultural sector, which remains constrained by low productivity, limited technological diffusion, and weak integration into global value chains. This study examines the long and short run relations of artificial intelligence adoption and AgriTech infrastructure with agricultural export performance in Pakistan and assesses how climate variability shapes these relationships. Using annual time-series data from 2003 to 2024, the study develops an integrated analytical framework linking AI adoption, AgriTech infrastructure, climate variability, innovation capacity, global demand, exchange rate volatility, and institutional quality to agricultural export performance. The empirical analysis employs the Autoregressive Distributed Lag bounds-testing approach to distinguish long-run relationships from short-run dynamics, with Fully Modified Ordinary Least Squares and Dynamic Ordinary Least Squares) used as robustness checks. The results show that AI adoption, AgriTech infrastructure, and climate variability are the three central technology–environment correlates of agricultural exports: a one-unit increase in the AI Adoption Index is associated with roughly 20% higher agricultural exports, while a comparable increase in AgriTech infrastructure is associated with roughly 18% higher exports; in contrast, a one unit increase in climate variability is associated with about 13% lower exports.

The Effect of AI Virtual Influencers on Purchase Intention: The Mediating Role of Parasocial Interaction: A Field Study on the Fashion Industry in Egypt
candidates.abstract: The objective of this study is to investigate the effect of AI virtual influencers (VIs); in terms of perceived authenticity and perceived anthropomorphism on Purchase intention, viewing the mediating role of Parasocial interaction, by application on the women fashion industry in Egypt. Questionnaire was used to collect data, and a non-probability purposive sampling technique was adopted. A total of 128 responses were collected and analyzed. Partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) was performed in R using the SEMinR package (version 2.5.0). The findings supported all the proposed direct and indirect hypotheses, concluding that perceived authenticity and anthropomorphism play a vital role in directly influencing purchase intention, and that parasocial interaction also plays an indirect role in mediating this relationship.

candidates.title: Federated Learning for Official Statistics: A Systematic Review of Privacy‐Preserving Architectures and the Path Toward GSBPM Integration
candidates.abstract: ABSTRACT National Statistical Offices (NSOs) face an escalating “privacy‐utility” impasse, where the demand for high‐granularity data must compete with the near zero risk tolerance of legal frameworks like the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR). Traditional centralized collection creates “honeypots” for breaches, exposing a nation's entire digital census or tax records. This paper provides a systematic review of Federated Learning (FL) as a decentralized framework that eliminates raw microdata consolidation. Drawing on 77 peer‐reviewed. Studies and technical reports published between 2020 and 2026, the study evaluates Horizontal and Vertical FL architectures alongside Privacy‐Enhancing Technologies (PETs). The analysis reveals that while PETs introduce a “utility gap,” Under controlled experimental settings and standardized non‐IID configurations, the evaluated architectures frequently achieve utility bounds exceeding 90% of their centralized equivalents, though this outcome varies based on the assigned privacy budget () and data distribution. Crucially, the study demonstrates that the mathematical noise required for Differential Privacy (DP) can threaten strict accuracy thresholds; for example, an aggressive privacy budget can cause census distributions to shift more than 77% from the true mean, rendering indicators like Gross Domestic Product (GDP) or unemployment rates statistically meaningless. Beyond these accuracy trade‐offs, the paper addresses the Non‐Independent and Identically Distributed (Non‐IID) nature of government datasets and identifies research gaps in standardized audit trails. The paper proposes a novel roadmap for integrating FL into the Generic Statistical Business Process Model (GSBPM), offering NSOs and international statistical bodies a technically grounded and legally coherent pathway toward next generation data infrastructure.

candidates.title: Crafting Persuasive Environmental Messages for Virtual Influencers: The Role of Anthropomorphic Conversational Style, Persuasion Appeal, and Behavioral Context
candidates.abstract: The use of virtual influencers (VIs) has emerged as an alternative to human influencers for marketing initiatives. Prior studies have focused primarily on the visual characteristics of VIs and their use in advertising settings, with limited attention given to their capacity to drive pro-environmental behaviors (PEBs). We have developed an integrated persuasive framework, grounded in the Elaboration Likelihood Model and Congruity Theory, that links VI characteristics, message appeals, and behavioral context to persuasion outcomes. Study 1 examined VI message strategies and found that competence (vs. warmth) anthropomorphic conversational style and influencing (vs. de-influencing) appeal enhanced message persuasiveness. Study 2 explored the effectiveness of VIs in promoting plastic waste reduction behaviors across different behavioral contexts and found that messages pertaining to difficult (vs. easy) and private (vs. public) behaviors significantly enhanced message persuasiveness, but that messages promoting easy and private behaviors generated stronger behavioral intentions. The insights from these studies can provide valuable guidance to businesses, marketers, and environmental advocates on effective VI message strategies for addressing challenges related to climate change.

candidates.title: Sensorium: An Open-Source Multimodal Data Collection and Curation Library for Embodied Surgical AI
candidates.abstract: Embodied surgical AI requires reliable multimodal data, yet surgical data collection remains costly, difficult to repeat, and strongly dependent on the hardware setup. We present Sensorium, an open-source Python library for recording, processing, annotating, and curating multimodal surgical data from configurable robot and sensor streams using the Robot Operating System (ROS) and ROS2 middleware. The library combines operator-facing data acquisition, configurable processing, semantic annotation, and episodic dataset generation. We evaluate Sensorium across 1516 recordings of phantom, ex vivo, and in vivo porcine experiments involving multiple surgical tasks and sensing configurations, and report preliminary usability feedback.

candidates.title: Gaze-Assisted Supervisory Control for Lunar Robotic Arm Teleoperation Under Concurrent Monitoring
candidates.abstract: Rover-mounted robotic arms can extend human reach during lunar sample handling, but continuous joystick teleoperation requires repeated visual-motor alignment while operators may also need to monitor system states. This paper presents a gaze-assisted supervisory control framework in which gaze nominates a rock or placement target, explicit confirmation authorizes the action, and the robot performs bounded autonomous grasp-and-place execution. The framework was evaluated against manual joystick teleoperation in a mission-analog virtual reality study with 16 participants. The study used a 2 x 2 x 3 within-subject design varying control mode, placement difficulty, and concurrent monitoring load. Mean recorded task completion time decreased from 47.65 to 18.43 s per rock, with 72.5% of this difference arising during grasping. Under the tested auditory monitoring conditions, gaze-assisted supervisory control showed less average proportional slowing, with no detected control-mode difference in monitoring-response accuracy or speed. The rate of gaze shifts between core areas of interest decreased from 49.98 to 27.73 shifts/min, while the raw NASA Task Load Index score decreased from 32.54 to 18.26. However, the benefit was task dependent. In precision placement, manual control yielded lower mean placement error and a higher placement success rate. These findings support a mixed-initiative allocation in which gaze enables rapid task-level intention specification and autonomous execution, while precision-critical stages retain manual refinement.

candidates.title: Making Meets Informal Innovation: Formalisation, Access and Openness in Indian Makerspaces
candidates.abstract: ABSTRACT Makerspaces and fabrication labs (fablabs) are inclusive and open infrastructures. They democratise access to tools and technologies and facilitate bottom‐up innovation. Research on these spaces thus highlights the importance of openness, community orientation and the ability to foster informal experimentation that these spaces enable. In this paper, I examine how these features have been operationalised in contexts characterised by a high degree of economic and institutional informality by focusing specifically on Indian makerspaces and fablabs. I ask how these spaces relate to need‐driven local innovation practices and how they are sustained. The paper uses qualitative data collected through semi‐structured interviews and analyses the organisation of access, learning and innovation in these spaces. The analysis indicates that makerspaces and fablabs in India do not work as open infrastructures in their entirety. Instead, they serve as mediators between informal innovation practices and institutionalised pathways shaped by an entrepreneurial discourse. The analysis further indicates that they create new limits of participation, expertise and knowledge exchange. The paper contributes to the body of literature on open infrastructures and informal innovations by reconceptualising the notion of openness as a result of governance rather than as a characteristic of such spaces.

candidates.title: Emotional and behavioral asymmetries in user responses to virtual versus human influencers
candidates.abstract: As AI virtual influencers (AIVIs) proliferate, understanding human-AI emotional engagement is vital for advancing affective computing. To examine whether AIVIs evoke comparable affective responses to human influencers (HIs), we analyzed 156,918 Instagram comments that received 12+ million likes, integratinglarge language model (LLM)-derived knowledge graphs, emotion analysis, and machine learning. HI-directed discourse shows more differentiated emotional expression and a pattern consistent with more cohesive semantic networks than AIVI-directed discourse. AIVI-directed comments are less likely to express positive affect (24.8% vs. 41.5%) and also less likely to express negative affect (5.8% vs. 9.3%), indicating reduced affective expression of either valence rather than heightened negativity. This group-level tendency is not uniform: affective engagement varies substantially across AIVIs, and that variation is more closely associated with positive than with negative expression. Our Multi-Signal Embedding Network (MSEN), incorporating behavioral metrics and OpenAI semantic embeddings, classified influencer types from behavioral, affective and semantic features (F1 = 0.89), outperforming baselines including a state-of-the-art zero-shot LLM. These findings identify a boundary condition for the Computers Are Social Actors (CASA) paradigm: human-like appearance can elicit social responses without producing affective and semantic response patterns as rich as those elicited by HIs.

candidates.title: From digital shadows to assured intervention: a systematic review of embodiment, authority, and assurance in manufacturing quality digital twins
candidates.abstract: Abstract Rapid advances in AI and robotics are extending manufacturing digital twins beyond passive monitoring to closed-loop control and physical intervention. Yet in manufacturing QA, the term “digital twin” is used for both systems that only observe and systems that act on the physical process. This distinction matters because once a digital twin acts, model validity is no longer enough; the intervention must also be authorized, bounded, traceable, and verified. Existing maturity frameworks capture connectivity and automation but give less attention to the assurance requirements that arise when digital-twin outputs are translated into physical action. We address this gap by introducing an Embodiment-Authority-Assurance (EAA) framework that distinguishes how quality information leads to physical action, who has authority over that action, and how the intervention is assured. We apply the framework to a systematic review of 235 manufacturing QA studies, selected from 868 publications identified through Scopus and Web of Science between 2017 and 2026, classifying them across five maturity levels from digital shadows to governed adaptive QA twins. We found that the frontier of manufacturing QA digital twins is shifting from monitoring and advisory support toward human-approved and bounded autonomous intervention, with higher-maturity applications becoming increasingly visible in recent years. Yet these advances remain fragmented across the literature, with no reviewed study bringing them together into a fully assured intervention chain. By revealing this shift, our study reframes manufacturing QA digital-twin maturity around a new frontier: not simply whether digital twins can act, but whether increasingly autonomous interventions can be governed and assured.

candidates.title: Neither queer, nor just a transaction: realignment speech and the pursuit of heteronormative intelligibility in otome cosplay commissions
candidates.abstract: The commercial rise of Chinese otome games has birthed a novel gig economy: ‘cosplay commissions’, where female fans hire female cosplayers to enact fictional romances. Drawing on 32 in-depth interviews, this study explores the tension in this novel fan practice: while the practice enables participants to experiment with a feminized, consumer-driven model of intimacy, where women actively orchestrate their ideal romance, it simultaneously triggers anxieties about violating scripts of heteronormativity. To manage these tensions, participants collaboratively enact a ‘sanitized romance’ through relational work that meticulously curates idealized heteronormative romance scripts (caring, pampering, and exclusivity), compensating for the perceived failures of real-world masculinity. More importantly, to secure moral legitimacy within China’s patriarchal constraints, participants produce what we term realignment speech, drawing symbolic boundaries to distance themselves from any association with sex work, queerness, or moral deviance. Through this boundary work, they reframe their actions not as ‘buying love’ or ‘loving a woman’, but as ‘immersing in pure love fantasy’. We argue that this ambivalent mode of intimacy – transgressive in practice yet normatively policed in self-understanding – demonstrates how realignment speech renders female desire intelligible and thus survivable within a rigid moral economy through both micro-resistance to dominant norms and creative reappropriation of their toolkit.

candidates.title: Understanding Post-Quantum Cryptography Adoption: Practices, Challenges, and Evolution in Open-Source Software
candidates.abstract: Post-quantum cryptography (PQC) standards establish algorithms for quantum-safe systems, but empirical evidence about how software projects implement and maintain PQC support remains limited. We investigate this implementation and maintenance work by mining 114,361 commits and 5,713 issues across 179 open-source repositories. We use human annotation and validated LLM classification to identify PQC algorithms in commits, classify their adoption status and deployment mode, and identify technical challenges in issue discussions. The commit classification for PQC algorithms reveals that 90% of commits concern maintenance of existing support. From the issue discussions, we construct an 11-category taxonomy of recurring technical challenges. Build, packaging, and dependency failures, along with functional defects, account for approximately half of categorized issues. To examine how PQC support evolves, we use time-series analysis and first implementations of individual algorithms within repositories around NIST standardization milestones. After the 2024 finalization, standardized algorithm names appeared in more than 80% of the PQC development changes analyzed, although earlier names such as Kyber continued to appear. Development activity increased over the observation period. Our milestone analysis, however, did not find a significant increase in first implementations. Migration plans should therefore account for sustained maintenance, prioritize build reliability and integration testing, and track both standardized and predecessor algorithm names. We make the dataset, taxonomy, annotations, and analysis pipeline publicly available.

candidates.title: Beyond Being Accurate: Implications for Using Natural Language Descriptions for Accessible 3D Modeling with~Blind and Low Vision Makers
candidates.abstract: People who are blind or have low vision (BLV) are largely excluded from 3D modeling tools that rely on visual representations of geometry. Natural language descriptions offer a potential path to accessibility, but it is unclear whether language alone can support the deep spatial understanding that editing, not just browsing, requires. Advances in generative AI offer the promise of automatic model description, yet descriptions suited to BLV modelers are structurally distinct from alt-text and from existing 3D model captioning datasets, and the domain-specific requirements for generating them are not well understood. We address this through two coordinated studies: an autoethnographic pilot in which the blind first author worked with 12 sighted participants to develop a taxonomy of descriptive strategies, and a Wizard-of-Oz main study that applied those strategies as idealized scripts with 10 BLV participants. We identify a systematic use-to-editing gap: descriptions that support accurate but incomplete mental models are insufficient for specifying modifications, because editing requires knowing the state of features the user did not know to ask about. We show that this gap produces four failure types (accuracy, completeness, expression, and navigation) that accuracy-focused evaluation frameworks cannot detect. We propose a two-phase evaluation framework that diagnoses the failure type a description system exhibits and guides developers toward targeted design interventions, thereby providing a methodological standard for assessing whether description-based systems genuinely support BLV modelers as creators.

candidates.title: Hierarchical Multimodal Interaction Reasoning for Dyadic Relationship Recognition
candidates.abstract: Dyadic relationship recognition aims to identify the latent social relationship between two individuals from their multimodal interactions. Existing methods typically project heterogeneous cues into a shared representation and optimise a flat classification objective, overlooking that relationships may rely on different interaction patterns. For instance, distant relationships can often be inferred from direct behavioural correspondence, whereas close relationships are better reflected by coordinated affective, behavioural, and multimodal responses. To address this limitation, we propose HiRe-DRR, a Hierarchical Multimodal Interaction Reasoning framework that organises relationship evidence from three complementary perspectives: feature level, interaction type, and relationship hierarchy. HiRe-DRR decomposes facial, bodily, acoustic, and textual cues into low- and high-level representations and constructs homogeneous and heterogeneous cross-participant interactions. We further introduce the Mixture-of-Interaction Transformer (MoI-Former), which treats diverse interactions as specialised experts and employs relation-aware sparse routing to identify relationship-relevant evidence while preserving contextual interaction information. The proposed Hierarchical Conditional Loss (HC-Loss) exploits the hierarchical nature of social relationships through coarse-to-fine supervision, enabling structured relationship reasoning. Extensive experiments on three dyadic relationship benchmarks demonstrate that HiRe-DRR outperforms recent representative image-, video-, and multimodal methods. Our routing analysis further reveals that distant relationships tend to rely on low-level homogeneous interactions, whereas closer relationships focus on high-level heterogeneous interactions. Our code is publicly available at: https://github.com/tw-repository/HiRe-DRR.

candidates.title: Editorial: Computational multimodal sensing and perception for robotic systems
candidates.abstract: Each sensor captures its own slice of the physical world. For robots working in complex and dynamic 2 environments, robust perception requires integrating complementary information from multiple sensory 3 modalities. Vision may provide global context, while tactile, auditory, event-based, and other emerging 4 sensing technologies can reveal more interaction details that are difficult to obtain by vision alone. Together, 5 these modalities can support more robust and adaptive robotic behaviors. candidates.title: From Decision-Maker to Decision Architect: Generative AI and the Changing Role of Leadership
candidates.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is becoming an integral part of managerial work, changing how leaders analyse information, communicate, coordinate, and decide. Much of the existing leadership literature emphasizes productivity effects or debates substitution versus augmentation. We argue that the more fundamental leadership challenge is the reconfiguration of decision authority and the design of decision processes across human–AI arrangements. As GenAI systems become more capable, context-aware, and agentic, leadership becomes less about individual judgement and more about structuring how judgement is distributed across human and AI actors. This conceptual paper asks how GenAI changes leadership decision-making in contemporary organizations. Drawing on research on algorithmic management, the automation–augmentation paradox, AI-mediated leadership, and principal–agent perspectives on AI agents, we develop a framework that positions leaders as decision architects, i.e., actors who deliberately design and govern decision processes rather than merely participate in them. The main contribution of the paper is a typology of four roles GenAI can have in leadership decision making, distinguished by the degree of AI autonomy and the locus of decision authority: AI as assistant, AI as advisor, AI as oversight partner, and AI as delegated actor. For each role, we discuss implications for decision rights, employee autonomy, and managerial expertise. We further argue that the agentic AI highlights classical delegation problems of goal alignment, information asymmetries, and control, turning governance decisions into a core leadership concern. By focusing on design of human–AI decision architectures, the paper contributes to leadership and organization literature by clarifying how GenAI can change concepts of authority, control, and legitimacy in contemporary organizations. We outline a research agenda on AI-augmented leadership capabilities, responsible delegation to AI agents, and the conditions under which GenAI can improve leadership legitimacy.

candidates.title: Housing Prices and Robot Adoption in Corporate Management
candidates.abstract: High housing prices may hinder firms from adopting labor-saving technologies, limiting opportunities for technological upgrading. This paper examines the mechanisms through which housing prices affect firms’ robot adoption. Using fixed effects and two-stage least squares (2SLS) methods on data from 2000–2013, we find that a 10% increase in housing prices reduces a firm’s probability of adopting robots by 1.44 percentage points. Rising housing prices decrease firms’ robot adoption on the extensive margin rather than the intensive margin. The negative impact is stronger for non-state-owned firms and those highly dependent on external finance, but weaker in industries with low capital and skill intensity. Further, we find that investments outside a firm’s core business crowd out robot adoption. Weak corporate governance that exacerbates managerial myopia amplifies these effects. Against the backdrop of China’s overheated housing market, our findings highlight the risks that high housing prices pose to technological upgrading and underscore the importance of improved corporate governance.

candidates.title: Towards Designing for (Dis)Trust in Technologies for Aging
candidates.abstract: Across cohorts of older adults and generations of technology, (dis)trust has continued to shape the acceptance of technologies for aging. Yet, we still know little about if or how to design for older adults’ distrust in technology. Towards this, we reviewed empirical studies in which older adults discussed trust and distrust in relation to technology. Our analysis shows that (dis)trust is constituted in three key ways: emerges when material arrangements of digital systems become illegible, such as when older adults cannot determine where information is stored or trace its movement; is temporally constituted and fluid, building and shifting through prior experience and breakdowns, and at times distrust can operate as boundary work through which individuals limit technology’s reach into their autonomy, relationships, and everyday lives. Our work yields design directions for supporting trust across different phases of technology use and by designing systems that make the movement and persistence of information more perceptible.

candidates.title: Towards Enhanced Psychosocial Well-Being for Persons Living with Dementia: An Integrative Review of Meaningful Activities in Long-Term Care
candidates.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Meaningful engagement in clinical interventions or technology-mediated activities can support the psychosocial well-being of persons living with dementia. However, meaningfulness is often assumed rather than explicitly conceptualized in both academic context and in care practice.OBJECTIVES: This review aims to examine how interventions and activity provision can support psychosocial well-being and how meaningful engagement is shaped by the conditions surrounding their provision, with particular attention to people with moderate and advanced dementia in long-term care facilities. METHODS: An integrative review was conducted through article searching in databases including PubMed, Scopus, and the ACM Digital Library dated from 2014 through 2025. In this review, 60 publications were synthesized for answering proposed objectives and questions.RESULTS: We identified six activity forms and five recurring mechanisms through which activities acquire psychosocial value and are considered meaningful. The central finding is that meaningfulness is not an inherent property of an intervention or technology-mediated activity. It was shaped by the changing relationship between the person, activity, other stakeholders, and care environment. Activities are more likely to become meaningful when they connect with the person’s identity and retained abilities, permit supported forms of agency, are facilitated within responsive relationships and workable care routines.CONCLUSION: This review advances a person-centered design agenda that shifts attention from isolated interventions toward activity-care ecosystems. It extends previous intervention- and technology-centered reviews by explaining how meaningful engagement can be co-produced, evaluated, and sustained in everyday dementia care.

candidates.title: Seeing the Forest for the Trees: Emergent Agreement from Individual Conversations
candidates.abstract: As LLM agents interact in the wild and shape each other's decisions, understanding how they converge toward agreement becomes important. We study this in multi-turn conversations where two LLMs discuss subjective matters, can agree or disagree, and may change their stances. Using a linear classifier on individual conversation activations, we identify an internal representation of agreement. We find that it varies substantially across turns and conversations and does not reliably track external agreement at the individual conversation level. We therefore move beyond the representation of agreement in individual conversations, by aggregating the agreement representation across conversations. Externally, this aggregate view reveals a simple structure: when pooled across conversations, agreement can be predicted well with a Markov process, with agreement at each turn being a direct function of agreement at the previous turn. Similarly, when internal agreement is aggregated, it couples with the external Markov agreement through a power-law mapping, exposing Markovian dynamics in internal representations. Additionally, we find that after a change of stance, models express agreement externally before their internal representations reflect the same shift. These results reveal a joint structure between internal and external agreement that emerges only when internal features are aggregated across conversations. Code available at https://github.com/technion-cs-nlp/SeeingTheForestForTheTrees.

candidates.title: Hybrid optimization of multimodal SLAM for underground robots with seismic vibration geomagnetic and tactile sensing
candidates.abstract: Abstract Reliable underground SLAM remains difficult when GPS, visual features, LiDAR, or external anchors are unavailable or degraded, while non-visual sensors exhibit noise, drift, and environment-dependent uncertainty. We propose a hybrid-optimized seismic/vibration-geomagnetic-tactile SLAM framework that combines complementary sensor factors in a robust factor graph and uses staged COA-PSO-GSA optimization for automated parameter calibration. Evaluation covered 23 complete trajectories (10.2 km; approximately 7.5 h) from simulation, controlled underground corridors, and field tunnel/mine environments, with non-overlapping trajectory-level optimization, validation, and testing subsets. On the test trajectories, mean absolute trajectory error was 0.53 m, convergence occurred in approximately 37 iterations, and error growth remained between 1.81% and 4.09% under the evaluated magnetic, vibration, and tactile degradation conditions. Loop-detection AUC was 0.76, but its difference from the strongest GWO-SLAM baseline (0.74) was not statistically significant after Holm correction (adjusted p = 0.184). The measured foreground update latency was 57 ± 10 ms (approximately 17.5 Hz), indicating near-real-time online operation on the tested platform rather than hard real-time performance. These results support technical feasibility under the tested conditions, while broader claims require larger multi-site validation.

candidates.title: CollabSciReM: Aligning Language Models for Scientific Conversations via Science-Aware Reward Decomposition
candidates.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly used as research collaborators for hypothesis refinement, methodological planning, and technical analysis across multi-turn interactions. In this setting, a useful assistant must be accurate, methodologically justified, logically consistent, and token-efficient. Current alignment approaches rarely achieve all of these together. Instruction-tuned models gain conversational quality through verbosity, and we show that science-agnostic general collaborative rewards compress responses at the expense of scientific rigor. We propose CollabSciReM, a goal-conditioned reward framework that decomposes the session-level reward into conversational quality, scientific rigor, and structural efficiency. We also introduce SciQuality, a pairwise evaluation of multi-turn research conversations grounded in 300 held-out scientific papers and scored on six dimensions: methodological soundness, justification, logical consistency, factual correctness, novelty, and responsiveness. Fine-tuned on 8.62K synthetic research conversations, CollabSciReM is preferred on SciQuality over a science-agnostic reward baseline trained on the same data for all four Llama and Qwen models, including a 65.3% win rate at matched response length. For the 7B and 8B models, CollabSciReM outperforms the science-agnostic reward baseline on the primary metric in 8 of 10 single- and multi-turn benchmark settings. In a blind study, domain experts rated CollabSciReM significantly higher on novelty than the general-reward variant and reported fewer hallucinated responses than both the general-reward variant and the base model.

candidates.title: Remote Expert Evaluation of Tabletop Avatar Gaze Control in Asymmetric Multi-Scale MR--VR Collaboration
candidates.abstract: This paper proposes an integrated setup for a multi-scale asymmetric collaboration scenario in the context of a remote-expert use case, focusing on the expert side. In this system, the remote expert (with an exocentric view in Mixed Reality (MR)) uses a Tangible User Interface (TUI) to precisely position and rotate their avatar within a scaled tabletop World-in-Miniature (WIM). Inside the WIM, the expert's avatar and the operator share the same scale and egocentric view, while the expert retains a global tabletop overview of the plant to support collaboration. Interviews with industry experts during the participatory design phase revealed the need for an egocentric view inside the plant on the remote-expert side to enable full collaboration. We designed and studied three interaction-visualisation combinations to integrate and control the expert avatar's gaze: VR (fully immersive with direct head control), Head (floating screen with direct head control), and Touch (on-avatar screen with touchpad control). We evaluated these methods with 29 participants across two fault-detection tasks: Same Machine, where both collaborators inspect the same machine, and Twin Machine, where they inspect identical machines in separate locations. The VR condition, which combines immersion, direct head control, and a full-scale view, yielded the strongest overall performance and user experience, while the tabletop avatar setup was well received for collaboration. Our findings inform the design of gaze-control techniques for asymmetric MR-VR collaboration and reveal challenges and opportunities for future work.

candidates.title: Voice Design Compass: Guidance for Developing and Reflecting on Voice Concepts for Embodied Characters
candidates.abstract: Abstract An embodied character's voice can shape how we perceive the whole character. Nevertheless, the voice is often overlooked during the planning process, or no explanation is given as to why certain approaches were chosen. We present the Voice Design Compass, a conceptual framework for developing, reviewing, and documenting voice concepts for embodied characters. A voice concept describes how a character's voice should sound and be perceived. It provides a basis for voice selection and production. The Voice Design Compass offers questions to help designers consider early on what influences their voice choices and which unintended effects they might otherwise overlook. These questions address, for example, how a voice relates to the character's appearance, whom it might remind users of, and whether it could reinforce stereotypes.We developed a literature-informed prototype. Ten domain experts from research and industry reviewed its written questions, examples and workflow in formative think-aloud interviews. Qualitative content analysis identified experts' accounts of component relevance, process structure, potential support for design work, and reflection. Needs for change concerned missing content, wording, conceptual distinctions, ease of understanding, cognitive load, and overall organization. Experts suggested using the prototype to clarify requirements, communicate intentions, and revisit decisions across project phases, identifying researchers, practitioners, and non-experts as potential users.We used these findings to revise the prototype into the Voice Design Compass. Four work areas cover project context, voice-concept development with four modular Design Sets, review and practical testing, supporting designers in creating and maintaining their own Project Record.

candidates.title: Trade, AI-robot adoption, and manufacturing transformation: cross-national determinants of firm-level automation in heterogeneous institutional contexts
candidates.abstract: It investigates the multi-dimensional determinants of AI-driven robot adoption among manufacturing firms to examine how perceived benefits, industry peer pressure, and international trade exposure jointly shape firm-level automation decisions across heterogeneous institutional contexts during 2016–2024. Using a firm-level 12,000 manufacturer panel data, it employs PPML estimation with high-dimensional fixed effects, instrumental variables using historical tariffs and partner-country demand shocks to address trade endogeneity, and System GMM to capture dynamic adjustment. The analytical framework integrates TAM, institutional isomorphism theory, and Melitz’s heterogeneous firm model. Empirical results show the strongest adoption driver, with long-run effects nearly double short-run estimates. Industry peer pressure accelerates diffusion through competitive mimicry and network density. Trade exposure causally stimulates automation, exporters respond to quality demands, import-competing firms automate defensively. Cross-country analysis reveals Germany’s highest benefit responsiveness, Korea’s strongest peer effects, and China’s policy-coordinated balanced patterns. It provides the first integrated cross-national empirical analysis of behavioral, institutional, and trade-related automation mechanisms within a single framework, demonstrating that effective automation policy must verify benefit perceptions, industry coordination, and trade integration across diverse institutional contexts. First published online 19 October 2026

candidates.title: MemRevise: A Self-Revising Memory for Conversational Search
candidates.abstract: In conversational search, users correct misun-derstandings, revise their requests and return to earlier topics, so part of the history no longer reflects what they want. Existing benchmarks do not isolate such turns. Current search methods either re-read the history or keep a record of every turn, and none of them marks earlier content as dropped. We introduce CONVREVISE, a benchmark of 4,429 test questions in six tiers of returns and revisions over TopiOCQA, CORAL and OR-QuAC. We also propose MEMREVISE, which combines a revisable memory graph, a 3B writer distilled from teacher memories, and a search guided by the memory. The writer reads each turn once and adds a node that records its topic, its facts and the operations it performs, such as adding, abandoning or reactivating a topic. Topic status follows from these operations, so a dropped topic keeps its facts and can be restored. With a frozen retriever, MEMREVISE reaches a mean MRR@10 of 0.701, against 0.589 for the best competitor, ConvSearch-R1-FT, and 0.617 for a writer distilled the same way without the memory, so the memory and the steps built on it add 0.084. MEMREVISE is significantly better on Topi- OCQA and OR-QuAC, statistically tied with prompted 32B rewriters on CORAL, and never significantly behind the strongest competitor of any tier.

candidates.title: Quantum technology adoption in Japanese industry: prevalence, application interests, timelines, and barriers
candidates.abstract: Abstract Public and private investment in quantum technologies has grown rapidly, yet evidence on the demand side—which firms are adopting, for what applications, on what timelines, and against which barriers—rests largely on industry surveys with undisclosed sampling frames. We report a descriptive, prevalence-style analysis of quantum technology adoption based on a census-approach survey of the complete population of listed firms in Japan. A postal questionnaire was mailed to all 3,890 firms listed on Japanese stock exchanges (December 2025–January 2026); 154 firms returned analyzable questionnaires (crude response rate 4.0%). Because the full sampling frame with firm attributes was available, response propensities were modeled (AUC = 0.671) and inverse-probability weighting (IPW) was used to adjust prevalence estimates for response bias; population totals were obtained with Horvitz–Thompson estimators. Proportions are reported with Wilson 95% confidence intervals. An estimated 59.9% (95% CI 50.5–68.6) of listed firms express at least interest in quantum technologies, but only 16.0% (10.3–24.0) have reached even the PoC-planning stage and 7.2% (3.7–13.6; ≈276 firms) have begun concrete activities. Interest concentrates in quantum machine learning (48.5% of engaged firms), chemistry/simulation (45.6%), and optimization (44.7%). Expected timelines are dominated by indecision: 64% of engaged firms answering could not name a target year for full commercialization, and only 3% expect it by 2030. The most prevalent barrier is the internal shortage of quantum talent (85.3% of engaged firms); the barriers associated with progression from interest to active engagement, however, are the lack of collaboration partners and the lack of a basis for decision-making. The most requested facilitator is expert demonstration of business potential (43.7%), far ahead of government financial support (9.7%). Interest in quantum technologies is widespread among Japanese listed firms, but concrete planning is rare and capability investments are concentrated in a small set of large firms. The findings highlight the importance of use-case demonstration, partnership brokering, and talent development alongside financial support.

candidates.title: A Deep Learning-based Feature-level Privacy-preserving and Intrusion Detection Framework for Intelligent Cybersecurity Using Blockchain
candidates.abstract: The advent of the fast growth of interconnected digital infrastructures has increased the necessity of privacyconserving cybersecurity solutions that can detect network intrusions without revealing sensitive traffic data.Traditional intrusion detection systems (IDSs) typically analyse raw network traffic in a centralized manner, a practice that heightens the risk of data leakage and privacy breaches.This study proposes an IDS that preserves privacy at the feature level by coupling deep representation learning with encrypted, blockchain-based storage.The architecture suggested uses a hybrid Convolutional Neural Network and Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (CNN-BiLSTM) model for extracting compact and discriminative representations of network traffic flows.A multi-stage privacy pipeline comprising feature normalization, secret permutation, and AES-256-GCM encryption is proposed and empirically evaluated against membership-inference, reconstruction, and attribute-inference attacks before storage in a permissioned blockchain ledger.The suggested framework uses encrypted deep feature vectors, unlike current methods of storing raw traffic data or sharing model gradients, which significantly lowers the privacy attack surface and preserve detection.The framework was tested on four popular databases of intrusion detection, such as CICIDS2017, IoTIDS20, NSL-KDD, and TRAIN_TEST_NETWORK.Experimental results demonstrate strong detection performance, with accuracy exceeding 0.95 and reaching approximately 0.997, alongside high processing throughput and low computational overhead.The findings indicate that integrating deep feature learning, cryptographic protection, and blockchain-based storage achieves a favorable balance among privacy preservation, system efficiency, and detection accuracy.The proposed architecture could be scaled to privacy-sensitive environments, such as in IoT systems, healthcare systems, and enterprise security monitoring systems.

candidates.title: A Trust-Boundary Reference Architecture for Secure Cyber-Physical Agriculture: Design and Software-Based Proof-of-Concept for Smart Irrigation
candidates.abstract: Smart irrigation is an operational technology (OT) problem as much as an Internet of Things (IoT) one: software decisions act directly on valves, pumps, pressure and water delivery, so a spoofed reading or a replayed command has physical consequences. This paper presents a technology-neutral reference architecture that makes those consequences controllable. It is organised into seven functional layers and three cross-cutting planes, six trust-boundary classes that fix which properties must be re-established at each crossing, and an auditable crown-asset inventory with an explicit trust-level rubric. Two governing execution principles enforce this structure: local safety authority, which keeps final actuation permission at the field gateway, remote terminal unit (RTU) or programmable logic controller (PLC), and feedback-aware execution, which treats a command as complete only when independent physical feedback confirms it. Building on process-aware and safety-supervision ideas from industrial control, the architecture makes physical confirmation a mandatory completion condition at the local enforcement point, which catches a fully authorised command that is nonetheless physically unsafe, a failure mode that authorisation checks alone cannot detect. These properties are examined through a deterministic, openly available software proof-of-concept that verifies the design against its own acceptance criteria; it is not a field validation. The software executes six attack and failure scenarios plus one nominal-operation control against an intentionally unsecured negative control and a secure controller, under identical, controlled conditions: the negative control is compromised in all 6 attack scenarios and the secure controller in 0/6, with 0/1 false positives on legitimate operation. Analytically, the design costs 21 bytes and 50–60% additional Long Range Wide Area Network (LoRaWAN) time-on-air per record, and 78% of single-step perturbations of the trust-scoring inputs leave asset classification unchanged: the actuator class (A2) is completely stable, and the gateway/RTU/PLC class (A3) is stable under 6 of 7 admissible perturbations (86%), changing only when its credential/update authority reaches the trust-anchor threshold. A sensor-level mapping from sampling rate, measurement drift and physical fault modes to the edge-verification controls they dictate, provisions for secure time, counter recovery and the choice between fail-closed and fail-open safe states, an illustrative hypothetical worked deployment example, and a transfer of the model to greenhouse, fertigation, livestock-watering and cold-chain settings show how the architecture could be applied in practice.

candidates.title: VIP-MINGLE: A Corpus for Videoconference and In-Person Multimodal Interaction in Group Language Engagement
ProAct: Harnessing Streaming Motion Generation and Agentic Reasoning for Realtime Embodied Social Interaction
candidates.abstract: Real-time embodied social interaction places two equally demanding requirements on an agent: continuously generating fluent multimodal interaction behavior, and proactively reasoning over accumulated dialogue and visual context to decide when to take initiative. These requirements must both be satisfied under a strict latency budget, making them difficult to meet simultaneously. We present ProAct , a dual-system framework that manages these time-critical requirements by integrating a low-latency Behavioral System for streaming multimodal interaction with a slower Cognitive System that performs long-horizon social reasoning and produces high-level proactive intentions. The Cognitive System incorporates an efficient memory mechanism and a user-motivation prediction module to reason over accumulated dialogue and visual context and determine when proactive intervention is appropriate. The Behavioral System further includes an intention-conditioned streaming flow-matching motion generator with a disentangled Control-Net branch, which translates deliberative intentions into continuous nonverbal behavior without disrupting interaction fluency. We deploy ProAct on a physical humanoid robot and validate the framework through comprehensive experiments, including real-world user studies, motion-generation benchmarks, and evaluation on ProActBench , a new, targeted benchmark for evaluating proactive trigger detection and restraint in embodied interaction. Code and ProActBench will be released at https://proactrobot.github.io/.

candidates.title: Cloud‐Native and Distributed Systems for Efficient and Scalable Large Language Models—A Research Agenda
candidates.abstract: ABSTRACT Objective Large Language Models (LLMs) are rapidly transforming artificial intelligence applications, but their unprecedented computational, memory, communication, and data‐management demands pose significant challenges to existing computing infrastructures. Traditional cloud and distributed systems were not designed for the scale, dynamic execution patterns, heterogeneous hardware requirements, and service‐level demands of modern LLM workloads. This paper aims to examine how cloud‐native and distributed systems can evolve to support efficient, scalable, reliable, and sustainable LLM training and inference. Methods We conduct a structured analysis of representative research advances and practical developments in distributed LLM training, inference serving, cloud‐native orchestration, resource management, heterogeneous computing, and edge‐cloud intelligence. We organize the analysis around major system challenges, including computation, distributed execution and system software, resource management and serving, security and privacy, data management, and standardization. We further examine representative resource‐management strategies and emerging paradigms, including serverless inference, federated and decentralized learning, trustworthy distributed AI, and heterogeneous computing with emerging accelerators. Results Our analysis reveals that supporting LLMs at scale requires a transition from general‐purpose cloud infrastructure toward LLM‐aware, cross‐layer, and adaptive systems. Existing approaches have improved distributed execution, elastic resource management, multi‐tenant serving, and hardware utilization, but important gaps remain in cross‐layer coordination, workload‐aware orchestration, data and context management, interoperability, security, and system‐level optimization. Based on these gaps, we develop a research agenda covering future directions in sparse and heterogeneous computation, LLM‐enhanced system software, prompt and context management, autonomous cloud management, decentralized intelligence, edge‐cloud collaboration, personalized LLM services, and emerging computing paradigms. Conclusion Cloud‐native and distributed systems will play a central role in enabling the next generation of LLM services. Future infrastructures should evolve toward more intelligent, elastic, interoperable, secure, and heterogeneous platforms that jointly optimize computation, memory, communication, data, and service objectives. Continued advances in system design, standardization, and cross‐disciplinary collaboration will be essential for realizing scalable and sustainable LLM infrastructures.

candidates.title: A study on the effects of mixed explicit and implicit communications in human-artificial-agent interactions
candidates.abstract: Abstract Communication between humans and artificial agents is essential for their interaction. This is often inspired by human communication, which uses gestures, facial expressions, gaze direction, and other explicit and implicit means. This work presents interaction experiments where humans and artificial agents interact through explicit and implicit communication to evaluate the effect of mixed explicit-implicit communication against purely explicit communication and the impact of the task difficulty in this evaluation. Results obtained using Bayesian parameter estimation show that the task execution time did not significantly change when mixed explicit and implicit communications were used in neither of our experiments, which varied in the type of artificial agent (virtual agent and humanoid robot) used and task difficulty. The number of errors was affected by the communication only when the human was executing a more difficult task, and an impact on the perceived efficiency of the interaction was only observed in the interaction with the robot, for both easy and difficult tasks. In contrast, acceptance, sociability, and transparency of the artificial agent increased when using mixed communication modalities in both our experiments and task difficulty levels. This suggests that task-related measures, such as time, number of errors, and perceived efficiency of the interaction, as well as the impact of the communication on them, are more sensitive to the type of task and the difficulty level, whereas the combination of explicit and implicit communications more consistently improves human perceptions about artificial agents.

candidates.title: Beyond Technocratic Optimism: A Systematic Review of Repair in the Circular Economy
candidates.abstract: ABSTRACT Repair is increasingly promoted as a key strategy within the circular economy, yet research on repair remains fragmented. This article provides a systematic review of management and social science research on repair, combining a critical thematic review with bibliometric analysis. We map key features of the field and integrate research streams related to governance, consumer behaviour, repairability, business models and outcomes. Our study shows that the literature is structured around four assumptions related to policy effectiveness, repairability, sustainability outcomes and scalability. By critically examining these assumptions, we challenge the technocratic optimism that dominates the field and reconceptualise repair as a context‐dependent socio‐technical and political‐economic phenomenon shaped by institutional constraints and competing value logics, rather than an inherently beneficial circular economy strategy. We conclude by deriving implications for managers and policymakers and by outlining a research agenda to better understand when and under what conditions repair contributes to circular economy objectives.

candidates.title: From digital companionship to real-world withdrawal: the deep impact of anthropomorphic AI on college students' social interaction and educational responses
candidates.abstract: The rapid advancement of Artificial Intelligence (AI) is reshaping mental health services in higher education, and the widespread adoption of anthropomorphic AI is noteworthy. This article employs a literature-based theoretical reasoning approach, integrating parasocial interaction theory, self-determination theory, and uses and gratifications theory to construct a Triggering–Satisfying–Differentiating framework, systematically examining the mechanisms through which anthropomorphic AI affects college students' social psychology. The study finds that AI effectively alleviates loneliness and social anxiety in the short term by enhancing social presence, providing unconditional acceptance, and offering immediate accessibility. However, its "frictionless socializing" experience simultaneously carries three latent risks: substitute gratification weakens motivation for real-world social interaction; idealized interaction raises interpersonal expectation thresholds; and emotional dependence reinforces social avoidance behavior. For students with social anxiety tendencies, the digital haven may evolve from relief to chronic avoidance, hindering essential social skills and resilience. Accordingly, this paper proposes that universities establish "human–AI boundary" awareness, adopt a "reality-first" principle for behavioral guidance, develop connection-promoting AI tools, and build a multi-tiered digital literacy education system. The article aims to provide theoretical and practical pathways for interventions in college students' social development.

candidates.title: Artificial Narrow Intelligence and Organizational Effectiveness in Higher Education: The Parallel Mediating Roles of Technology Acceptance and Organizational Culture
candidates.abstract: Artificial narrow intelligence (ANI) is being embedded into teaching, research administration, and governance faster than management theory can evaluate it, yet empirical evidence on how ANI shapes organizational effectiveness in higher education remains fragmented. This study proposes and tests the ANI Dual-Pathway Framework, in which technology acceptance (TA) and organizational culture (OC) act as parallel mediators linking ANI to the organizational effectiveness (OE) of academic staff. A sequential quantitative-qualitative design combined a structured questionnaire (511 valid responses from 550 distributed; 97.5% effective recovery rate) with 20 semi-structured interviews and focus-group discussions across public, private, and vocational higher education institutions in Beijing. Confirmatory factor analysis and structural equation modeling, estimated with maximum likelihood and 5000-resample bias-corrected bootstrap for specific indirect effects, were applied. The measurement model was reliable and valid (Cronbach's alpha = 0.914-0.952; KMO = 0.931; CFI = 0.994; RMSEA = 0.015), and the respecified structural model fit well (χ²/df = 1.691; CFI = 0.991; RMSEA = 0.037). ANI had a significant direct effect on OE (β= 0.290). The bootstrap specific indirect effects showed significant indirect effects through TA (β= 0.061) and through OC (β= 0.097). The organizational-culture indirect pathway exhibited a larger effect magnitude relative to the technology-acceptance pathway. Two exploratory propositions regarding socio-technical strain and AI anxiety were examined exclusively using qualitative interview data and were not subjected to quantitative hypothesis testing. Findings indicate that organizational culture constitutes the stronger mediating channel and that investments in trust building and benevolent leadership should accompany technical deployment. Given the cross-sectional nature and geographically bounded sample, causal inferences cannot be definitively established. This work provides evidence-based guidance for higher education managers and policy makers in emerging-economy contexts.

candidates.title: WARMTH, COMPETENCE, OR BOTH? DUAL-PATHWAY CONCEPTUALISATION OF ROBOTIC RESTAURANT ENCOUNTER AND CUSTOMER REVISIT INTENTION
candidates.abstract: Service robots have become a routine presence in restaurants across Asia, yet customer responses to them remain ambivalent. Studies of service robots in hospitality typically bundle the attributes of the machine into a single quality score and regress satisfaction on it. Social cognition research suggests a different structure. People judge any agent, human or artificial, along two largely independent dimensions, competence and warmth, and these dimensions carry different emotional and behavioural consequences. This paper applies that logic to the robotic restaurant encounter and proposes a dual-pathway conceptual model. Robotic service quality and robotic efficiency are specified as competence cues, robotic anthropomorphism and robotic empathy as warmth cues; the two sets of cues form separate appraisals that jointly determine customer satisfaction and, through it, revisit intention. Eight propositions are advanced, including a non-monotonic relationship between anthropomorphism and perceived warmth, and two boundary conditions: cultural service expectations and the utilitarian or hedonic character of the dining occasion. The model offers a way of explaining why robots that perform flawlessly can still disappoint, and it treats the mixed case of a competent but cold robot as the commercially common outcome rather than a measurement anomaly. It also predicts that a service failure met with a warm response will damage satisfaction less than one met with correct but impassive handling. For operators, the framework gives a basis for allocating investment between the two pathways, separating competence attributes fixed at procurement from warmth attributes that can be staged after deployment. For researchers, it specifies a validation strategy combining experimental manipulation with survey-based estimation.
