candidates.title: HomeLoop: A Simulation Framework and Benchmark for Robot-IoT Coordination in Everyday Domestic Assistance and Safety
candidates.abstract: Recent progress in embodied robotics is bringing robots closer to deployment in homes, as vision-language models (VLMs) are demonstrating significant advances in reasoning, making VLM-driven robots promising home assistant agents. These agents will often be introduced into homes that already have cameras, Internet of Things (IoT) devices, and residents with wearables. To fulfill their potential, they need to integrate with existing smart infrastructure and reason through ambiguous scenarios: a smoke alarm may come from a pan about to ignite, a pan already on fire, a resident cooking or a faulty sensor, and each calls for a different response. To that end, we introduce HomeLoop, a simulation framework and benchmark built on Isaac Sim that combines robot bodies, networked devices and wearables, simulated residents and visitors, faulty sensors, and hazards that evolve over time. Our benchmark is composed of 20 tasks across five families grounded in real-world household hazards and needs, and designed so that the same alert can have different causes. A runtime monitor scores each episode with temporal-logic checks on the final outcome and the actions along the way, and every action carries a predefined cost. We evaluate six open-weight and proprietary VLMs. The best achieves a family-balanced score of 61.9%, and across models we see a pattern of over-reaction: failed episodes involving prohibited interventions outnumber those involving missed required interventions by more than two to one, with models often shutting off the stove before investigating the alarm's cause. HomeLoop is an extensible foundation intended for use in research on robot-IoT coordination, long-term memory, proactive assistance, and privacy-safety trade-offs. HomeLoop will be released with 2,100 home layouts that can be automatically furnished in diverse configurations, five robot bodies and 20 networked device types.

candidates.title: AffectiveVLA: Safe and Intent-Aware VLA Control for Human-Humanoid Social Interaction
candidates.abstract: Social touch interactions, such as handshakes, fist bumps, and hugs, require humanoid robots to infer human intent, generate contact-rich motions, and maintain safe physical contact. We present AffectiveVLA, an intent-gated Vision-Language-Action (VLA) pipeline deployed on a Unitree G1 humanoid with dexterous hands. A lightweight RGB-based model recognizes interaction intent from two onboard cameras and converts it into a language prompt for the VLA policy. Low-confidence predictions suppress motion execution, reducing unintended activations. During physical contact, interaction-specific compliance profiles adjust arm impedance, while an independent voice-triggered mechanism initiates a latched safe-stop procedure. Using VR teleoperation, we collected approximately 1,300 multimodal interaction episodes and fine-tuned four VLA models: GR00T, RLDX-1, Being-H0.5, and UnifoLM-VLA-0. On-robot evaluation identifies GR00T as the best-performing standalone model. Integrating intent recognition increases its macro-F1 score from 0.75 to 0.90, while the intent model achieves a p95 inference latency of 6.27 ms. These results demonstrate that explicit intent gating improves the reliability of VLA-based social interaction without compromising real-time operation.

candidates.title: LIVING ENGLISH THROUGH K-POP: AN IPA STUDY OF INDONESIAN EFL LEARNERS' ACQUISITION EXPERIENCES
candidates.abstract: The growth of digital media and online fan communities has opened informal spaces in which Indonesian EFL learners encounter and use English outside formal classroom instruction. K-Pop fandom is one such space, where fans of diverse linguistic backgrounds communicate largely in English through platforms such as TikTok, Instagram, X, and Weverse. However, little is known about the specific kind of English input this communicative interaction provides, or about how Indonesian EFL learners themselves make sense of their acquisition experiences within this informal context. This study addressed two research questions: (1) what kind of language input is found in K-Pop fandom communicative interaction, and (2) how do Indonesian EFL learners perceive their English acquisition experiences through K-Pop fandom practices. Sixteen Indonesian K-Pop fans with five to ten years of fandom involvement and varying levels of communicative activity participated. Data were drawn from documentation of fandom social media interaction across multiple platforms and from semi-structured interviews analyzed through Interpretative Phenomenological Analysis (IPA). Results show that fandom input is layered and multimodal, combining lexical, pragmatic, discourse-level, and multimodal features that typically co-occur. Learners' lived experiences were represented by five group experiential themes: a non-linear shift from anxiety toward confidence, differentiated parasocial motivation, varying degrees of social participation, a perceived functional contrast between fandom-based and classroom-based language use, and a partial, domain-specific reconstruction of self-identity as an English user. These findings suggest that K-Pop fandom functions as a rich but internally differentiated informal English acquisition space, with practical implications for educators who may integrate authentic fan-generated texts as supplementary material while continuing to provide structured speaking practice that fandom-based exposure does not reliably supply. ABSTRAK Perkembangan media digital dan komunitas fandom daring telah menciptakan ruang informal baru bagi pembelajar EFL Indonesia untuk menemukan dan menggunakan bahasa Inggris di luar pembelajaran kelas formal. K-Pop fandom merupakan salah satu ruang tersebut, tempat penggemar dari berbagai latar belakang bahasa berkomunikasi terutama dalam bahasa Inggris melalui platform seperti TikTok, Instagram, X, dan Weverse. Namun, masih sedikit yang diketahui mengenai jenis input bahasa Inggris yang tersedia melalui interaksi komunikatif tersebut, maupun bagaimana pembelajar EFL Indonesia memaknai pengalaman pemerolehan bahasa mereka dalam konteks informal ini. Penelitian ini menjawab dua pertanyaan: (1) jenis input bahasa apa yang ditemukan dalam interaksi komunikatif K-Pop fandom, dan (2) bagaimana pembelajar EFL Indonesia mempersepsikan pengalaman pemerolehan bahasa Inggris mereka melalui praktik K-Pop fandom. Enam belas penggemar K-Pop Indonesia dengan pengalaman fandom lima hingga sepuluh tahun dan variasi tingkat keterlibatan komunikatif menjadi partisipan. Data diperoleh dari dokumentasi interaksi media sosial fandom dan wawancara semi-terstruktur yang dianalisis menggunakan Interpretative Phenomenological Analysis (IPA). Hasil menunjukkan bahwa input fandom bersifat berlapis dan multimodal, mencakup fitur leksikal, pragmatik, wacana, dan multimodal yang umumnya muncul bersamaan. Pengalaman hidup pembelajar direpresentasikan melalui lima tema pengalaman kelompok: pergeseran non-linear dari kecemasan menuju kepercayaan diri, motivasi parasosial yang terdiferensiasi, variasi tingkat partisipasi sosial, kontras fungsional antara penggunaan bahasa berbasis fandom dan kelas formal, serta rekonstruksi identitas diri sebagai pengguna bahasa Inggris yang bersifat parsial dan spesifik ranah. Temuan ini menunjukkan bahwa K-Pop fandom berfungsi sebagai ruang pemerolehan bahasa Inggris informal yang kaya namun terdiferensiasi, dan implikasinya bagi pendidik adalah bahwa teks autentik berbasis fandom dapat diintegrasikan sebagai bahan ajar pelengkap sambil tetap menyediakan latihan berbicara terstruktur yang tidak dapat dipenuhi oleh keterlibatan fandom semata.

candidates.title: Older adults’ social responses to AI virtual humans in digital kinship contexts: associations of loneliness, perceived cues and appraisals with purchase intention
candidates.abstract: As AI virtual humans become increasingly prominent communicative actors on short-video platforms, digital kinship content characterized by kinship-based forms of address, family narratives, caring expressions, and companionship-oriented interaction has begun to enter older adults’ everyday media use and become intertwined with commercial recommendation. Selectively drawing on the three-factor theory of anthropomorphism and integrating it with the Computers Are Social Actors (CASA) paradigm, this study conceptualizes loneliness as a manifestation of sociality motivation; emotional appeal, human likeness, and homophily as perceived cues and appraisals associated with elicited agent knowledge; and social presence and empathy as proximal social responses within the CASA framework. It examines older adults’ social perceptions of and emotional responses to kinship-oriented AI virtual humans and their associations with purchase intention. Using a standardized set of AI virtual human short videos representing key features of digital kinship content as stimuli, we collected valid data from 372 Chinese adults aged 65 years and older and employed partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) and fuzzy-set qualitative comparative analysis (fsQCA) as parallel and complementary analytical approaches. The PLS-SEM results revealed distinct antecedent patterns for the two proximal responses. Emotional appeal showed the strongest association with social presence, whereas homophily was more strongly associated with empathy than with social presence. Human likeness was significantly associated only with social presence, while loneliness was positively associated with both responses. Empathy showed a stronger association with purchase intention than social presence, and all indirect associations were significant except the pathway from human likeness through empathy. The fsQCA results further showed that the combination of emotional appeal and empathy constituted the most stable configuration associated with high purchase intention, whereas loneliness emerged as a core condition only when homophily was also present. This study provides empirical evidence for understanding perceptions of social presence and empathy in later-life human–AI relational perception and offers practical implications for the governance of kinship-oriented AI commercial content and the protection of older consumers.

candidates.title: Reality and Perceptual Gaps in Expressive Swarm Robotics
candidates.abstract: Moving robot swarms from simulation into the physical world can be difficult because small discrepancies in hardware, timing and communication can cascade across interacting robots and alter group behaviour. This challenge is known as the reality gap. When swarms operate in human environments, a second challenge emerges: a perceptual gap between what the swarm physically does and what human onlookers actually perceive. This study examines the same decentralised coordination code deployed across three robotic swarms-tabletop, aerial and human-scale mobile manipulators-during live artistic performances. We find that while the underlying algorithms executed reliably on all three platforms, physical embodiment drastically altered visible motion-distorting execution timescales by more than a factor of three and reshaping trajectory geometry. More importantly, audience surveys revealed that human interpretation does not mirror technical success: how observers attribute meaning (perceived purpose) and how they react emotionally (comfort versus threat) depend heavily on physical form. Meaning attribution and emotional responses did not vary together. Our results demonstrate that successfully transferring swarm software to physical hardware is insufficient for real-world deployment. Addressing the reality gap does not guarantee that the resulting collective motion will be readily interpreted by human observers. Swarms destined for human environments must be engineered not only for decentralised stability but also for the expressive physical dynamics through which humans interpret collective motion.

candidates.title: A preliminary design framework for human-friendly AI interaction: grounded in anthropomorphism
candidates.abstract: People converse with AI as they would with friends in daily life, collaborate with it, and form personalized relationships. In response to these emerging forms of interaction, this study clarifies the concept of Human-Friendly Interaction with conversational AI and develops the Human-Friendly AI Interaction Design Framework (HFAI-DF). This study positions anthropomorphism, a foundational phenomenon in human–AI interaction, as a theoretical bridge and reviews literature on anthropomorphism theory and related research on human cognition. On this basis, this study interpretively derives and organizes how anthropomorphism-inducing stimuli can be applied to AI agents, systematizing them into 30 AI behavioral items that enable human-friendly interaction. Subsequently, a survey was conducted and exploratory factor analysis performed to identify six dimensions as a preliminary structure for a design framework for AI’s human-friendly interaction. These dimensions are: Self-Aware Interaction, User-Adaptive Responsiveness Interaction, Context-Aware Reasoning Interaction, Socio-Emotional Interaction, Creative Collaboration Interaction, and Proactive Assistance Interaction. Within the evolving AI research landscape focused on interaction, this study extends the human-centered AI concept toward human-friendly interaction that operates in an organic manner comparable to human–human conversation, grounded in an understanding of human cognitive functioning. The proposed framework provides both AI providers and designers with an initial structure for shaping and improving the quality of human-friendly interaction.

candidates.title: Student’s Reading Interest in the Use of English AU Fanfiction at Tadulako University
candidates.abstract: The increasing popularity of digital reading platforms has transformed how EFL learners engage with English texts beyond formal classroom settings. Among various forms of digital reading, English Alternate Universe (AU) fanfiction has emerged as a popular literacy practice among university students, offering opportunities for voluntary reading and authentic language exposure. This study aimed to explore EFL university students’ reading interest in the use of English AU fanfiction. Employing a qualitative case study design, the study involved five undergraduate students from the English Education Study Program at Tadulako University who actively read English AU fanfiction. Data were collected through semi-structured interviews and analyzed using thematic analysis. The findings revealed five interconnected themes: reading habits and engagement, reading motivation, positive attitudes toward English reading, enjoyment of reading activities, and willingness to read. The participants reported engaging regularly with English AU fanfiction through various digital platforms, including X (formerly Twitter), Webtoon, TikTok, and Instagram. Their reading practices were primarily driven by personal interest, curiosity, and emotional attachment to stories and characters. The findings further indicated that engagement with English AU fanfiction contributed to increased confidence in reading English texts, greater enjoyment of reading activities, and stronger willingness to engage with English reading beyond academic requirements. In addition, English AU fanfiction functioned as a form of Informal Digital Learning of English (IDLE), providing learners with meaningful opportunities for self-directed language exposure and literacy development. This study highlights the potential of interest-driven digital reading materials to foster reading interest and sustained engagement with English among EFL university students.

candidates.title: Path Dependence in the Development of Surgery in China: From Neolithic Trepanation to Minimally Invasive and Robotic Surgery
candidates.abstract: Background The history of surgery in China has often been interpreted through two partial narratives: modern surgery as a nineteenth-century Western import, and ancient Chinese surgery as originating from Hua Tuo and mafeisan. Both perspectives identify important milestones, but neither fully explains why early operative practices existed in China while safe, reproducible, and scalable major surgery emerged only much later through hospitals, anesthesia, asepsis, professional teams, and health-system infrastructure. Objective This study aims to reinterpret the development of surgery in China through path dependence theory, explaining how empirical intervention, textual external medicine, hospital-based surgery, minimally invasive techniques, and robotic innovation formed historically layered surgical pathways. Methods This study applies path dependence theory and historical institutionalism. It synthesizes archaeological evidence, early Chinese medical manuscripts, classical external-medicine texts, hospital and anesthesia history, surgical literature, health-system studies, workforce and hospital-operations research, and contemporary regulatory materials. The analysis focuses on initial path formation, self-reinforcement, institutional layering, lock-in, critical junctures, and path creation. Results Chinese surgery developed through seven interconnected phases: prehistoric empirical intervention from approximately 3000 to 168 BCE; Han-period textualization of external and invasive therapies between 168 BCE and 145 CE; the symbolic but discontinuous breakthrough of Hua Tuo and mafeisan; imperial stabilization of traditional external medicine from 652 to 1835 CE; modern hospital-based surgery from 1835 to 1949 CE; post-1949 state-building and specialist expansion from 1949 to 1978 CE; and reform-era minimally invasive surgery, robotics, and domestic device innovation from 1978 to the present. These phases show that Chinese surgery did not evolve as a simple linear progression, but through layered institutional pathways shaped by texts, risk, hospitals, state capacity, professional training, technology, regulation, and industrial systems. Conclusions Surgery in China was neither merely a late Western import nor a continuous extension of ancient anesthesia-associated surgery. It was a path-dependent process in which operative capacity became safe, teachable, governable, and scalable only when technical practices were embedded in institutions, teams, infrastructures, financing, regulation, and public trust. This historical perspective highlights the need to evaluate contemporary minimally invasive and robotic surgery not only as technological progress, but also as a governance challenge involving safety, equity, workforce sustainability, and regional surgical capacity.

candidates.title: Sprinkler irrigation for sustainable water management in rabi crops: A comprehensive review
candidates.abstract: Irrigated agriculture accounts for the largest share of freshwater withdrawals worldwide, and nowhere is the tension between food security and water scarcity more acute than in the rabi (winter) cropping systems of South Asia, where wheat, barley, chickpea, mustard, potato, and onion depend overwhelmingly on groundwater during the dry, post-monsoon months. Sprinkler irrigation has re-emerged as a strategically important pressurised irrigation technology for these systems because it combines moderate capital cost, suitability for close-grown cereal canopies, and substantial water savings relative to surface flooding. This review synthesises the recent peer-reviewed evidence (2014–2026) on sprinkler irrigation for sustainable water management in rabi crops, with particular attention to the Indian context. A structured search of Google Scholar and allied scholarly platforms retrieved 232 records, of which 47 studies - verified through CrossRef for authentic DOI assignment - met the inclusion criteria. The evidence indicates that well-managed sprinkler systems routinely achieve application efficiencies of 60–80%, save 20–40% of irrigation water relative to conventional flooding in wheat with little or no yield penalty, and interact synergistically with deficit scheduling, fertigation, conservation agriculture, and soil-moisture-based automation. Indian field studies at the ICAR institutes and state agricultural universities consistently report water productivity gains in wheat and rice–wheat systems. However, the literature also reveals persistent contradictions: plot-level efficiency gains do not automatically translate into aquifer recovery because of rebound effects in water allocation, and adoption among smallholders remains constrained by capital cost, energy pricing, and fragmented holdings. The review identifies research gaps in long-term system performance, sensor-driven automation under smallholder conditions, salinity interactions, and basin-scale impact assessment, and proposes an integrated research and policy agenda linking sprinkler technology with groundwater governance. Sprinkler irrigation, when embedded within such an institutional framework, can be a cornerstone of sustainable rabi water management.

candidates.title: The 2026 State of Open Source in Financial Services: Fintech Open Source Foundation (FINOS)
candidates.abstract: The financial services sector is managing a balancing act between rapid AI adoption with enterprise risk. Now in its sixth year, this annual industry report produced by FINOS and LF Research and in partnership with GitHub, Scott Logic, and sponsor BrightQuery, delivers definitive data on industry adoption and risk management in the era of modern AI. Key findings from the survey include: financial sector GitHub commits jumped 63% year-over-year 58% of institutions now operate an OSPO While 88% credit open source with faster delivery, 52% cite security and privacy as the primary barrier to production AI. To overcome adoption hurdles, leaders must treat open source as a governed discipline and pool resources around shared standards. Read the full report now to benchmark your strategy!

candidates.title: Trail: Accurate Local Smart Home Control Using Decision Models
candidates.abstract: Natural-language driven smart home control remains challenging: cloud-hosted Large Language Models (LLMs) raise privacy concerns, while local Small Language Models (SLMs) can generate invalid actions or misinterpret requests. We introduce Trail (Typed Registry-Anchored Inference for Language commands in Smart Homes), a fully local framework that replaces open-ended command generation with hierarchical typed decisions. Trail exploits the natural structure of a home's action space, selecting a room, device, and operation from candidates derived from the runtime device registry. This ensures valid actions while enabling confidence-based abstention when requests cannot be reliably resolved. We also design a structured memory module that uses typed decisions to support user preferences, device references, and multi-turn interactions. To evaluate Trail, we extend HomeBench and generate three datasets: Trek-Base, which tests natural-language variation; Trek-Robust, which evaluates robustness to changes in the home and its description; and Trek-Memory, which assesses conversational memory across multi-turn interactions. Trail achieves 85.3% accuracy on Trek-Robust versus 69.8% for a finetuned Qwen3.5-4B baseline, while remaining competitive on Trek-Base requests. With memory, Trail resolves 75.6% of the requests that depend on earlier turns, compared with 42.5% for the finetuned baseline given conversation history.

candidates.title: Helping Dementia Patients Find Comfort: Tom Stevens, Founder of Tombot
candidates.abstract: Inspired by his experience caring for his mother with Alzheimer's disease, entrepreneur Tom Stevens founded Tombot to create a realistic robotic companion for people with dementia and others who cannot care for a live pet. Developed with input from hundreds of seniors and animatronic expertise from Jim Henson's Creature Shop, Tombot's robotic puppy Jennie combines lifelike movement, touch response, and sound to encourage emotional attachment. In this article, Stevens discusses the engineering challenges behind Jennie, Tombot's path from startup to commercialization, and his goal of using technology to provide comfort, companionship, and improved quality of life.

candidates.title: Capability-building before transformation: How manufacturing SMEs pursue Industry 4.0 through operational-first digital transformation
candidates.abstract: Digital transformation has become critical for manufacturing competitiveness, yet small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) often struggle to leverage Industry 4.0 technologies because of limited resources and underdeveloped capabilities. While prior research highlights the role of dynamic capabilities and organisational ambidexterity in digital transformation, less is known about how SMEs themselves diagnose digitalisation challenges and prioritise improvement initiatives. This study analyses 17 Detailed Development Plans prepared by manufacturing SMEs within a national Industry 4.0 readiness programme. Using the Gioia methodology, we examine nearly 900 pages of self-assessed challenges and proposed actions. The results suggest that SMEs predominantly interpret Industry 4.0 adoption through an operational lens, emphasising real-time data capture, shop-floor control, and process stabilisation rather than strategic innovation or business model renewal. However, selected cases indicate early planned elements of organisational ambidexterity, where exploitation-oriented digitalisation is combined with exploratory initiatives such as R&D activity, modular capability expansion, and new production technologies. For managers, the findings suggest linking operational digitalisation roadmaps to small-scale exploratory experiments that may help firms gradually move toward ambidextrous capability development. For policymakers, the results indicate that support instruments should follow graduated, capability-staged transformation pathways rather than assuming SMEs are ready for advanced digital adoption.

candidates.title: Robots, artificial intelligence and spirituality/religiosity: a critical literacy perspective on human development
candidates.abstract: Artificial Intelligence, a natural language processing tool, connects human learning and interpretation to algorithms whose source code is hidden to us and uses linguistic modeling, a primarily statistical method, for analyzing and predicting character collocation patterns (Peters et al, 2023, p. 14). Humans willingly have given in to the charms of a “superior” technological cognition that is incapable, in fact, of thinking critically. In this article we aim at presenting the introduction of the use of AI in spiritual/religious spaces from the perspective of critical literacy (Freire, 1974, 1989, 2005, 2015). Thinking in terms of critical literacy allows for a flexibility of the emergence of meanings from diverse loci of enunciation and it enhances social justice. Drawing on a qualitative and interpretive methodology, this study embraces a sample of illustrations of the uses of AI in different contexts of faith, and one particular experience in a Candomblé house, while the authors analyse them from critical perspectives. The results unsettle modernist conceptions regarding meaning and sense making and move towards more pluriversal and situated relationality regarding AI and faith. We conclude that AI helps to expand inter-religious dialogues, spiritual engagement and accessibility may also be fostered outside institutional frameworks through AI. Despite such advantages, profit-driven algorithms can shape spiritual/religious experience, replicate universalized ethics and onto-epistemologies, spread fake news and distort sources of information, while strengthening capitalism, surveillance, racism, not to mention unsustainability.

candidates.title: Making Worlds: For an Ecology of Cultural Production
candidates.abstract: So many modes of culture that are essential to artistic communities are missed when research and policy focus primarily on economic success stories in the so-called creative industries. What about the non-profits, the volunteers, the temporary and non-commercial spaces and groups? And what about the glorious failures? Making Worlds and the book series it initiates, Cultural Production and Everyday Life, correct these oversights by spotlighting the small-scale cultural production of amateurs, hobbyists, autodidacts, and various countercultural scenes. Miranda Campbell and Benjamin Woo advocate for an ecological view of the grassroots forces that sustain and develop cultural and artistic activity. The authors ground this book in examples from their own involvement in and research with cultural communities such as comics creators, game players, music scenes, zine-makers, artist co-operatives, and fan cultures. Serving as a response to some of the early twenty-first century’s gig-economy boosterism, this is also a book that seeks to document how culture is not only consumed but produced in everyday practices. Broadening the field of cultural studies and understandings of what constitutes culture, Making Worlds recognizes and celebrates the work of the chronically unsupported, underfunded, and the precariously situated in spaces at risk of eviction and gentrification.

candidates.title: Robotic Assistants in the Operating Room: A Systematic Review of Vision‐Based Systems for Nonoperative Tasks
candidates.abstract: Nonoperative tasks in the operating room, such as instrument handling, sterile packaging, and logistics, are demanding yet have received less robotics attention than autonomous surgery. This review, the first to synthesize this literature, maps the perception methods, autonomy levels, methodological quality, and clinical readiness of vision‐based robotic assistants for scrub nurse, circulating nurse, and OR logistics roles. Searches of PubMed, IEEE Xplore, Scopus, ACM Digital Library, Web of Science, and Google Scholar returned 465 records; 20 publications describing 11 robotic system families met inclusion criteria. Most evidence, 17 publications across eight system families, concerns scrub nurse assistance; circulating nurse support, OR logistics, and dental assistance are each represented by one system. Vision methods have moved from classical image processing and predefined gestures toward deep learning, multimodal perception, and vision–language–action models, but autonomy has not kept pace: one system family reaches LoA 1, seven LoA 2, and three LoA 3, with Technology Readiness Levels spanning TRL 4 to TRL 6. Reported success rates are often high but rarely comparable and mostly generated in laboratory or simulated settings. Closing that gap requires stronger evidence on safety, sterility, failure recovery, workflow integration, execution speed, reproducibility, and, notably absent, manipulation of deformable sterile materials.

candidates.title: Artificial Intelligence in Embodied Learning: A Systematic Literature Review
candidates.abstract: ABSTRACT Background Embodied learning (EL) is an educational approach that posits that cognition develops as learners interact with their environment through physical activity or sensory experiences. Artificial intelligence in education (AIED) supports teaching and learning for both teachers and students, for example through personalised intelligent tutoring systems. However, prior research on EL has focused primarily on students' cognitive and emotional abilities and the integration of body and task, rather than on technological elements, and research on technology‐based embodied learning (TBEL) has centred on immersive technologies such as VR and AR. Objectives This study aims to explore the relationship between AI technology and EL by analysing (1) the types of AI utilised in EL‐related research (algorithm or model, data modality, AI role), (2) learners' outcomes obtained from AI‐based EL, and (3) the limitations and solutions when applying AI to EL. Method This study is a systematic literature review based on the PRISMA 2020 guidelines, and no meta‐analysis was conducted. This study only referenced papers published since 2016 that included both AI technology and EL, were written in English, and dealt with learning processes mediated by physical activity. A study was treated as within scope only where the physical activity was tied to the concept to be learned. Papers were excluded if they did not specify the AI algorithm or model, were not peer‐reviewed, were secondary studies, were not in the field of education, were unavailable in full text, emphasised only simple skill acquisition in physical education or music, or emphasised only simple speaking activities in foreign language learning. Searches were conducted on 16 September 2025 in ACM, ERIC, and Web of Science. Given the diverse types of included studies, risk of bias was assessed using the MMAT2018 tool. Due to the varied nature of the data, a multi‐faceted data synthesis was performed. Co‐occurrences between data modality and AI role, and between AI role and learner outcomes, were visualised using heatmaps. The flow between the three variables was represented using a Sankey diagram. Finally, all frequencies were recalculated after excluding papers appraised as Low or not appraised, to test which patterns depended on weaker evidence. Results A total of 23 papers were reviewed. As multiple data points could be extracted per item, the relative proportion was calculated against the number of coding instances per item. The most frequently used AI algorithm/model in the EL context was deep learning, and the data modality was image data. Where multiple data types were used, it was tagged as multimodal, accounting for 34.8%. Analysis and evaluation roles were most frequently extracted, and cognitive outcomes were reported most often. Key limitations identified included restricted participant numbers due to research design and studies conducted in controlled environments. Among papers appraised as High, the most frequent pathways ran from multimodal data to recognition and detection and from sensor data to analysis and evaluation, and cognitive outcomes were the most frequently reported. When papers appraised as Low or not appraised were set aside, the concentration of AI in analytical roles persisted, whereas the evidence for AI as an interactive or generative participant weakened. Discussion This review describes reported patterns rather than pooled effect estimates, as no meta‐analysis was conducted. Exclusion of grey literature may introduce publication bias. Furthermore, the potential risk of selection bias exists as literature was collected based on inclusion/exclusion criteria. This study is significant in that it identified how AI is utilised within the EL context and the learner outcomes reported alongside it, particularly as the scope of AIED broadens.

candidates.title: Ethics by Configuration: AI Ethics Principles in Coding Agent Instructions
candidates.abstract: As AI coding agents become integral to software development, projects increasingly utilise configuration files, such as context files and skills, to govern agent behaviour. While AI ethics principles are widely used in research and policy, little is known about whether and how they are reflected when developers configure coding agents. We studied ethics principles in 40,079 configuration files across 8,893 GitHub repositories. Using a validated large language model (LLM) classification, we measured the prevalence of ethics-related statements, and qualitatively analysed 702 stratified samples across 679 files to uncover the ethical considerations reflected in these files and the parties they concern. Ethics-related statements appeared in 39.4% of files and 61.5% of repositories; concentrated on accountability, transparency, privacy protection, and reliability; and occurred more often in task-specific files such as skills than in project-wide context files. Our qualitative analysis identified 30 categories of ethical considerations, which take the form of concrete rules for the agent. Accountability appeared mainly as requirements for human approval, transparency as explain and honestly report the agent's work, and fairness as accessibility and localisation. These considerations reveal a difference in focus. Whereas public ethics frameworks aim to protect society and end users, configuration files mainly concern developers, maintainers, and community members in the development workflow. Ethics-related content appeared mainly in prose-based files, and whether agents follow these instructions remains untested. We discuss the implications for practitioners, researchers, and policymakers.

candidates.title: Being a Padawan and Mastering the Force: A Dissertation Quest
candidates.abstract: This study explores the experiences of one doctoral researcher and two doctoral peers navigating mentor-mentee relationships through a literary lens, employing autoethnographic methods to capture the nuanced dynamics of guidance, expectation, and emotional labor. Data were drawn from narratives found in reflective journals, personal memos, email exchanges, text messages and conversations with four faculty mentors and two doctoral peers accumulated through the doctoral journey. The narratives were analyzed using thematic analysis. Using vignettes and incident reports, the research highlights key turning moments in the doctoral journey that shaped perceptions of mentorship, emphasizing both the cognitive and affective dimensions of academic identity development. Findings reveal that mentees often confront mismatched expectations, experience emotional labor, and negotiate cognitive dissonance when aligning their scholarly identities with mentor guidance. By centering the mentee perspective, this study challenges traditional views of passive doctoral socialization and underscores the importance of active, reciprocal engagement in mentorship. The research contributes to understanding the complexities of doctoral mentorship and offers practical implications for cultivating supportive, reflective, and equitable mentor-mentee relationships in higher education. Additionally, the study contributes to the literature by offering an experience-based framework of JOY (Journey, Openness, Yield) for understanding doctoral mentorship process and proposes to help guide productive mentor-mentee relationships.

candidates.title: Relational Complexity: Making Sense of Social Companion AI Use
candidates.abstract: The adoption of social companion AI (SCAI) is often framed in terms of the positive features it offers users, including its nonjudgemental nature, agreeableness, and availability. Here, we argue the appeal of these features primarily arises from the difficulties inherent in human sociality. SCAI reduces what we term relational complexity, or the demands and risks inherent in human relationships. Drawing insights from studies of human cognition, communication, and human-computer interaction, we identify six distinct sites of relational complexity that we posit are integral to understanding SCAI adoption. These include: (i) relationship formation and dissolution; (ii) achieving mutual understanding; (iii) interpersonal motives and strategic uncertainty; (iv) social partner evaluation and self-presentation; (v) social embeddedness and information flow; and (vi) reciprocity and relationship maintenance. By attenuating relational complexity, SCAI offers users some of the experiences associated with companionship while reducing the demands intrinsic to obtaining such experiences from another person. However, the lower interpersonal risk and diminished cognitive load that attracts users to SCAI may contribute to myriad negative impacts, including relationship displacement, social demotivation, social deskilling, and risks to privacy. The concept of relational complexity thus provides a framework for studying both the appeal of artificial companionship and its implications for human wellbeing.

candidates.title: Talking with language models
candidates.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) produce text that invites us to treat our interactions with them as conversations, and to treat them as intelligent interlocutors who remember, act, and make commitments. We argue that this conversational presupposition is mistaken. We introduce the artifactual stance, which describes human–AI interaction in terms of their design and affordances, rather than potential intentional attitudes. On our account, LLMs produce candidate text that users interpret, evaluate, and sometimes adopt as their own speech. We argue that such exchanges are not conversations, since generating text does not itself constitute an utterance or the performance of a speech act. Rather the communicative and normative work of interpretation, commitment, and action remains with the user. Our framework explains both the sophistication and usefulness of LLMs, and the conversational appearances that can be traced back to properties of the interface and to artifact design. It also reframes puzzles about AI reference, the persistence of supposed interlocutors, and responsibility for AI-generated text. These questions are better approached through an account of how artifacts mediate human linguistic practices than through assumptions about AI speakerhood.

candidates.title: SocialCoAct: Enabling and Benchmarking Egocentric Social Co-Action for VLM-Based Humanoid Robots
candidates.abstract: Enabling humanoid robots to participate effectively in social interactions is important for their integration into human-centered environments. Existing methods, however, typically map pre-generated speech directly to continuous motion trajectories but have limited awareness of complex social environments and lack explicit high-level semantic action planning. We introduce SocialCoAct, a unified agent-centered framework for VLM-based egocentric social co-action. We formulate egocentric social co-action as an end-to-end agent task and develop SocialCoAct-Agent, which transforms egocentric observations and dialogue history into verbal responses and atomic action sequences, aligns each action with its corresponding utterance span, and executes the resulting behaviors in MuJoCo and on a physical humanoid robot. To evaluate the VLM capabilities required by this task, we construct SocialCoAct-Bench from continuous egocentric recordings of natural multi-party interactions. The benchmark comprises 423 human-verified multiple-choice questions across three subtasks: Long Episode Understanding (LEU), Speaker Intention Understanding (SIU), and Coordinated Action Planning (CAP). Across a diverse set of closed-source and open-weight VLMs, including general and egocentric models, the highest overall accuracy is 77.54%, while accuracy on the hard subset reaches only 46.51%. Extended reasoning improves Qwen3-VL-2B and Qwen3-VL-4B by 19.62 and 17.02 percentage points, respectively, but reduces inference throughput by 53.6$\times$ and 20.2$\times$. Visual-input ablations further show that the benefits of visual context vary across models. SocialCoAct provides a foundation for developing and evaluating VLM-based humanoid agents that coordinate context-aware speech and action in complex social interactions. The codebase and benchmark will be made publicly available upon publication.

candidates.title: InstAgent: A Recursively Self-Improving Agent Operating System for Heterogeneous Robot Collaboration
candidates.abstract: Heterogeneous robot teams enable complex, long-horizon tasks by combining complementary sensing, mobility, and manipulation capabilities across multiple embodiments. Yet existing systems struggle to retain execution-time corrections as reusable experience, maintain task-relevant context memory across space and time for reliable handoffs, and explicitly represent the inter-robot dependencies required for structured collaboration. In order to address these challenges, we present InstAgent, a recursively self-improving (RSI) Agent Operating System for heterogeneous robot collaboration. InstAgent organizes team behaviors as agentic behavior trees (BTs) that explicitly model capability assignment, inter-robot dependencies and handoff checks. The RSI mechanism updates these collaboration programs from execution feedback and preserves successful revisions for reuse in future tasks, while shared multimodal spatio-temporal memory provides context for planning and handoff validation. Experiments on 20 real-world multi-robot tasks with three high-level models show consistent gains in task success, first-attempt completion, and execution efficiency.

candidates.title: Machine psychology for language models
candidates.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) show increasingly advanced emergent capabilities and are being incorporated across various societal domains. Understanding their behavior and reasoning abilities is therefore important. We argue that a fruitful direction for research is engaging LLMs in experiments inspired by psychology that have traditionally been aimed at understanding human cognition and behavior. Here, we highlight and summarize theoretical perspectives, experimental paradigms, and computational analysis techniques that this approach brings to the table. It paves the way for a "machine psychology" for LLMs that goes beyond performance measurements and focuses instead on computational insights that move us toward a better understanding and discovery of emergent abilities and behavioral patterns in LLMs. We review existing work taking this approach, synthesize best practices, and highlight promising future directions. We also describe the important caveats of applying methodologies designed for understanding humans to machines. We posit that leveraging tools from experimental psychology to study LLMs will become increasingly valuable as models evolve to be more powerful, opaque, multimodal, and integrated into complex agentic real-world settings.

candidates.title: Opening Musical Creativity? Embedded Ideologies in Generative AI Music Systems
candidates.abstract: AI systems for music generation are increasingly common and easy to use, granting people without any musical background the ability to create music. Because of this, generative-AI has been marketed and celebrated as a means of democratizing music making. However, inclusivity often functions as marketable rhetoric rather than a genuine guiding principle in these industry settings. In this paper, we look at four generative-AI music making systems available to the public as of mid-2025 (AIVA, Stable Audio, Suno, and Udio) and track how they are rhetoricized by their developers, and received by users. Our aim is to investigate ideologies that are driving the early-stage development and adoption of generative-AI in music making, with a particular focus on democratization. A combination of autoethnography and digital ethnography is used to examine patterns and incongruities in rhetoric when positioned against product functionality. The results are then collated to develop a nuanced, contextual discussion. The shared ideology we map between producers and consumers is individualist, globalist, techno-liberal, and ethically evasive. It is a 'total ideology' which obfuscates individual responsibility, and through which the nature of music and musical practice is transfigured to suit generative outcomes.

candidates.title: MTAVG-Bench 2.0: Diagnosing Failure Modes of Cinematic Expressiveness in Multi-Talker Audio-Video Generation
candidates.abstract: In recent years, Multi-Talker Audio-Video Generation (MTAVG) models have shown promising performance on fundamental metrics such as lip-sync and audiovisual alignment. However, these metrics remain insufficient for assessing cinematic expressiveness in scene-level generation. In multi-character scenes, generation models must go beyond audiovisual realism to convey coherent character performance and other higher-level cinematic qualities. To fill this gap, we introduce MTAVG-Bench 2.0, a benchmark for diagnosing failure modes of cinematic expressiveness in multi-talker audiovisual generation. Unlike prior settings that mainly focus on the quality of basic multi-turn dialogue, MTAVG-Bench 2.0 targets short-drama and scene-level generation, and establishes a high-level failure taxonomy spanning acting, atmosphere, and cinematography. Based on this taxonomy, we construct 11.6K diagnostic QA instances, together with subsets for short-drama-level assessment and temporal localization of failure modes, to systematically evaluate the ability of omni large language models to diagnose high-level audiovisual failures. Experimental results show that commercial omni models such as Gemini substantially outperform other evaluators, yet even the strongest models continue to struggle with complex failures in our benchmark. These results demonstrate that MTAVG-Bench 2.0 provides a systematic benchmark for failure diagnosis in cinematic multi-talker audiovisual generation. The code and data are available at GitHub and Hugging Face.

candidates.title: TARMAC as a taxonomy for robot manipulation in chemistry
candidates.abstract: Abstract Laboratory automation has benefited substantially from well-defined protocols and machine-readable representations of chemical procedures. Yet a long tail of context-dependent physical tasks, including setup, adjustment, and cleanup, continues to require manual intervention or bespoke robotic implementations tailored to individual workflows and platforms. This study examines whether this apparent diversity can be organized into a structured and reusable action space. TARMAC ( TA xonomy for R obot MA nipulation in C hemistry), an empirical taxonomy of laboratory actions, is derived through a bottom-up analysis of instructional chemistry practice. The taxonomy comprises 18 physically meaningful primitives organized by three dimensions: wrench dependence, actuation directness, and motion periodicity. Evaluation through cross-corpus protocol decomposition and robotic instantiation addresses expressive coverage and proof-of-concept executability. Across 23 procedures, 904 of 917 manipulative steps map to the primitive set, while robotic tests instantiate 8 primitives in five tasks across four robotic configurations. Together, these results indicate that laboratory manipulation can be organized as a structured action space across the examined contexts. TARMAC therefore provides a descriptive basis for organizing and comparing manipulation requirements across experimental workflows and robotic embodiments.

candidates.title: MOSAIC: Unveiling the Moral, Social and Individual Dimensions of Large Language Models
candidates.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed in sensitive applications including psychological support, healthcare, and high-stakes decision-making. Existing evaluation benchmarks rely almost exclusively on Moral Foundation Theory (MFT), neglecting other key dimensions such as social values, personality traits, and individual characteristics that shape human ethical reasoning. We introduce øurbenchmark , the first large-scale benchmark designed to jointly assess the mo ral, s ocial, a nd i ndividual c haracteristics of LLMs. øurbenchmark comprises nine validated questionnaires drawn from moral philosophy, psychology, and social theory, alongside four platform-based games designed to probe morally ambiguous scenarios, totaling over 600 curated items. We validate the benchmark across six models from different families, providing empirical evidence that MFT alone is insufficient for comprehensive ethical evaluation of LLMs. All resources are publicly available.

candidates.title: Open source laser-scanning photostimulation for neuroscience with Zapit
candidates.abstract: Optogenetic tools are indispensable for understanding the causal neural mechanisms underlying animal behavior, providing millisecond-precision control over genetically defined neural populations. Random-access laser-scanning optogenetics is a powerful and underutilized method for transiently manipulating cortical activity in mice. Despite the utility of this technique, no general-purpose open-source implementation currently exists, and potential users need expertise across optics, real-time hardware control, and programming. This represents a major barrier to adoption, particularly for newly established research groups. Here we present ‘Zapit’, the first open-source general-purpose platform for random-access laser-scanning optogenetic experiments in head-fixed mice. Zapit is fully documented, has a user-friendly GUI, works in stereotaxic coordinates, and comes with easy-to-build hardware options that extend functionality beyond any published system. We validate Zapit’s performance through electrophysiological recordings and cortical photoinhibition in behaving mice. Zapit is a novel and innovative tool with the potential to democratize laser-scanning optogenetics and significantly increase uptake throughout the scientific community.

candidates.title: A Taxonomy of Mental Health and Technology Needs for Alzheimer’s and Dementia Caregivers
candidates.abstract: Family members caring for individuals with Alzheimer's disease and related dementias (AD/ADRD) provide the foundation of long-term care worldwide. In 2023, more than 11 million U.S. family and friends contributed 18 billion hours of unpaid care, often at the cost of their own physical and mental health. These informal caregivers-also referred as the "invisible second patients"-experience elevated rates of mental health problems. Yet research commonly reduces their complex psychosocial experiences to a single construct of caregiver burden, obscuring which specific needs are unmet or effectively supported. At the same time, digital and AI-enabled technologies are rapidly expanding, from smartphone apps and videoconferencing to sensor platforms and AI chatbots. However, the absence of shared frameworks across medicine, psychology, and technology research limits cumulative progress. This study introduces a Caregiver Mental Health and Technology Taxonomy that systematically links AD/ADRD caregiver needs with corresponding classes of technology-based interventions. Drawing from an interdisciplinary literature review and two qualitative studies with caregivers, the taxonomy identifies mismatches between caregiver priorities and existing technological support, highlights under-served domains such as relational strain and compassion fatigue, and proposes design directions for adaptive, responsive systems. The framework offers a shared vocabulary to guide clinicians, researchers, and technology designers in developing more person-centered and clinically grounded innovation in dementia care. Supplementary Information: The online version contains supplementary material available at https://doi.org/10.1007/s12126-026-09686-4.

candidates.title: SWAP: Test-Time Steerable Humanoid Whole-Body Collision Avoidance
candidates.abstract: Humanoid robots operating in human-centric environments must coordinate the entire body to traverse tight, cluttered spaces while maintaining balance. Existing methods often struggle to jointly consider dynamic stability and collision avoidance from high-dimensional perceptual inputs. Moreover, for humanoids, safe behavior is inherently multimodal: the same obstacle may admit multiple valid traversals, which is difficult to represent with a single deterministic policy. To address these challenges, we propose SWAP (Steerable Whole-body Avoidance Policy), a hierarchical framework that separates collision-aware decision making from stabilization. A high-level, perception-conditioned diffusion policy generates multimodal, collision-aware motion proposals, while a low-level whole-body RL controller tracks these proposals and maintains dynamic balance. To efficiently train the high-level policy, we obtain scalable supervision via hindsight labeling: we roll out the low-level policy under randomized commands, place obstacles only in the space that each executed motion did not sweep, so the motion is collision-free by construction, and re-render the perception the robot would have seen. At deployment, Monte Carlo sampling with simple cost signals steers the diffusion model toward safe, task-aligned behaviors without heavy reward tuning. Experiments in simulation and on a real Unitree G1 humanoid show reliable avoidance with static and dynamic obstacles. Test-time steering further enables customization, improving targeted rewards (e.g., speed, orientation, or posture) by 34% on average while maintaining a high collision avoidance rate. Together, these results support a practical solution to humanoid whole-body collision avoidance with test-time steerability. Project website: https://iscoyizj.github.io/SWAP-steerable-humanoid-oa-website/

candidates.title: Formal Raising: Embedding Verifiable Ethical Properties into the Development of AI
candidates.abstract: Alan Turing proposed constructing a ``child machine'' and educating it rather than directly programming an adult-like intelligent machine. Recent work on model raising revives this developmental view for Large Language Models by arguing that moral values should accompany capability acquisition from the beginning rather than be added only through post-hoc alignment. This paper proposes Formal Raising (FR): selected moral values are represented as explicit, machine-checkable properties that participate in development, evaluation, and action selection. We present a C-based reasoning framework in which candidate actions are evaluated against prioritized ethical properties. Conflicts are resolved w.r.t. a given order, strict rules are non-defeasible, and underdetermination is reported explicitly. Exceptions are not encoded as special cases but emerge from the comparison of alternatives. We provide examples that cover conflicts involving life, truthfulness, harm, privacy, autonomy, and strict rules. We outline a property layer inspired by a Property Specification Language (PSL) for state and temporal requirements and discuss its integration into a raising process.

candidates.title: Designing IoT Applications with Serverless Concepts and Open Source Tools
candidates.abstract: This work explains step-by-step development and implementation of serverless functions at sensor, edge, and cloud levels for IoT-enabled applications, addressing data privacy, cost inefficiency, and scalability challenges. It discusses the systematic deployment of serverless functions across sensor nodes, edge clusters, and cloud infrastructure using open-source tools such as ESP-IDF, WasmEdge, and OpenFaaS. It covers key topics including edge-fog-cloud computing, IoT communication protocols (MQTT, LoRa, Zigbee, etc.), benchmarking methods, and performance comparisons. It highlights the integration of serverless concepts to build efficient computing platforms, drawing on insights from collaborative research with leading universities. Discusses the application of serverless functions on edge-enabled clusters, such as Raspberry Pi clusters mounted at our research labs. Details exploration of IoT communication protocols and offers benchmarking methodologies for evaluating serverless IoT systems. Expresses the utilization of open-source tools and frameworks to activate serverless functions in IoT-enabled applications. Explains future directions for scalable and efficient IoT application development. This book is for professionals, academicians, and students interested in IoT-enabled applications.

candidates.title: The Generative Economy of Agony: Latent Structures of Meaning and Resilience Mechanisms in the Lyrical Work of Taylor Swift
candidates.abstract: Abstract This article employs the methodology of Objective Hermeneutics to reconstruct the latent structures of meaning and resilience mechanisms within the lyrical oeuvre of American songwriter Taylor Swift. Moving beyond intentionalist and biographical reductionism, the analysis identifies a generative case logic structured around four sequential dimensions: the dialectic of emotional staging and drive structure, the somatization and material reification of psychological trauma, the establishment of a generative economy of agony, and the ultimate transition toward absolute indifference. Drawing on the sociology of emotion and theories of emotional capitalism, the study demonstrates how the lyrical subject converts vulnerability, powerlessness, and rage into highly liquid aesthetic and emotional capital, culminating in a structural resilience defined as a "sequin armor". Furthermore, the paper integrates the Aristotelian concept of catharsis to illustrate how this autofictional narrative serves as a therapeutic script, facilitating collective emotional regulation, purification, and empowerment within transnational fan communities. Ultimately, the work is analyzed as a late-capitalist protocol of emotional labor, where private suffering is systematically economized and transformed into a globally resonant resilience framework.

candidates.title: ADDITIVE MANUFACTURING: CHARACTERIZING CARTEL UAS INNOVATION PATHWAYS
candidates.abstract: Additive manufacturing (AM), particularly low-cost 3D printing, is creating a new pathway for Mexican cartels to locally reproduce, modify, and customize unmanned aircraft systems (UAS) and their components. Cartels already demonstrate technical adaptability, commercial-off-the-shelf (COTS) supply chains, and the use of 3D-printed components that could support broader AM adoption. The growing availability of digital UAS designs, technical documentation, inexpensive printers, and commercially available electronics could reduce cartels’ dependence on identifiable COTS platforms while enabling more decentralized and adaptable drone supply chains. Over the next five years, advances in AI could further lower the technical expertise and time required to design and manufacture customized UAS components, increasing the potential significance of AM as a component of the cartel UAS ecosystem.

candidates.title: Designing an Open-Source Multi-Vat Digital Light Processing Printer
candidates.abstract: Abstract Additive manufacturing has undergone rapid evolution in modalities that can mimic some of the aspect of native human tissue architectures with high resolution. Among these emerging approaches, digital light processing (DLP)-based printing enables the fabrication of intricate biomimetic architectures through the photopolymerization of polymer-based hydrogels. The recent emergence of multivat printing further enhances this capability, enabling the spatial arrangement of differently formulated or labeled photocrosslinkable resins. However, the widespread adoption of DLP printing remains constrained by the high cost, proprietary hardware, and limited customizability of commercially available systems. Here, we present an open-source multivat DLP printing platform developed through the integration and modification of two low-cost commercially available 3D printers. A dedicated Python-based graphical user interface was developed, providing user-defined control over critical printing parameters, including exposure time, layer height, printing sequence, and vat switching. Comprehensive hardware documentation and a complete bill of materials (BOM) are provided to ensure reproducibility and accessibility across research laboratories. In addition to multivat printing, the system enables spatial modulation of mechanical properties within a single photocrosslinkable formulation through programmable light exposure and supports enhanced z-axis resolution through user-defined layer thickness control. The platform was validated through the fabrication of geometrically complex, multivat, and mechanically heterogeneous constructs. Collectively, this work establishes an accessible and customizable DLP printing platform that enables advanced hydrogel fabrication and demonstrates automated multivat printing.

candidates.title: Water–material interactions in underwater laser additive manufacturing: process physics, microstructure evolution, and performance
candidates.abstract: Abstract A harsh marine environment causes severe surface damage to underwater infrastructure, jeopardizing its long-term reliability and necessitating in-situ underwater repair. Underwater laser additive manufacturing (ULAM) is a promising technique that enables direct deposition of metallic materials on water-exposed components. While there is a consensus that ULAM fundamentally deviates from land-based processing due to extreme boundary conditions such as strong optical attenuation, intensified heat dissipation, and environment-assisted chemical reactions, significant scientific controversies remain. Current studies present contradictory conclusions regarding the exact mechanisms of defect nucleation, the stability of the gas-liquid interface in local dry cavity, and the competing effects of thermal gradients on microstructural phase evolution versus residual stress. This review evaluates these disputed mechanisms. By dissecting the multi-physics coupling among the laser, melt pool, and underwater environment, we identify the fundamental causes of discrepancies in existing literature. This review establishes a comprehensive process-structure-property framework that systematically links transient thermophysical phenomena to microstructural characteristics and surface degradation behavior. By delineating established knowledge from unresolved contradictions, this work highlights the critical scientific gaps and provides a clear roadmap for achieving controllable quality and reliable engineering deployment of the ULAM technique.

candidates.title: A Low-Cost Co-Designed Robotic System for Selective Sweet Pepper Harvesting with Edge-Computed Perception and Decision-Making
candidates.abstract: Existing selective sweet pepper harvesting systems use industrial arms and high-performance computers, which limits adoption on small farms and replication by researchers. We developed a low-cost, open-source modular harvesting robot based on Raspberry Pi 5 and a 3D-printed manipulator. The system has three modules. First, an improved YOLOv13n detector combines GhostConv, ReLU6, and DIoU Loss. It reaches 96.9% mAP@0.5 for fruits and 95.1% for peduncles with 2.35 M parameters. Compared with the YOLOv13n baseline, parameters and GFLOPs drop by 4.1% and 3.2%, while overall mAP@0.5 falls by 1.8 percentage points. Second, an adaptive size measurement and multi-criteria decision strategy uses the correlation between median depth and tilt angle (R2 = 0.824), giving a mean absolute error of 5.0 mm and a 95.4% effective hit rate. Third, a ROS 2-based full-stack platform enables closed-loop perception–decision–execution. Laboratory tests give a selected-target harvesting success rate of 95.4% (103/108) and an overall success rate of 85.8% (103/120), with 1.9% fruit damage. Motion planning and execution consume 83% of cycle time. All hardware designs, ROS 2 packages, and model weights are released.

candidates.title: PoET²S: Folding a digital twin into validator selection for blockchain consensus in peer-to-peer energy trading
candidates.abstract: Blockchain platforms for peer-to-peer energy trading often add a digital twin that forecasts each meter's generation and demand. In most designs the twin only raises alarms, while validators are still chosen by stake or computation. The proposed scheme, PoET²S, incorporates the twin's evidence into validator selection: a node's weight is a stake-and-energy term multiplied by its Twin-Trust Score raised to γ = 2.5, so nodes that contradict the physical forecast quickly lose committee seats. A discrete-event simulator compares PoET²S (500 nodes, 15% Byzantine, 30 paired seeds) with seven classical baselines and three design points from recent work: a binary veto, an additive energy-and-trust score, and a linear (γ = 1) reputation weight. Detection is a near-tie: PoET²S catches 91.0% of attackers and the veto 91.7%. PoET²S raises more false alarms per catch by default (13.9 against 9.7) but matches the veto's catch rate at equal false-alarm cost. The malicious committee share is 10.8% under the veto, 3.8% under the linear weight, and 2.6% under PoET²S, and on 100 seeds the gain over the linear weight is 37% (Holm-adjusted p = 7.2 × 10⁻⁹). At 45% Byzantine nodes, the one-third fault bound fails in 64.4% of veto blocks and 2.4% of PoET²S blocks. Simulated commit latency (30.2 ms) is higher than for Proof of Stake and Delegated Proof of Stake, lower than for Practical Byzantine Fault Tolerance, and flat up to 4,000 nodes; an optional fast path lowers it to 26.8 ms. Against Sybil attacks, top-K selection needs certified meter identities.

candidates.title: Wellness Robots and the Path to Full Autonomy
candidates.abstract: This paper introduces the autonomous wellness robot as a distinct category of socially assistive system, defined by its capacity to continuously assess and respond across the seven ICAA dimensions of wellness (see Figure 2). We propose the Care Robot Autonomy Scale (CRAS): a six-level taxonomy (L0-L5) modeled on the automotive automation standard SAE J3016 and evaluated across four wellness-aligned dimensions. We present Ryan, developed initially at the University of Denver and commercialized by DreamFace Technologies, as a case study. NIH/NIA-funded longitudinal evidence (N = 18; 887 hours) shows statistically significant cognitive improvement (SLUMS +2.61, p = 0.015) and a clinically meaningful directional reduction in depressive symptoms (PHQ-9 -2.50, p = 0.073), with no novelty effect. We position Ryan today at CRAS Level 1-2, with emerging Level 3 capabilities in some dimensions, and outline a three-phase roadmap to L5 (full autonomy) by the early 2030s.

candidates.title: Construction of Adolescent Self-Identity in K-Pop Artist Roleplay: A Phenomenological Study of NCT Dream Premium Roleplayer Account Users on Telegram
candidates.abstract: Roleplayer activities provide adolescents with a space to explore and make sense of sexual identity through characters and relationships in digital spaces. In the NCT Dream Premium roleplayer community on Telegram, this process can be seen through the use of K-Pop idols as face claims and BxB (Boy x Boy) shipping practices. This study aims to understand the construction of adolescent sexual identity through experiences of engaging in roleplayer activities using NCT Dream face claims on Telegram Premium. Using a qualitative approach and Interpretative Phenomenological Analysis (IPA), data were collected through in-depth interviews with six informants and analyzed using open coding, axial coding, and selective coding. Stuart Hall identity construction theory served as the primary theoretical foundation, supported by Jenkins’ fandom concept and Boyd affordance concept. The findings show that sexual identity is constructed through creating spaces and characters, self-expression, relationships and safety, and reflection on sexual identity. It is shaped by experiences and interactions within the roleplayer community rather than by the face claim itself.
