candidates.title: Artificial Intelligence and Media: Assessing the Risks and Rewards
candidates.abstract: Exploring how artifical intelligence (AI) technologies— from generative AI (GenAI) to robotics—are reshaping the media landscape, this groundbreaking text critically examines the nature of AI and its impact on journalism, media, and society. In this timely analysis, John V. Pavlik explores the opportunities and challenges of AI integration across the media landscape, from newsrooms to entertainment platforms, offering critical insights into how AI technologies are reshaping content creation, distribution, and public engagement. The book provides readers with a clear and comprehensive understanding of AI's transformative impact on media by offering accessible explanations of complex AI concepts and applications, evidence-based analysis of current AI implementations in journalism and entertainment, a critical examination of ethical challenges and regulatory frameworks, and practical insights into GenAI, robotics, and emerging media technologies. Featuring case studies and real-world examples from across journalism, film and television, social media, and beyond, the book offers invaluable insight into the practical application of AI technologies and an overall understanding of the risks and rewards surrounding AI-driven media. This book will be essential reading for students and scholars of media, journalism, and communication studies, as well as media professionals seeking to understand AI's impact on their field. It also offers crucial insights for policymakers involved in media regulation and AI governance.

candidates.title: RoboARCade: Benchmarking Agentic Robot Control
candidates.abstract: Improvements in multi-modal capabilities have enabled agents to act directly as robot policies, a setting we refer to as agentic robot control (ARC). We introduce RoboARCade, a benchmark of long-horizon manipulation tasks across three embodiments designed to test in-context adaptation, memory, and reasoning for precise control. The tasks build on existing open-source benchmarks, which we make harder by widening the range of initial conditions. RoboARCade is easy to use and extend: all tasks run on a single simulation backend, MuJoCo, each task is a self-contained data pack, and agents connect through interchangeable interfaces, so new tasks, agents, and interfaces can be added independently. The benchmark separates leading agents: GPT-6 Astra achieves 49.8% compared with 43.6% for Claude Fable 5.1, leaving substantial room for improvement. Comparing two interfaces, we find that a richer visual interface adds only 1.5 to 6.8 points at 1.7 to 2.3 times the cost. Failures stem mostly from choosing a poor manipulation strategy or executing a good one imprecisely, rarely from misunderstanding the scene, and agents incorrectly claim success on 24% to 39% of attempted subtasks. Agents can also improve without human input: one successful demonstration in context raises Astra's score from 53.5% to 73.0% on a five-task subset, and a prompt the agent writes and revises itself reaches 72.0%. Code, videos and full traces are available at roboarcade.org.

candidates.title: Selective attention or inattention? Enabling efficient perception in embodied intelligence agents
candidates.abstract: Abstract As embodied intelligence increasingly operates in the physical world, perception efficiency, robustness, and adaptability become central bottlenecks separating artificial agents from biological organisms. Unlike conventional perception pipelines, biological perception is inherently selective and resource-aware: attention amplifies task-relevant information, while inattention suppresses distraction and redundancy. This survey investigates attention-driven adaptive perception as a promising mechanism for improving embodied systems. We consolidate interdisciplinary findings from neuroscience, cognitive science, robotics, and machine learning to clarify the distinct yet complementary roles of selective attention and inattention in optimizing perceptual processing. Building on these insights, we introduce the Unified Selective Attention and Inattention Model (U-SAIM) and extend it into a three-tier architectural framework that maps biological principles to embodied perception systems. Guided by this structure, we review existing implementations across robotics, multimodal fusion, lightweight perception, and attention modulation strategies, extracting design patterns and performance implications. Moreover, we discuss the challenges and opportunities for future development. Together, these perspectives chart a unified theoretical and practical roadmap toward attentional embodied perception—agents capable of perceiving, reasoning, and acting with the adaptive intelligence, efficiency, and flexibility that define human perception.

candidates.title: Leave It Better Than Found: Value-Guided Cooperation in Sequential Tasks
candidates.abstract: We consider the problem of sequential task continuation, where one robot acts in a workspace that has been affected by a previous robot. Current approaches in multi-robot cooperation rely heavily on co-training or co-optimization, assumingthat the robots have access to collective interaction data during the policy training or planning process. However, as increasingly varied robotic embodiments and policies are deployed and operate in the same real-world environment, learning policies for cooperation becomes infeasible due to the combinatorial explosion of possible robot combinations that need to be accounted for. To address this challenge, this paper considers the problem of ad hoc sequential cooperation between robots that have never before operated together in a shared environment. We demonstrate that robots can explicitly communicate their environmental preferences through sharing their value functions, enabling coordination without the need for prior joint training. To ground this exchange and prevent overconfidence in out-of-distribution states, we further introduce a k-nearest neighbors (KNN)- based uncertainty filter. Our method yields an increase of up to 48.5 pp compared with naive or even selfish agents, in task success rates across simulated and real-world experiments, demonstrating that value function transmission between agents is useful not merely as an internal learning tool, but as an effective basis for ad hoc coordination. Website: https://proroklab.github.io/PAVE/

candidates.title: A STATEWIDE EVALUATION OF LOW-VALUE IBC USAGE AND ITS IMPLICATIONS FOR CTE PROGRAMMING
candidates.abstract: Industry-Based Certifications (IBCs) have emerged as a significant element of the Career and Technical Education (CTE) accountability models for Texas high schools, especially within the College, Career, and Military Readiness (CCMR) framework. Nevertheless, concerns have grown about the labor-market worth, equity considerations, and accountability use of low-value certifications. In this study, the patterns of IBC use across the state were evaluated and their associations with CTE programming, accountability policy, and student readiness indicators were examined. The study was based on the Improvement Science framework; it had a quantitative descriptive and longitudinal research design that was conducted with analysis conducted in JASP and Python. The dataset was a combination of statewide IBC master records, district accountability datasets, CCMR indicators, regional certification counts, and program-level workforce pathway data from 2022-2025. The results showed that the value of approved certifications is unevenly distributed across the statewide IBC list. Among the 474 current certifications on the 2025–2030 accountability list, Tier 1 credentials, those most strongly aligned with high-wage, high demand occupations constituted only 4.9% (n = 23), while Tier 2 credentials dominated at 73.6% (n = 349) and Tier 3 accounted for 21.5% (n = 102). A chi-square goodness-of-fit test confirmed that this distribution departs significantly from uniformity, χ² (2, N = 474) = 2 366.09, p < .001, indicating constrained access to the most valuable credentials. Analysis of multi-cycle list data showed that certification sunsetting is a recurring feature of the system: comparable cohorts of roughly 60 certifications were phased out at successive cycle transitions, while the approved list expanded substantially across cycles, from 207 certifications (2019-2022) to 294 (2022-2024) to 474 (2025-2030). Persistent demographic inequalities were also evident. Non-economically disadvantaged students significantly outperformed economically disadvantaged students within the same districts (mean gap = .164, t(921) = 36.40, p < .001, Cohen’s dₖ = 1.20, a very large effect, and special education students performed lowest of all (dₖ = 1.52 relative to economically disadvantaged peers). Regional variation was also significant, F(19, 999) = 3.64, p < .001, η² = .065. A composite equity-adjusted index and a Pareto decomposition across the 20 regions showed that regional standing reorders substantially once the evenness of readiness is weighed alongside its level, and that each region’s readiness shortfall concentrates in roughly three student groups. A pathway-substitution analysis further showed that the college-ready route dominates for every student group in every region and that access to the certification pathway is lowest for the same groups that trail on college readiness. Although the study originated as an examination of credential value, equity in access to readiness pathways emerged as its most significant system-level concern: the subgroup disparities were the largest and most statistically robust effects observed and were stable across cohorts. Taken together, the findings indicate that Texas CTE accountability systems may benefit from weighing credential value and equitable access alongside certification counts rather than treating all certifications as equivalent. Consistent with the study’s diagnostic, non-causal design, these results are interpreted as system-level patterns rather than demonstrated causal effects. Policy implications to consider include refining IBC tiering, monitoring subgroup access to high-value pathways, and supporting districts through 3 accountability transitions.

candidates.title: Para-authenticity, ontological flexibility, and ontological detachment: how creatives construct and manage virtual endorsers
candidates.abstract: Research on virtual endorsers has largely focused on consumers, leaving the creative strategies behind their development underexplored. This study examines how creatives construct and manage the authenticity of virtual influencers and brand ambassadors while navigating an evolving ethical landscape. Based on in-depth interviews with eleven practitioners, our findings suggest they deliberately construct virtual personas plausibly situated in recognizable social and material worlds despite their artificiality. To manage the tension between brand control and perceived relatability, practitioners integrate imperfections and contextual cues to evoke para-authenticity – a strategic illusion of plausibility. We also explore the business case for virtual endorsers and how practitioners navigate ethical complexities through strategic disclosure, ontological flexibility (the capacity to vary an endorser’s form), and ontological detachment (the ethically ambivalent use of such flexibility to move beyond human embodiment and its associated demographic categories). Overall, this study reframes authenticity as a strategic construction in a synthetic advertising landscape.

candidates.title: Robots in the City: Persona-Based Perceptions of Urban Robots
candidates.abstract: Pedestrians increasingly encounter robots in urban public spaces without interacting with them, but how robots change the perceived safety of a street remains unclear. We examine how robot presence and type affect perceived safety across urban contexts. We generate 18 images of Seoul streets that vary in time of day, road class, and robot condition (no robot, a delivery robot, or a humanoid). Two multimodal large language models (MLLMs), Qwen3.8-27B and Gemma4-26B, each conditioned on 500 synthetic personas, choose the safer image in each pair, and 25 human respondents complete the same task. Both models prefer streets without robots and favor the delivery robot over the humanoid. Robots are chosen more often at night and less often by older personas, whereas road class has smaller effects. In the model rationales, the delivery robot appears as a physical obstacle, whereas the humanoid appears as either a threat or a source of protection. Like humans, both models chose robots more often at night, but chose the humanoid over the delivery robot far less often, and Gemma showed a night effect for the humanoid about three times that of humans. These results show that the effect of a robot on perceived safety depends on when it appears, and that persona-conditioned MLLMs capture only part of human judgments.

candidates.title: For You, Not for Everyone: Bystander-Aware Delivery of Critical Feedback in Robot Tutoring
candidates.abstract: Robots in shared settings may expose information intended for an individual user to nearby bystanders. Robot tutoring makes this concern particularly salient: critical feedback is directed at an individual learner, yet bystanders may overhear or see it. To address this, we compared context-invariant and context-adaptive robot behaviors in a between-subjects study with 40 participants. Following an initial phase without a bystander, a bystander entered the setting. Participants then received two scripted critical feedback messages concerning their pronunciation and handwriting, independent of their actual performance. With the context-invariant behavior, the robot tutor delivered both messages aloud. With the context-adaptive behavior, the robot tutor scanned for the bystander, turned its body and display away after detecting them, gave a spoken attention cue, and presented the same feedback messages silently on its display. Participants rated the robot tutor higher in perceived privacy awareness and perceived social competence in the context-adaptive condition than in the context-invariant condition, while evidence for reduced experienced embarrassment was inconclusive. These findings inform the design and evaluation of robots that respond to bystander presence by adapting how they communicate potentially sensitive information.

candidates.title: LLMs as MDP Designers: A Dependency-Aware Agentic Framework for Automated Robot Policy Generation
candidates.abstract: We investigate the automated generation of executable robot reinforcement learning (RL) policies from natural-language task descriptions. Rather than using large language models (LLMs) as execution-time decision makers, we use them as designers that construct RL pipelines before deployment, including Markov decision process (MDP) formulation and simulator implementation. We identify a phase-wise structure in this problem: MDP formulation is dependency-structured and sequential, whereas simulator implementation becomes modular once the formulation is fixed. Based on this structure, we propose ARPG, a dependency-aware agentic framework that performs sequential MDP modeling, localized verification and correction, and simulator-structured implementation while externalizing intermediate artifacts. ARPG targets a key failure mode of automated policy generation: executable code may still yield non-learnable policies when state, action, reward, and termination artifacts are not semantically aligned. Experiments in Isaac Sim show that ARPG improves modeling correctness, environment executability, and policy-generation success compared with monolithic LLM baselines and off-the-shelf agentic systems. Additional demonstrations on custom robotics, standard RL, and engineering-domain MDPs further suggest that the same modeling pipeline can be reused beyond the main benchmark suite.

candidates.title: Smart Robotic Inspection of Levees and Culverts: A Scoping Review of Robotic Platforms, Sensing Technologies, AI Methods, and Multi-Robot Coordination for Flood-Control Infrastructure
candidates.abstract: Abstract Earthen levees, dikes, flood-control embankments, culverts, and stormwater drainage conduits represent vital lifelines for mitigating catastrophic inun-dation in urban and rural watersheds. However, conventional manual walk-downs and tethered closed-circuit television (CCTV) surveys remain severely labor-intensive, hazardous, subjective, and difficult to scale across vegetated, flooded, submerged, and GPS-denied environments. Autonomous robotics, multimodal remote sensing, deep-learning-based computer vision, and multi-robot coordination offer transformative opportunities to enhance inspection frequency, spatial accuracy, and maintenance decision-making. Following the Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) methodology and the PRISMA extension for Scoping Reviews (PRISMA-ScR), this study maps the multidisciplinary land-scape across six major scholarly databases: Scopus, Web of Science, IEEE Xplore, ScienceDirect, SpringerLink, and Google Scholar (2010–2026). Out of 1,860 initially retrieved records, 1,314 unique studies were screened, 212 full texts were assessed, and 64 primary empirical studies were systemati-cally synthesized. We chart the evidence across seven interconnected the-matic streams: (1) unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) corridor surveying; (2) unmanned ground vehicles (UGVs) and pipe crawlers; (3) amphibious and autonomous underwater vehicles (AUVs/ROVs); (4) multimodal sensor fusion (RGB, thermal infrared, LiDAR, sonar, and GPR); (5) deep learning for defect detection and semantic segmentation; (6) degraded-environment SLAM and GPS-denied navigation; and (7) multi-robot coordination, com-munication relays, and digital-twin maintenance integration. Quantitative findings show that while aerial thermal/RGB levee inspection and in-pipe YOLO/U-Net defect detection achieve high localized accuracy (mAP ex-ceeding 75–86%, segmentation IoU > 0.71), end-to-end systems integration remains scarce. Only 10.9% (n = 7) of the literature validates heterogeneous multi-domain robot teams in operational flood-control environments, and fewer than 5% close the loop from automated anomaly detection to predic-tive maintenance prioritization. To bridge these gaps, we propose a resilient six-tier reference architecture for communication-aware, heterogeneous robot teams and establish a concrete ten-point research agenda for operational flood-control infrastructure management.

candidates.title: Exploring Proximity and Tactile Sensing for Robotic Manipulation
candidates.abstract: Pre-touch sensing, or sensing information about an object before contact, is an attractive modality for robot hands as it can allow a robot to anticipate and respond to a contact before it happens. In this work, we introduce ToFTouch, a multimodal tactile sensor combining three multizone (4$\times$4 resolution) time-of-flight sensors with an optics-based pressure sensing array. We mount this sensor on a parallel jaw gripper and demonstrate its utility on three distinct tasks: (i) pre-grasp adjustment, (ii) item extraction from clutter, and (iii) item insertion into tight spaces. For pre-grasp adjustment, ToF feedback reduced cycle time by 7.4$\%$ by enabling anticipatory gripper closure during approach. For extraction, ToF sensing enabled successful retrieval across all tested depth offsets ($\pm$2 cm) deviating from the nominal pick point, including conditions where baseline approaches failed, with standard deviations below 0.4 cm. For insertion into dense clutter, we explore the proximity and tactile information provided from ToFTouch during an insertion trajectory. The results demonstrate the utility of multizone ToF sensing in a manipulation environment.

candidates.title: Religious Conflict and Coexistence in Korea
candidates.abstract: This Reprint brings together a set of essays that examine the question of religious conflict and coexistence in the Korean context. Using a range of disciplinary perspectives, the contributions offer fresh insights into both longstanding and emerging issues in the study of religion, including shamanic rituals and cosmologies, ecumenical engagement, interreligious dialogue, the dynamics of religion and politics, religious art, Confucian ritual and its interpretation, and the religious dimensions of space and time. Despite their thematic and methodological diversity, the essays share a common concern with how religion in Korea, both historical and contemporary, responds to changing and often challenging conditions. These responses take multiple forms: epistemological and behavioral adjustments, the development of new institutional and ritual configurations, the articulation of idealized values through aesthetic media, and the reconfiguration of spatial meanings. Taken together, the volume highlights the creativity and vitality of religious traditions in Korea as they engage an evolving social and cultural milieu.

candidates.title: Digital Technology and Artistic Interventions for Rural Revitalization in China
candidates.abstract: China’s rapid urbanization continues to exert structural pressures on agriculture, rural communities, and farmers. The practice of artistic intervention in rural communities – yishu xiangjian – has shifted since the mid-2000s from avant-garde experiments to a nationwide multistakeholder movement. Under the Digital China initiative, this movement now encompasses blockchain-traced ancient tea forests, algorithmically enhanced village football tournaments, and points-based governance platforms, among others. This chapter examines three empirically grounded pathways through which digital technologies mediate rural cultural practice: the digital preservation of intangible heritage, integrated urban–rural cultural tourism scenarios, and digitally enabled governance for civilized rural customs. Our analysis suggests that technological empowerment reconfigures community relationships and advances institutional adaptation toward esthetic governance, but simultaneously subjects rural agency to platform metrics, algorithmic visibility, and financialized assetization. China’s experience offers a Global South model of postagricultural civilization that integrates ecological concerns, vernacular creativity, and community governance with advanced digital infrastructure; however, its sustainability depends on negotiating the tension between flexible connectivity and digital sovereignty. Technology functions not only as an instrumental tool but also as a contested mediator connecting locality with globality, cultural inheritance with modernization, and rural subjects with expanded yet uneven horizons of participatory cultural practice.

candidates.title: Fit4MedRob: Design and Preliminary Validation of a Modular Robotic Framework for Hemispatial Inattention Rehabilitation
candidates.abstract: The Fit4MedRob initiative (“Fit for Medical Robotics”) is a large-scale project funded by the Italian Ministry of University and Research under the Italian Complementary National Plan, involving 25 partners across academia, clinical centers, and industry. Within this framework, Mission 2 – Activity 5 (Match-Making #53) focuses on the development of robotic solutions for the rehabilitation of post-stroke hemispatial inattention (HI), a condition characterized by impaired awareness of one side of space. This work presents the design and preliminary validation of a modular robotic framework based on the TIAGo platform, a collaborative mobile manipulator developed by PAL Robotics. The proposed architecture integrates six functional modules: Navigation, Patient Identification, Patient Interaction, Patient Monitoring, Exercise Delivery, and Evaluation. The system is designed to support structured rehabilitation sessions while enabling the acquisition of quantitative sensor-based measurements. Preliminary validation was conducted with healthy participants under controlled conditions and focused on selected technological components of the framework, including autonomous navigation, patient identification, speech-based interaction, markerless head-orientation estimation, and upper-limb motion tracking. Ground-truth kinematic measurements were obtained using a stereophotogrammetric system where applicable. Navigation enabled the robot to establish an interaction configuration compatible with subsequent identification, although systematic differences were observed between onboard and reference estimates of subject distance and alignment. Patient identification was successfully achieved within the intended interaction range, while the speech-based interaction module reached an overall intent-classification accuracy of 92.6%. Markerless head-orientation estimation showed high agreement with the reference system for yaw, whereas larger errors were observed for pitch. Upper-limb tracking captured the main spatial and temporal characteristics of robot-guided movements, although angular alignment showed greater variability.

candidates.title: Humanness Inversion in AI Care Discourse: Humanising Robots and Erasing Care Workers in South Korean News Media
candidates.abstract: ABSTRACT Existing studies have examined AI eldercare, anthropomorphic care technologies, and the devaluation of feminised care labour. Yet little is known about how public discourse humanises machines while rendering human care workers less visible. To fill this gap, this study examines how AI care robots are represented in South Korean news media and how these representations position human care workers. Drawing on critical discourse analysis of 75 articles selected from a corpus of 2077 Korean‐language news articles published in 2025, the study identifies a recurring discursive mechanism, which I call humanness inversion. The findings of this study suggest that AI care robots are endowed with the qualities conventionally associated with human care of warmth, companionship, vigilance, filial obligation, and moral responsibility, while human care workers are rendered absent, inefficient, or replaceable. This inversion operates through three dominant patterns of relational inversion, efficiency inversion, and heroic inversion, alongside a minority counter‐discourse that seeks to reclaim the relational and labour‐intensive dimensions of care. The study contributes to theories of dehumanisation, care work, and AI discourse by showing that humanness is not only denied to marginalised workers but can also be publicly transferred to non‐human actors. The results of this study also highlight the need for organisations, policymakers, and journalists to frame AI care technologies as supports for human care rather than substitutes.

candidates.title: Closer, Not Just More Credible: How Parasocial Interaction Explains Consumer Responses to Virtual and Human Influencers
candidates.abstract: concentrated on Europe, Asia Pacific and North America [12], and responses to VIs depend on the cultural setting [13].To address these questions, this study compares VIs and HIs on trustworthiness, expertise, attractiveness and authenticity among Lithuanian consumers.It tests two routes to purchase intention (PI): a credibility route, through which source characteristics make the message believable (message credibility, MC), and a relational route through PSI.The study extends source credibility research on VIs with a relational explanation and gives brands evidence for choosing between the two influencer types.The remainder of the paper is structured as follows.Section 2 reviews the literature and develops the hypotheses, Section 3 describes the method, Section 4 discusses the findings and their implications, and Section 5 concludes.

candidates.title: Designing Immersive Learning Experiences: Teaching Robotics Programming in Virtual 3D Environments
candidates.abstract: This article presents a teaching scenario using virtual environments, often referred to as part of the ‘metaverse’, to address educational challenges highlighted during the COVID-19 pandemic. The increasing shift to online learning environments emphasizes the need for flexible, anytime-anywhere access to education. Virtual 3D environments offer a level of immersion that surpasses traditional online formats, such as video conferencing, and enable innovative didactic concepts, including collaborative group activities. To illustrate these benefits, we showcase a case study involving the simulation of robot programming within a virtual 3D environment. Additionally, the integration of personal assistants, such as conversational or pedagogical agents, is explored as a means to alleviate teachers' workloads. Advances in artificial intelligence have made natural language interactions with these agents highly effective, further enhancing the potential of virtual 3D environments in educational contexts. Keywords: e-learning, e-teaching, immersion, virtual 3D rooms, gamification, cyber-physical systems

candidates.title: Present Drawing: Exploring Avatar-Mediated Drawing Events with Physical Traces
candidates.abstract: We introduce Present Drawing, an approach for staging an avatar-mediated drawing event that leaves physical traces in the real world. Present Drawing aims to reconfigure conventional drawing events by relaxing their physical constraints. We describe an organizer-oriented design space for such an event along four elements: Time, Site, Control Source, and Avatar Embodiment. To ground this concept, we developed a proof-of-concept prototype in which an observer wears a head-mounted display to view an avatar. The avatar’s motion is synchronized with a customized pen plotter whose mechanical parts are hidden from the observer. We also developed five application examples spanning live, playback, multi-site, mascot, and system-controlled configurations. We conducted an initial evaluation of one representative playback autograph configuration, showing the basic plausibility of the core Present Drawing experience as an avatar-mediated drawing event and highlighting factors associated with perceiving the avatar as the drawer.

candidates.title: Revisiting the Uncanny Valley in the AI Era: A Review of Visual Artifacts and Aesthetic Perceptions in AI-Generated Characters
candidates.abstract: The rapid evolution of generative artificial intelligence (AI), particularly diffusion-based image synthesis models, has fundamentally transformed digital character design and visual storytelling. However, the frequent occurrence of "visual artifacts"—such as anatomical distortions, unnatural skin smoothness, rigid facial expressions, and latent space blending—presents significant aesthetic and psychological challenges. This paper provides a critical, multidisciplinary review that re-examines the classic "Uncanny Valley" hypothesis within the contemporary context of AI-generated media. Moving beyond the conventional engineering perspective that views these artifacts merely as technical deficiencies to be eliminated, this study investigates their potential reinterpretation through the lenses of post-digital media art, glitch aesthetics, and visual semiotics. We analyze how audience perception, cognitive friction, and emotional engagement are affected by these synthetic cues. Furthermore, we explore how human designers utilize advanced node-based control frameworks (e.g., ComfyUI, ControlNet) to negotiate, fix, or intentionally embrace these algorithmic anomalies. Finally, we establish a conceptual framework for human-AI co-creation and highlight future research trajectories for character narrative design in generative media.

candidates.title: FabDreamer: Exploring the Image-to-Physical Workflow Through AI-Assisted Layered Fabrication
candidates.abstract: Generative AI lets anyone create rich visual content in seconds, yet translating that content into a physically fabricable artifact still demands manual decomposition, occlusion repair, and structural verification that most tools leave entirely to the user. We present FabDreamer, an image-to-physical system that carries an image to fabrication-ready SVGs through three stages with deliberately staged AI initiative: (1) AI leads decomposition into depth-ordered layers, (2) assists on demand during creative editing with real-time 3D preview, and (3) advises on structural integrity before export. We instantiate this workflow for layered laser-cut art and evaluate it through three rounds including a formative analysis, an early prototype user evaluation (N=13), and a cross-domain practitioner study with specialists from 6 fabrication domains (N=6). Our findings show that physical awareness during design opens creative opportunities beyond error prevention, that practitioners appropriate the system’s generic geometric operations for their own domains, and that the fabrication agent covers geometry-readable constraints while domain knowledge remains with the maker.

candidates.title: Reconstructing Cyber Literature Pedagogy in the Digital Literary Ecosystem of Society 5.0: A Three-Pillar Conceptual Framework
candidates.abstract: The rapid digital shift in Indonesia has transformed reading and writing practices from print-based methods to creative participation involving AI, multiple modes, and platforms. While this change has democratized access, it raises concerns about declining deep reading skills, shallow aesthetics, and uncritical reliance on generative technologies. This paper aims to (1) examine how cyber literature has evolved and fits within the Society 5.0 theoretical framework in today's digital ecosystems, (2) analyze how media changes affect aesthetic experience, reader agency, and literacy development, and (3) propose a human-centered approach to teaching literature. Methodologically, the study employs an interpretive and conceptual synthesis integrating digital humanities, multiliteracies, and posthuman authorship theory, drawing on recent scholarly literature from Indonesia and globally. Findings reveal that cyber literature has developed into four main types: web-based, social media-based, platform-based, and AI-augmented. Each is characterized by progressively hybrid authorship and algorithmically mediated participation, with distinct ways of knowing and engaging readers. Digital transformation significantly impacts multimodal aesthetics, social engagement patterns, and literacy practices, necessitating pedagogical change. In response, the study proposes a comprehensive three-pillar framework comprising deep reading, multimodal creation, and ethical AI literacy, emphasizing that literature education in the digital age must accommodate technological advancements while preserving human critical judgment, interpretive depth, and ethically informed creativity. Rekonstruksi Pedagogi Sastra Siber dalam Ekosistem Sastra Digital Masyarakat 5.0: Suatu Kerangka Konseptual Tiga Pilar Pergeseran digital yang cepat di Indonesia telah mengubah praktik membaca dan menulis dari metode berbasis cetak menjadi partisipasi kreatif yang melibatkan AI, berbagai mode, dan platform. Meskipun perubahan ini telah mendemokratisasi akses, hal ini menimbulkan kekhawatiran tentang menurunnya keterampilan membaca mendalam, estetika yang dangkal, dan ketergantungan yang tidak kritis pada teknologi generatif. Makalah ini bertujuan untuk (1) meneliti bagaimana sastra siber telah berevolusi dan sesuai dengan kerangka teoritis Masyarakat 5.0 dalam ekosistem digital saat ini, (2) menganalisis bagaimana perubahan media memengaruhi pengalaman estetika, agensi pembaca, dan pengembangan literasi, dan (3) mengusulkan pendekatan yang berpusat pada manusia untuk pengajaran sastra. Secara metodologis, penelitian ini menggunakan sintesis interpretatif dan konseptual yang mengintegrasikan humaniora digital, multiliterasi, dan teori kepengarangan pascamanusia, dengan mengacu pada literatur ilmiah terkini dari Indonesia dan global. Temuan menunjukkan bahwa sastra siber telah berkembang menjadi empat jenis utama: berbasis web, berbasis media sosial, berbasis platform, dan berbasis AI. Masing-masing dicirikan oleh kepengarangan hibrida yang progresif dan partisipasi yang dimediasi secara algoritmik, dengan cara yang berbeda dalam mengetahui dan melibatkan pembaca. Transformasi digital berdampak signifikan terhadap estetika multimodal, pola keterlibatan sosial, dan praktik literasi, sehingga memerlukan perubahan pedagogis. Sebagai respons, studi ini mengusulkan kerangka kerja komprehensif tiga pilar yang terdiri dari membaca mendalam, kreasi multimodal, dan literasi AI yang etis, menekankan bahwa pendidikan sastra di era digital harus mengakomodasi kemajuan teknologi sambil tetap melestarikan penilaian kritis manusia, kedalaman interpretasi, dan kreativitas yang berlandaskan etika.

candidates.title: GURU: A Hierarchical Neuro-Symbolic Multi-Agent System for Verification-Aware Automation of Mission-Critical Digital Engineering and Operations
candidates.abstract: An AI can find a safe action faster than any human, but it must never decide what counts as safe. We present GURU, a hierarchical neuro-symbolic multi-agent system for mission-critical digital engineering and operations, built on one partition of authority: learned models propose, rank, and accelerate; a symbolic rules engine checks every consequential action against hard limits before it executes; and validated physics confirms and decides. GURU runs a workflow as a closed control loop, with Navigation, Action, and Planning agents sharing one Common Internal Language and one training factory. Nuclear, aviation, and national-security guidance now requires this pattern; a harnessed language model keeps the model at the center, GURU puts a validated reference there. In computational fluid dynamics, the workflow raised the converged-simulation rate on unseen aircraft geometries from under 1 percent to 74 percent over 100 single-attempt cases, ran 54 live cases to Mach 6 on three facilities, and an ablation put the symbolic layer at 13 points of boundary-layer capture. Knowledge-graph retrieval and role adapters raised ParaView control success from 55 to 75 percent. In space domain awareness, where a language model cannot be trusted to decide, a frozen self-supervised world model under validated propagation scored highest of five methods at conjunction risk, including fully fine-tuned language models, with several-times-lower seed variance: the trustworthy design gives up nothing in accuracy, and the recipe transferred to reactor anomaly detection. A radar-to-avoidance debris pipeline was demonstrated in stages on a 2026 reentry; the hierarchy coordinates simulated teams of 200 aircraft. Training scaled near-linearly past 1,000 Aurora nodes and ran at 8,000. The approach extends to a control-grade microreactor digital twin with validated physics, not a learned model, as the safety basis.

candidates.title: Staged Gastrostomy Decompression, Total Parenteral-Enteral Nutritional Optimization, and Delayed Primary Thoracotomy Repair in a Late-Referred Term Neonate With Gross Type C Esophageal Atresia and Symmetric Intrauterine Growth Restriction: An Observationa
candidates.abstract: Background: Late referral of neonates with Gross type C esophageal atresia and distal tracheoesophageal fistula (EA/TEF) can be complicated by aspiration pneumonia and nutritional depletion. Objective: To describe physiological, nutritional, and surgical recovery in a late-referred term neonate with EA/TEF and reported symmetric intrauterine growth restriction. Methods: This longitudinal observational case study at Dr. M. Djamil General Hospital, Padang, Indonesia, covered inpatient and outpatient care from June 16 to August 11, 2025. Serial clinical, biochemical, and anthropometric measurements were described using percentage changes, oxygenation ratios, and growth velocity. The manuscript also reports Bradford Hill and Naranjo assessments; no within-patient inferential testing was performed. Results: A 7-day-old male neonate with a birth weight of 2,600 g presented with aspiration pneumonia, oxygen saturation of 88%, and weight loss to 2,200 g (15.38%). Stamm gastrostomy on hospital day 2, parenteral nutrition (84–110 kcal/kg/day), two albumin infusions (1.0 g/kg each), and trophic enteral feeding preceded weight recovery to 2,700 g. Thoracotomy, fistula ligation, and primary anastomosis were performed on day 17. Oral intake reached 280–320 mL/day by discharge on day 27, when weight was 2,955 g. Follow-up weight reached 3,700 g. Conclusion: This case describes recovery following staged decompression, nutritional support, and delayed repair. A single case cannot establish comparative safety, treatment efficacy, or causality.

candidates.title: Artificial Intelligence for Sustainable Development: A Structured Critical Review of Applications, Benefits, Risks and Governance Priorities
candidates.abstract: Abstract This structured critical literature review examines the multidimensional role of artificial intelligence (AI) in advancing global sustainability and supporting progress towards the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). Drawing on multidisciplinary academic and institutional literature, the review critically synthesises AI applications, sustainability benefits, implementation challenges and associated risks. Particular attention is given to applications in energy management, agriculture, environmental monitoring, smart cities, circular economy practices and industrial processes, alongside their potential contributions to resource efficiency, decarbonisation and environmental resilience. The analysis also considers the ecological footprint of AI technologies, including energy consumption, carbon emissions, water requirements and electronic waste, together with data-related, algorithmic, socioeconomic and ethical concerns. These interconnected challenges are examined through the concept of the AI Green Paradox and an exploratory multidimensional risk-prioritisation framework incorporating indicative likelihood and severity assessments. The review highlights the importance of distinguishing improvements in technological performance from independently demonstrated sustainability outcomes, particularly where evidence is limited by differences in research methodologies, geographical contexts and implementation conditions. Responsible governance, Green AI development, international cooperation, technological accessibility and capacity building are identified as important priorities for supporting sustainable and equitable AI implementation. Overall, the review argues that AI's contribution to sustainable development depends not only on its technological capabilities but also on the effective management of its environmental and societal consequences.

candidates.title: The Ethics of "Digital Resurrection”
candidates.abstract: In an age where technology blurs the boundary between memory and presence, the prospect of digital resurrection compels us to reconsider the meaning of identity, mortality, and moral responsibility. This paper aims to examine the ethical and philosophical implications of “digital resurrection,” which refers to the upcoming development and practice of using artificial intelligence to create interactive chatbots and holograms of deceased individuals using their digital footprints and other data. This raises ethical questions about the authenticity of recreations, which will be elaborated on using theories based on ethics of consent. This practice has turned AI into a mediator between the alive and dead. Immanuel Kant’s theory, which relies heavily on duty, autonomy, and human dignity, states that without explicit, informed, ante-mortem consent, the digital resurrection of an individual is completely unethical. Using the Information Philosophy, coined by Carl Öhman and Luciano Floridi as the “Digital Remains as Corpse” theory, we can discuss that digital footprints are not commercial assets but modern “digital remains” of the person. The study will investigate whether a deceased individual has the right to retain their privacy and digital autonomy. The paper will also draw upon Martin Heidegger, Karl Jaspers’ and Albert Camus’ existentialist theories like Being-towards-death, Boundary situations and The Absurd, which speak about concepts like the meaning of life, death, struggle, authenticity and individuality. Using the philosophical theory of Existentialism, we will analyse the way in which such AI avatars might change human relationship with life and loss. The paper will raise and analyze two important moral questions: Between data ownership and posthumous consent, who holds the moral authority to animate a person’s digital legacy? And does such “grief technology” aid people in dealing with loss, or entrap them in an absurd loop of never-ending grief, stripping away the meaning of life itself? Ultimately, the paper posits an urgent need of developing solid ethical structures to handle digital remains of those who have passed. While such AI technology could provide immediate comfort to those who mourn their loved ones, they are erasing the boundary between life and death, resulting in the commodification of memory and the loss of true existential healing. Keywords: Digital Resurrection, Digital Footprints, Ethical, Artificial Intelligence, Boundary Situations, The Absurd, Existentialism, Grief, Technology, Consent, Authenticity

candidates.title: MUSBRIC: LEGO-Compatible Pneumatic Muscle Bricks for Reconfigurable Musculoskeletal Robots
candidates.abstract: Musculoskeletal robots combine compliant actuators with articulated skeletons, but exploring alternative configurations often requires repeated fabrication. We present MUSBRIC, a modular hardware platform and accompanying MuJoCo-based simulator for reconfigurable musculoskeletal robots. LEGO-compatible endcaps turn fiber-reinforced extensile pneumatic artificial muscles into reusable, plug-and-play muscle bricks that connect directly to standard LEGO components. Experimentally identified actuator behavior supports corresponding musculoskeletal simulations. An elbow-joint prototype validates load-dependent flexion and extension, showing that pulley-guided routing enables reversible motion and a mechanical stop stabilizes the straight posture. A robotic hand demonstrates compliant grasping and multi-joint construction. Matched hardware and simulation sweeps across 15 leg configurations demonstrate systematic exploration of attachment geometry, while a quadruped assembled from four legs demonstrates walking. Together, these demonstrations span mechanism analysis, configuration exploration, and functional robot construction within a single reconfigurable system. The hardware designs and simulation code will be released as open source soon to facilitate reproduction and further development.

candidates.title: When "No Worries" Went Wrong: HRI Lessons for Foundation-Model Robots
candidates.abstract: When a person declined our robot's invitation to play, Alice turned her shoulder away and said "No worries, it's all good." Only after a brief pause did she drive off. The words and gestures were plausible but their order changed the message. In another episode, Alice informed a host that his visitor had arrived---while the visitor stood right beside him. Both came from a three-year ROS 2 HRI consortium that integrated large language and vision models as they emerged. Today's foundation models give robots broader capabilities to perceive their surroundings, reason about situations and generate behavior. Yet capability alone does not ensure that a changed situation shapes the action that reaches a person. Evidence may never be acquired, or a purpose or constraint may fail to survive planning and execution. A system may even report Success when an action no longer serves its intended purpose. Drawing on the consortium's engineering experience, we develop five design lessons about attention, knowledge, commitments, embodied timing and action authority. We then introduce TRACE, a lightweight review that changes one interaction premise, follows it to a decision or enforcement boundary, and produces an actionable architecture finding. A bounded analysis of a published LLM-generated behavior-tree system illustrates how an available clarification mechanism can go unused. The engineering lesson is to preserve accountability boundaries, not the computational pipelines that once exposed them.

candidates.title: Sign language teaching protocol with an interactive robotic arm and real-time vision feedback
candidates.abstract: BACKGROUND: Sign Language (SL) is essential for Deaf communities, yet limited SL proficiency sustains communication barriers in education and services. We propose an interactive tutoring system for Ecuadorian Sign Language (EcSL) that combines real-time, vision-based gesture assessment with an embodied "reward" delivered by a robotic arm, using fruit vocabulary as an initial learning domain. METHODS: We will conduct a two-arm randomized controlled experimental design, pretest-posttest control-group study with individual random assignment. About 70 university students without formal EcSL training will learn EcSL fruit signs through video and sign recognition feedback module. The system uses a webcam, MediaPipe landmark extraction, and a landmark-based fusion classifier that combines a local bidirectional LSTM with a transferred ST-GCN motion encoder; modules communicate via Robot Operating System (ROS). Outcomes. A total of six dependent variables will be assessed in both the experimental and control groups: (a) handshape, (b) palm orientation, (c) location, (d) movement, (e) non-manual signals and expressions, and (f) global coordination. Analyses will use descriptive statistics, reliability checks when applicable, and a mixed repeated-measures MANOVA. DISCUSSION: By coupling immediate feedback with embodied reinforcement, delivered through a robotic arm, the platform aims to support early sign accuracy and provide a motivating practice environment for learners. The robotic arm responds to participants' performance with physical rewards, thereby reinforcing correct execution through tangible, real-time stimuli. Results will guide improvements in robustness and inform extensions to broader vocabularies and deployment in educational contexts.

candidates.title: The Visual Arts, Technology, and Bodily Movements as Part of Cultural Trace-Making in the Preschool Atelier
candidates.abstract: This article explores children’s encounters with the visual arts, digital technology, and materialities in the preschool atelier. It is based on data from course assignments in a higher education programme for atelieristas in a Swedish Reggio Emilia inspired context. Analytically, the article examines how digital technologies, visual arts, and materialities participate in visual art encounters, and how bodily, material, and cultural trace-making emerge through the intra-actions (Barad, 2007) between children, artworks, and matter. The concept of cultural trace-making, as introduced by the author, is to be understood as the entangled process by which adults share culture with children, as well as the ways in which children, in turn, contribute to and reshape this culture. The findings demonstrate multiple ways of integrating the visual arts and digital technology into the preschool atelier, while highlighting how children contribute as cultural trace-makers within these practices.

candidates.title: Development of an intelligent IoT-based framework for boiler water quality monitoring and early warning using statistical process control and machine learning
candidates.abstract: ABSTRACT Boiler water quality directly influences the efficiency, reliability and service life of industrial steam generation systems, and inadequate monitoring can cause scaling, corrosion, reduced heat transfer efficiency and unplanned shutdowns. This study presents an intelligent Internet of Things (IoT)-based framework for continuous boiler water quality monitoring and early warning that integrates real-time sensing, statistical process control (SPC), rule-based decision support and machine learning. Six key parameters are monitored continuously: pH, conductivity, chloride concentration, hardness, dissolved oxygen and temperature. SPC performs real-time process monitoring, while a rule-based decision support system generates corrective recommendations from predefined operational limits. To validate the framework, nine supervised machine learning models were evaluated using representative operating scenarios; Random Forest and LightGBM achieved the highest classification performance, with 99.5% accuracy under 10-fold cross-validation. Correlation analysis showed strong positive relationships between conductivity and hardness (r = 0.73), conductivity and chloride (r = 0.70), and hardness and chloride (r = 0.72). Feature importance analysis identified temperature (31.9%), pH (27.9%) and hardness (18.1%) as the most influential variables. The framework enables continuous monitoring, rapid identification of abnormal boiler conditions and timely operational decision support, demonstrating proof-of-concept capability for further validation with long-term industrial boiler data.

candidates.title: Pretraining Knows What, Simulation Teaches How: Compositional Generalization for Agentic Robotics
candidates.abstract: Frontier models such as GPT-6 Astra now directly control robots and can generalize better than vision-language-action models (VLAs). We argue that this ability could arise from two distinct, composable skills: semantic reasoning, to understand what a task asks for in a scene, and motion control, to move the robot to do it. We show that small open VLMs are already capable of the first and mainly lack the second. We introduce Zero-real Agent Policy (ZAP), a recipe that teaches this missing motion skill, entirely in simulation on simple primitive tasks and from the model's own successes, with no frontier teacher or distillation and no real-world robot data. ZAP reaches 96.7% success on real-world tasks, matching GPT-6 Astra in our harness while running 3x faster and 17x cheaper, and 74.0% on a bimanual adaptation of RoboLab-120, on par with GPT-6 Astra's 72.2%. ZAP also generalizes to new objects, goals, and strategies, and in simulation to a robot embodiment on which it never trained.

candidates.title: Robots and wage inequality: evidence from individuals in China
candidates.abstract: Abstract This study examines the impact of industrial robot adoption on wage inequality and employment outcomes in China, which has the world’s largest robotics stock and fastest-growing adoption rate. Using data from the China Family Panel Studies and the International Federation of Robotics, we constructed a county-level robot exposure index and employed the two-stage least squares approach to address endogeneity. Our results show that robot adoption exacerbates wage polarisation in China. When faced with rising robot exposure, medium-skilled workers experience annual wage losses, while the wages of low-skilled and high-skilled workers are not significantly affected. Besides wage impact, we find occupational upgrading among past low-skilled workers and provide suggestive evidence of reduced labour-force participation among medium- and high-skilled workers. This pattern points to asymmetric labour-market adjustment across skill groups faced with robot exposure. We also examine how the wage estimates vary with trade exposure and demographic ageing. The trade interactions are consistent with a smaller annual-wage penalty for medium-skilled workers where intermediate-import exposure is greater. In counties with older populations, robot exposure is linked to a greater increase in hourly wages and a larger decline in hours worked. These findings highlight the need for targeted policies to mitigate wage inequality and support vulnerable groups during technological transformation.

candidates.title: SOCIOLINGUISTIC PECULIARITIES AND TECHNOLOGICAL CAPABILITIES OF VIRTUAL INFLUENCERS: ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE IN THE GENERATION OF LANGUAGE, BEHAVIOR, AND DIGITAL IDENTITIES
candidates.abstract: This study investigates the conditions under which AI-generated influencers attain social legitimacy within platform environments, with a specific focus on the empirical TikTok project called “Dundarev Family.” Drawing on the concept of simulacra, the research analyzes how synthetic characters establish credibility through language, humor, and culturally embedded communication, with particular attention to the role of platform-specific affordances in shaping audience perception. The research utilizes a mixed-methods design, incorporating the creation of five virtual personas representing the Dundarev family, experimental comparisons between human- authored and AI-generated texts, qualitative linguistic analysis of 951 user comments, and assessment of platform-based engagement metrics. The findings identify a central paradox: while AI exhibits limited ability to replicate culturally specific humor and dialectal nuance, the virtual characters nonetheless achieve high levels of user engagement, emotional response, and perceived closeness. Audience interaction is primarily affective and reactive, marked by predominantly emoji-based communication and minimal explicit recognition of the characters’ artificial nature. The study contends that social legitimacy in digital environments is not contingent upon linguistic authenticity, but rather emerges from the interplay of cultural recognizability, platform-specific communication practices, and affective engagement. AI influencers operate as hybrid entities rather than purely artificial ones, pointing to the increasing significance of human-AI collaboration in producing culturally resonant content and to a broader shift in how authenticity is constructed in algorithmically mediated environments.

candidates.title: Miao folk songs as a living musical practice in contemporary social contexts
candidates.abstract: This study examines Miao folk songs in Pengshui County, Chongqing Municipality, People’s Republic of China, as living musical practices whose meanings are shaped through contemporary social contexts. Employing a qualitative ethnomusicological approach, the research draws on fieldwork conducted between June 2025 and January 2026, including participant observation, audiovisual documentation, and semi-structured interviews with six purposively selected key informants comprising tradition bearers, experienced singers, and cultural practitioners. Data were analyzed inductively to explore the relationships among singing practices, performance contexts, modes of participation, and the roles of performers, audiences, and performance spaces. The findings reveal that Miao folk songs are practiced and transmitted across six principal contexts: traditional ritual ceremonies, agricultural labor and everyday life, communal gatherings and festivals, courtship and interpersonal communication, tourism-oriented performances, and digital and educational settings, each associated with distinct repertoires and organized modes of vocal practice. Four forms of musical practice are identified: spontaneous collective singing, ritual-prescribed performance, staged performance, and standardized pedagogical practice. Under contemporary conditions, these practices demonstrate a dynamic interplay of continuity and adaptation, characterized by shifts from community-internal spaces to public arenas, a reduced emphasis on improvisation in favor of fixed melodic and textual forms, and an expanded reliance on institutional and digital transmission. Conceptualizing Miao folk songs as musical practice thus extends analysis beyond musical structure toward a contextual understanding of how meaning is co-produced through participation, space, and time, offering a transferable framework for the study of ethnic folk music traditions in contemporary societies.

candidates.title: Robots in Nursing: A Qualitative Study of the Views of Nurses and Nurse Leaders
candidates.abstract: AIM: To explore the views of nurses and nurse leaders about the role of robots in hospital nursing care. DESIGN: This paper outlines two phases of a qualitative study exploring the role of robots in UK nursing over the next 10-15 years. METHODS: Twenty-five registered nurses and 12 nurse leaders took part in online focus groups during January and October 2022. Registered nurse data were analysed using the Fundamentals of Care framework to identify activities robots should assist with and those they should not. Reflective Thematic Analysis was then used to generate themes from both registered nurses' and nurse leaders' data. RESULTS: Registered nurses' level of agreement that robots can assist with activities within three nursing dimensions of physical, psychosocial and relational activity is presented in graphic form. In addition, registered nurses explored a fear of the future, the possibility of a negotiated reality and a positive opportunity to use robots. Nurse leaders discussed the essence of nursing, arguing for action: 'We have to do something' and to 'Reframe the future'. CONCLUSION: Nurses were more accepting of robotic assistance with physical tasks than with psychosocial or emotional support. Nurse leaders exhibited an appetite to lead the debate and reframe the narrative towards an assistive contribution. This study provides a foundation for further debate and offers insight to enable nursing to harness assistive technology. IMPLICATIONS FOR THE PROFESSION/PATIENT CARE: The study's findings expand the current literature on the acceptability of robots assisting nurses and offer insights that may underpin future discussions and considerations. IMPACT: The fundamentals of care framework considers nursing as a relational activity and therefore offers a broader perspective for discussing activities that robots may assist with. REPORTING METHOD: This study adheres to the SRQR EQUATOR guidelines for qualitative research. PATIENT OR PUBLIC CONTRIBUTION: Patients and members of the public were involved in study design, and their contributions influenced the planning stages.

candidates.title: Enabling Motion-Induced WiFi-CSI Sensing in Multi-Robot Systems: A Simulation Framework
candidates.abstract: WiFi Channel State Information (CSI) enables fine-grained sensing of spatial relationships between wireless devices. The WiFi Sensor for Robotics (WSR) toolbox demonstrated that WiFi-CSI measurements collected during robot motion, combined with odometry, can be used to synthesize virtual antenna arrays, enabling motion-induced bearing estimation in multi-robot experiments. However, deploying the WSR approach has remained challenging due to its limited integration with standard robotics tools and reliance on deprecated WiFi-CSI acquisition hardware. This work presents an open-source simulation framework that integrates the WSR sensing pipeline within the robotic simulator Gazebo. The framework generates synthetic WiFi-CSI measurements with realistic physical signal properties and leverages realistic robot motion required for motion-induced sensing and downstream localization. It further supports processing both simulated and real WiFi-CSI data for direct comparison and validation. Our aim is to make WSR-style sensing accessible as a modular sensing modality for robotic research. We validate our framework by comparing simulated and real-world experiments using TurtleBot3 robots, and demonstrate its use for bearing estimation and robot localization. This work lowers the barrier to entry for WiFi-CSI-based sensing in multi-robot systems and provides a foundation for integrating WiFi-CSI sensing with multi-modal perception for localization and coordination. All code and experimental details are publicly available at https://github.com/baharhaghighat/DARS_2026_Dijkstra_et_al

candidates.title: STEAM and educational robotics in the development of statistical literacy
candidates.abstract: In primary school, the teaching of mathematics and natural sciences should promote meaningful, context-based learning that enables students to apply knowledge in real-life situations. Interdisciplinary approaches such as STEAM foster 21st century competences through active and collaborative methodologies, while educational robotics (ER) supports the development of computational thinking and social skills. This study analyses the influence of a STEAM practice, incorporating ER on the development of statistical literacy and learning about ocean plastic pollution among 4th grade students. The research adopted a mixed-methods, interpretative action research design. Data were collected by the trainee teacher as participant researcher through performance tasks, field notes, photographs and audio recordings, later used to construct multimodal narratives. Findings reveal statistically significant improvements in global level of knowledge and global performance. The study concludes that steam practices incorporating ER and grounded in real-world problem-solving constitute an effective strategy for fostering statistical literacy.

candidates.title: Training-Free Inference-Budget Reduction in Flow-Matching Vision-Language-Action Models for Robot Manipulation: A Prespecified Evaluation Against a Fixed Task-Success Margin
candidates.abstract: Companion archive for the manuscript Training-Free Inference-Budget Reduction in Flow-Matching Vision-Language-Action Models for Robot Manipulation. It contains every closed-loop evaluation cell, latency and energy measurement, protocol document and analysis script behind the paper's tables. Contents. 722 eval_info.json closed-loop grids carrying per-episode outcomes and task identity; two-platform latency artifacts (NVIDIA GB10 and NVIDIA Jetson AGX Thor) with full hardware, protocol, thermal and GPU co-tenancy metadata; Thor board-energy measurements across four nvpmodel power modes; the prespecified non-inferiority protocol including its amendments; and the measurement harness. Reproducibility. Each latency record stores all 30 raw timings, thermal samples at the cell boundaries, peak device memory, a dtype census and a platform snapshot taken before and after the run. Per-run directories are kept alongside aggregates so a median-of-three can be re-derived rather than trusted. A SHA-256 manifest covers every file. Measurement bounds. Latency is timed on a dummy zero-input batch of the declared observation shapes; a paired real-observation check covering every configuration behind the three headline reductions is included, and agrees within 0.33 percentage points. Board energy is the largest single hwmon rail on the Thor module; that rail carries no label, so its identification as module input is an inference from magnitude. Ratios between settings are insensitive to that calibration while absolute joules are not. Energy figures are not idle-subtracted, and the GB10 exposes no comparable rail, so energy is reported for Thor only. Version 1.1.0 adds the second-platform latency study, board energy, a six-point pi0.5 latency curve verifying the affine cost model, the real-observation latency checks, and a task-identity clustered bootstrap sensitivity analysis declared before it was run. It also restores evaluation grids omitted from 1.0.0, including the co-primary confirmation behind Table 4 and the per-cell resolution study behind Table A7. Code is released under Apache-2.0; generated data and reports under CC BY 4.0. External assets are not mirrored; sources are listed in the manuscript's Data Availability Statement.

candidates.title: Open-source process simulation in DWSIM: A Biorefinery case study
candidates.abstract: Chemical process simulation supports chemical plant design by optimizing sustainability, yield, and economics, but commercial software costs can limit early-stage studies. This work demonstrates DWSIM, an open-source simulator with a graphical interface comparable to commercial platforms, through two lignocellulosic biorefinery case studies: (i) an ethanol organosolv process using rectification for solvent recovery and (ii) a γ-valerolactone (GVL) process using toluene liquid–liquid extraction and heteroazeotropic distillation of the water/GVL/toluene system. Both simulations used the NRTL model for flash calculations and were executed on a consumer-grade laptop. The designs process 100 t h -1 of corn stover into pulp, lignin, and dissolved sugars. Owing to milder extraction conditions (120 °C versus 190 °C), the GVL process recovered more lignin and dissolved sugars than the ethanol process (19.1 and 13.1 t h -1 versus 8.7 and 5.9 t h -1 ), with slightly lower pulp production (46.3 versus 50.7 t h -1 ). Its solvent-recovery sequence and lower solid-to-liquid ratio (1:4 versus 1:8.73) reduced energy demand by a factor of 3.2. Publicly available simulation and component files provide a reproducible baseline for open-source biorefinery research.

candidates.title: From AI boyfriends to AI shopping agents? The emerging convergence of relational AI and AI-assisted commerce
candidates.abstract: Abstract Generative artificial intelligence is becoming both relational and agentic. AI boyfriends are treated as a visible romantic exemplar within the broader theoretical and empirical domain of relational AI. This paper examines whether relational AI, including AI boyfriends, is emerging alongside AI-assisted commerce, and whether functional integration keeps pace with attention and market growth. Study 1 analyzes Google Trends data (2020–2026, six markets): relational-AI attention rises significantly in five countries, AI-commerce attention rises in all six, with substantial but non-invariant temporal co-movement in attention. Study 2 examines 44 AI-companion apps on Google Play: the category shows substantial downloads and spending, romantic positioning (e.g., AI boyfriends) shows no observable adoption penalty, in-app purchasing is universal, yet no app positions shopping as a core feature. Study 3 analyzes 181,226 Reddit posts from relational-AI communities: design-weighted coding estimates 9.1% of corpus posts contain commercial discourse, but only 0.3% involve the companion itself in consumer or purchasing decisions. We conceptualize this as an attention-market-integration gap, where attention and market realization outpace functional commerce integration. The study equips managers and researchers with guidance for engaging with the emerging AI boyfriend trend.

candidates.title: The impact of scenario-based simulation learning on clinical self-efficacy among pre-licensure nursing and midwifery students: A systematic review of design features and educational outcomes
candidates.abstract: AIM: To systematically review how scenario-based simulation learning (SBSL) shapes clinical self-efficacy among pre-licensure nursing and midwifery students and how simulation design, context and assessment timing influence educational and clinical translation. BACKGROUND: Scenario-based simulation learning (SBSL) is widely used in nursing and midwifery education, yet evidence on its effect on clinical self-efficacy and how simulation design moderate outcomes remains fragmented. DESIGN: A systematic review following PRISMA 2020 guidelines. METHODS: A PRISMA 2020-compliant review searched eight databases. Eligible studies measured task-specific clinical self-efficacy via validated tools in pre-licensure cohorts. Two reviewers independently screened records, extracted data on scenario complexity, theoretical integration, debriefing structure and outcome timing and appraised risk of bias. RESULTS: Fifty-two studies (N = 4774; 46 nursing, 6 midwifery) were included. SBSL broadly correlated with self-efficacy gains, yet only 55.8% (n = 29) demonstrated statistically significant between-group superiority. Psychomotor skill (54.1%), knowledge (61.9%) and cognitive reasoning (62.5%) improvements were documented. Studies embedding explicit theoretical frameworks, calibrated scenario difficulty ("Goldilocks Zone") and structured debriefing showed the most consistent benefits. Immediate post-simulation assessments were frequently distorted by acute simulation anxiety; self-efficacy crystallized only after cognitive consolidation. CONCLUSION: SBSL shows promise for building clinical self-efficacy, but effects are inconsistently captured and methodologically constrained by reliance on subjective self-report. Pedagogical architecture-progressive scaffolding, discipline-sensitive scenario design and rigorous debriefing-matters more than technical fidelity. Sustained efficacy requires longitudinal follow-up beyond immediate post-intervention windows. Faculty pedagogical preparedness, rather than equipment investment, is the decisive lever for translational impact. REGISTRATION: A Systematic Review.
