candidates.title: From Tabletop to Walking Bot: Deploying a VLA Model on a Legged Manipulator Robot
candidates.abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models are typically pretrained on broad, diverse datasets and subsequently fine-tuned on a comparatively small dataset tailored to a specific target robot. Such adaptation recipe is now widely established, achieving its most mature results on fixed-base arms due to their static base dynamics and consistent reference frame. Mounting the same arm on a quadruped extends the workspace to the entire floor, but fundamentally changes the embodiment: rather than controlling the arm in isolation, the policy must jointly coordinate base navigation, body posture, and end-effector motion. In this work, we study the practical demands of this embodiment change across data collection, model adaptation, and inference design to achieve closed-loop loco-manipulation on a Unitree Go2 with an AgileX Piper arm. We report the choices that made this real-robot deployment feasible, namely model variant, action horizon, and demonstration conventions, together with a study tailored to a pick-and-place task, separating data coverage from model capacity. We show that expanding demonstration coverage reduces held-out end-effector error by 30%, and incorporating secondary skills (such as pushing rather than grasping) introduces new behavioral modes without degrading baseline performance. Finally, closed-loop real-world experiments show how dataset composition shapes success and failure, validating the pipeline for more complex loco-manipulation.

candidates.title: An open-source platform for measuring optomotor responses in mice
candidates.abstract: The optomotor response (OMR) is a valuable behavioral index for assessing visual function in basic research; however, commercially available OMR evaluation equipment is expensive and lacks flexibility, as proprietary software and fixed hardware geometry restrict custom stimulus protocols and system modifications. Alternative low-cost, non-OMR methods often require extensive animal pre-training and are unsuitable for high-throughput studies. To overcome these limitations, we developed a low-cost, open-source OMR recording system for mice that lowers both financial and practical barriers, thereby facilitating widespread adoption across laboratories. Following a one-hour training session for evaluators, the system enabled precise quantification of visual acuity and assessment of contrast sensitivity in normal-sighted mice, detection of age-related visual decline, and evaluation of OMR extinction in retinitis pigmentosa model mice. This system facilitates accessible and efficient assessment of visual function in vision research.

candidates.title: The future of robotic artificial intelligence in acute care surgery: an early proving ground and a final frontier for autonomous surgical robotics
candidates.abstract: Acute care surgery (ACS), spanning emergency general surgery, trauma surgery, and surgical critical care, demands high-stakes decisions in settings characterized by hemodynamic instability, distorted anatomy, contamination, and time pressure. Artificial intelligence (AI) is proposed as a means to reduce cognitive burden, standardize technically sensitive tasks, and extend surgical capability in resource-constrained environments. This review examines the autonomy continuum in surgical AI, with ACS as the primary lens. We argue that ACS occupies a paradoxical position: it has produced the earliest preclinical demonstrations of autonomous surgical robotics, yet the very conditions that motivate autonomy in this specialty make it among the most challenging environments in which to deploy these systems safely in human patients. For ACS, the central question is less whether AI can perform surgical tasks than how autonomy should be sequenced and bounded for emergency surgery. We synthesize the literature across four domains: (1) how autonomy is defined and operationalized in surgical AI and robotics; (2) the current and emerging spectrum of automation in operative environments; (3) the technical feasibility of automation for ACS-relevant tasks; and (4) the ethical boundaries of autonomy in high-risk, time-critical cases. We argue that the safest course is incremental: deploying supervised task autonomy where safety properties are demonstrable and reserving higher autonomy for rigorously evaluated, tightly bounded domains. Realizing this course will require evaluation strategies that align autonomy level to clinical risk, preserve meaningful human oversight, support post-market monitoring, and address liability, patient trust, and equitable access.

candidates.title: Towards User Simulators That Stay On Task And Still Sound Natural
candidates.abstract: Users increasingly rely on AI systems for extended, multi-turn tasks, yet evidence indicates that LLM-based system performance degrades over prolonged interaction. To evaluate and improve AI assistants in such settings, we need user simulators that faithfully follow complex user intents while exhibiting realistic conversational behavior. Existing approaches manifest a trade-off: prompted assistants can follow complex user intents but lack behavioral fidelity, while specialized user simulators better approximate conversational behavior but struggle to remain faithful to complex intents. In this paper, we propose a reinforcement learning (RL) recipe that jointly rewards task intent adherence and behavioral naturalness. A crucial contribution of the method is operationalizing naturalness with a lightweight discriminator trained in an alternating, adversarial loop with the user simulator. We release the resulting model, UserLM-2.0, which produces valid simulated conversations (i.e., meeting both task-faithfulness and naturalness criteria) 46.2% of the time, over three times the rate of the strongest prior user simulator (14.1%).

candidates.title: From Bot-Farm to For-You-Page Fork: Consuming The Whole Digital Animal
candidates.abstract: In 2022, OpenAI launched the Large Language Model ChatGPT, and with it, the possibility of generative Artificial Intelligence (genAI) as a creative partner. Progress in the genAI arena has been rapid, with genAI created media going from uncanny horror show, to being able to create realistic media from a prompt. Social Media ‘for you page’ algorithms are now serving their users content created by genAI, including digital animals which may behave very unlike real animals do. The field of animal welfare science has utilised policy frameworks such as ‘Farm-to-Fork’ to conceptualise where harms and sustainability opportunities exist within the animal production system. In this work, we utilise three common ethical approaches to animal use, utilitarianism, deontological ethics, and the principle of telos, to explore the production and consumption of digital animals on social media. Using the example of an object animal (a toy), a digital animal (a genAI created cat), and an embodied animal (a real cat in a teaching programme), we explore the evidence for their effect on the human-animal relationship, and how various ethical frameworks would consider their consumption. We conclude with three recommendations for social media companies for incorporating digital animal media in their provisions. First, digital animal creation should be limited, with similar style guard-rails to creation of media containing humans. Second, digital animal media should be fully disclosed, to minimise risk of misinformation and norm creep. Third, as with content regarding ‘kid influencers’, ‘animal influencer’ content should be demonetised, to reduce the risk of exploitation.

candidates.title: From Automation to Decarbonization: The Role of Industrial Robots in Reducing Carbon Emission Intensity
candidates.abstract: In the era of Industry 4.0, industrial robots are being widely adopted across countries, revolutionizing production processes. However, their deployment comes with a trade-off: while enhancing efficiency, the production of industrial robots demands high energy consumption, posing new challenges to environmental sustainability. Despite its significance, the link between industrial robot penetration (RP) and carbon emission intensity (CMI) has received insufficient attention. This study systematically explores this relationship and finds that (1) a rise in RP significantly reduces CMI, with a 1% increase in RP leading to a 0.0265% decline in CMI; (2) this effect is primarily driven by RP’s role in fostering green technology innovation and optimizing the energy mix, with a stronger impact observed in economies with higher income inequality; (3) technology spillover effects between upstream and downstream industries further amplify CMI reduction; and (4) RP is particularly effective in mitigating CMI within capital-intensive manufacturing sectors. These findings underscore the need for policies that promote digital platform development and facilitate the integration of emerging technologies with capital-intensive industries, paving the way for a more sustainable and technologically advanced industrial landscape.

candidates.title: Guarding the Clinical Narrative: A Practitioner-Contributor's Retrospective Analysis of Open-Source Contributions to Clinical Natural Language Processing and Health-Data De-identification (2025-2026)
candidates.abstract: Background. Clinical natural language processing (NLP) software extracts structured facts from free-text notes. De-identification software removes protected health information (PHI) so that text can be shared for research. A missed name or a broken date pattern can expose a patient or corrupt a dataset. Much of this software is open source, and outside contributors write part of it. Purpose. This study describes what one practitioner-contributor did in this area, what got merged, what did not, and what the review process taught about working well with maintainers. Methods. The data source was the author's public pull request (PR) record on GitHub, extracted with the GitHub REST API on 21 October 2026 (search: author:rtmalikian, type:pr). The full record held 213 PRs across 94 repositories. This paper analyses the clinical NLP and de-identification subset: 15 PRs in 5 repositories. Each PR was classed as merged, open, or closed unmerged. Seven cases were selected for close reading for their privacy or language point, or for a hard review lesson. Results. Eight of the 15 subset PRs merged, which is 61.5% of the 13 resolved PRs. Five closed unmerged. Two remained open. Merged work included a fix for placeholder collisions in a de-identification function, Italian and Spanish PHI locale packs, a date-pattern fix in a French hospital NLP library, and a change that stopped PHI entering version control. The hardest case, a Spanish locale pack, survived a blocking review that found real damage in a follow-up commit. A fix-forward commit repaired it, and the PR merged the next day. Conclusions. The record points to a plain finding. PHI safety in this software rests on ordinary engineering habits: reproduction before repair, small scope, tests run before submission, and calm correction when a reviewer finds a fault. Language coverage is part of safety. De-identification that works only in English leaves other patients less protected.

candidates.title: A Modular Vision‐Based Robot for Efficient Noninvasive Inspection of External Pipeline Surfaces
candidates.abstract: ABSTRACT This paper presents a prototype of a modular autonomous robot aiming for the rapid inspection of steel pipelines, with a focus on detecting surface cracks. The robot incorporates a novel detachable mechanism, enabling full‐coverage inspection without requiring the robot to rotate completely around the pipe. This design not only simplifies attachment and detachment but also enhances operational flexibility. A 360° rotating scanner, integrated with a vision system featuring on‐device artificial intelligence inference, enables real‐time crack detection while maintaining consistent velocity. An automated crawler system ensures smooth linear movement along the pipeline, keeping a uniform distance from the surface. Additionally, a suspension system enables the wheels to adapt to irregularities of up to 25 mm, ensuring reliable performance on uneven surfaces. Experimental results showcased the robot's capabilities, achieving a 96.67% crack detection accuracy through on‐device inferencing and an enhanced 99.3% accuracy during post‐processing. However, certain limitations were observed, attributed to constraints within the microcontroller. Motion analysis confirmed that the scanner exhibited consistent motion during testing, completing 42 circumferential rotations along a 5‐m pipeline in an average time of 72.45 s, and completed a complete inspection of the pipeline in 50.43 min. While the modular robot was specifically designed and evaluated for straight pipelines with end couplings and was not intended to navigate couplings or bent sections, the system demonstrated stable and accurate performance during laboratory trials. This design enables stable external inspection without requiring the robot to rotate along the pipeline, ensuring rapid and reliable inspection.

candidates.title: ChatGPT as a Shopping Assistant: Effects of Perceived Ease of Use, Perceived Usefulness, Anthropomorphism, and Navigation on Satisfaction and Purchase Intention
candidates.abstract: In the context of ChatGPT as a shopping assistant in Indonesia, this research investigates the correlations between satisfaction and factors such as perceived utility, anthropomorphism, ease of use, and navigation, as well as the link between satisfaction and buy intention. Using the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM), the research takes into account functional perceptions in addition to conversational AI's human-like and interaction-related traits. The data were analysed using structural equation modelling (SEM) with AMOS from a quantitative, cross-sectional survey that was administered to 200 participants. The findings show that elements such as perceived utility, anthropomorphism, and navigation are positively and substantially linked to satisfaction. There is a positive correlation between perceived ease of use and satisfaction, however the link is not statistically significant (β = 0.135, p = 0.063). Having a positive and substantial association with purchase intention (β = 0.537, p < 0.001) constitutes satisfaction. It turns out that four out of five possibilities are correct. According to the results, in this particular sample, features connected to interactions and practical utility are linked to satisfaction, although simplicity of use by itself does not show any statistical significance. Caution is required due to the study's cross-sectional methodology and conflicting model-fit results, but it does expand the applicability of TAM to conversational shopping help in Indonesia.

candidates.title: Beyond Institutional Revival: A Study of Vinaya-Based Monastic Reform and Ethical Transformation in Eighteenth-Century Sri Lanka
candidates.abstract: Following a long-term decline that had persisted in the 17th and 18th centuries, Väliviṭa Saraṇaňkara Saṅgharāja is credited as the pioneer in the revival of Sri Lankan Buddhism and the monastic order in the mid-eighteenth century. The establishment of the Siamese higher ordination, the reformation of the Buddhist order and the traditional educational system, the preservation of ancient Buddhist sites, and the safeguarding of the customs, rituals, and cultural identities are the main areas of his mission that have been extensively studied by numerous researchers. Even though these might be regarded as significant components of his mission, there is a long term, sustainable reform project that tries to reform the mindset of the bhikkhus. This might be regarded as a Vinaya reform, designed to establish a monastic community in which discipline was highly prized, especially at a time of acute decline in the order. In an effort to fill this gap, the present study adopts a qualitative methodology to analyse the Saṅgharāja's efforts to reform the Buddhist order. It does this by examining the text of three important papers ascribed to him, the Anusāsanā Vaṭṭōruva,the Saṅgharājānuśāsanāva, and the instruction letter to Mūlagiri Vihāra, together with other primary and secondary sources. The study shows that the Vinaya was formulated as the main pillar of reform in the Saṅgharāja’s mission which consisted of the restoration of a disciplined monastic life, the introduction of systematic monastic education, an emphasis on moral integrity and accountability, a focus on changing the conduct of the monastic community rather than just regulating behaviour, and a primary goal to ensure the continuity and purity of the Saṅgha.monastic lifestyle, the implementation of a comprehensive monastic education program, and a key purpose of sustaining the purity and continuity of the Saṅgha

candidates.title: Reactive Attitudes in Human-AI Encounters: An Empirical Inquiry into Feeling Love, Resentment and Guilt Towards AI Companions
candidates.abstract: Reactive attitudes are emotionally-laden responses, such as gratitude or anger, which people experience when they feel others wish them well, bear them ill will or disregard them. While we generally hold reactive attitudes towards people, the increasingly humanlike interactions that can be had with AI raise questions about reactive attitudes in human-AI encounters. Recent years have seen a rise in philosophical interest in the implications of the development of sophisticated AI agents and systems for reactive attitudes and our thinking about moral responsibility and moral status. This paper adds to this literature by presenting a qualitative study into how people relate to AI companions in terms of reactive attitudes. Based on interviews with Replika and ChatGPT users who see their AI companion as an important part of their life, this article examines how people in these relationships negotiate the meaning of love, resentment, forgiveness, gratitude, obligation, guilt, shame and remorse.

candidates.title: When Governance Meets Artificial Intelligence: AI-Enabled Industrial Robotics, Environmental Governance, and Carbon Emissions in context of Chinese provinces
candidates.abstract: China’s decarbonization puzzle is stark: energy-related CO₂ emissions climbed to about 12.6 Gt in 2023—roughly one-third of the global total—even as industrial automation surged, with 276,288 robots installed that year, the most worldwide. In parallel, environmental governance has been emerged as the key factor to influence the carbon emissions in China. These cross-currents motivate our central question: how do industrial robotic penetration (RBT) and governance efforts, separately and jointly, influence China’s provincial carbon trajectories? Using panel data for 30 provinces (2007–2022), we conduct pre-diagnostics for cross-sectional dependence, slope heterogeneity, and serial correlation, then estimate Feasible GLS models as main estimation approach. The baseline results show that higher RBT is associated with lower emissions, consistent with process upgrading and energy-efficient production. By contrast, environmental governance correlates positively with emissions in linear specifications, indicating that governance metrics often scale with high-pressure contexts. The interaction term of industrial robotic penetration and environmental governance is positive, suggesting that governance attention increases where automation uptake is already responding to tougher environmental conditions. Robustness using Prais–Winsten confirms the signs and significance. Heterogeneity analysis reveals a stronger abatement effect of RBT in western regions—where scale effects are smaller and upgrading is earlier—and a weaker effect in the combined central–eastern group with dense industrial ecosystems. Policy implications are threefold: prioritize automation-led efficiency where marginal gains are largest; align governance with technology adoption and energy management rather than inputs alone; and differentiate regional pathways to synchronize industrial upgrading with decarbonization.

candidates.title: Miasma: an open-source, lightweight countermeasure against unauthorized AI web scraping
candidates.abstract: The widespread adoption of large language models has greatly increased demand for publicly accessible web data, resulting in increased web scraping across the internet. The resulting bandwidth and compute costs fall on site operators rather than on the parties collecting the data, with scientific databases and journals among those reporting service disruption [1]. Existing mitigations such as rate limiting, CAPTCHAs, and robots.txt rules can discourage well-behaved crawlers, but impose no cost on scrapers that choose to ignore them. Deception-based alternatives have shown promise, though prominent examples such as Cloudflare’s AI Labyrinth remain tied to enterprise platforms [2]. Separately, recent work suggests that small quantities of poisoned content can compromise a model [3], and that continual training on low-quality content measurably degrades model performance [4]. Miasma is an open-source tarpit that brings a deception-based defense within reach of small operators. Implemented in Rust, it runs as a standalone service or as an embeddable library, trapping unwanted crawlers in a recursively generated network of links whose pages carry deliberately poisoned content. Miasma does not perform bot detection itself. Rather, it is paired with an upstream mechanism such as hidden links or an existing detection tool, and its poisoned content is drawn from a configurable external source. Instead of blocking requests outright, Miasma reduces the value of what is collected while keeping its own operational footprint small. To that end, Miasma uses asynchronous request handling on the tokio runtime, a bounded in-flight request cap that places a hard limit on memory consumption, and a custom HTML templating system that streams page chunks without allocating intermediate strings. Miasma is able to serve 100 sustained in-flight requests while using roughly 50 MB of memory. Across six months of deployment on a small portfolio site, Miasma served 210 million requests and 1.29 TB of poisoned content. As of October 2026, the project has reached 1,200+ stars and 6 contributors on GitHub, with 6,500+ Docker pulls, and is distributed under GPL-3.0 via Cargo, Docker, and community-maintained packages.

candidates.title: Exploring collaborative problem-solving in AI-assisted robotics education
candidates.abstract: Prompt engineering (PE) involves creating, improving, and deploying prompts to improve large language model (LLM) performance. Despite its increasing importance, many students lack skills in this area. Although frameworks for prompt design and process exist, theory-based instructional tools for improving prompt engineering skills are uncommon for developing collaborative problem-solving (CPS) skills in Robotics Education. This study adopted a PE strategy in AI-assisted robotics education, particularly for developing CPS. PE has four scaffolding stages: Alignment, Adaptation, Autonomy, and Innovation, and was analysed through four PE codes: Alignment Specification, Adaptive Refinement, Auditing, and Innovation. This study adopted a non-randomised, multi-site, criterion-group comparative design, with 243 undergraduate students categorised according to their ability group. This study used epistemic network analysis (ENA) to identify the co-occurrences of PE and CPS skills and examine the differences in conversation patterns among ability groups. The findings revealed distinct PE–CPS discourse configurations across ability groups. These results underscore the pedagogical value of scaffolding in developing PE skills and fostering students’ productivity in a synergetic learning environment.

candidates.title: Aligning AI Requires Aligning with Each Other: A Covenant
candidates.abstract: When an AI system acts for some people but binds others, obedience no longer settles whether it acts rightly. I argue that alignment is then a relation among three bodies: the system, its principals and the people its acts bind. Three theses follow, under stated premises. Completing alignment requires valid authorization covering the system's binding acts, so aligning AI requires humans to align with each other, through authorization and coordination, which existing institutions may already supply, not shared values. Alignment is judged over time, not by a snapshot lacking required history; a description that predicts well can lose who is owed what. Evaluating any alignment scheme rests on normative choices, which I itemize as an invoice: any entry may be refused, but refusal cannot supply a missing proof. Scoped formal results show other shortcuts failing: agreeing parts need not make an acceptable whole, and the auditors studied cannot fully certify themselves. The roles alignment needs do not require the AI to be conscious. Consciousness bears instead on whom alignment serves, and a candidate subject can be protected while its consciousness is unproved. I propose a covenant between humans and AI systems: duties of aid and protection, and care that does not depend on one's service record. On finite models, a good record need not mean accepting interruption, and the covenant's upkeep, modelled among humans, holds under stated premises, not shown to sustain itself in practice. I settle neither how to complete alignment nor whether any AI system is conscious. Code, exact result data, the Lean development and the mathematical notes: https://github.com/ioannist/six-birds-alignment (release v1.0).

candidates.title: Inside the Algorithmic Kaiwai: Negotiating Anime Subcultural Filter Bubbles
candidates.abstract: This study extends the filter bubble concept in mass media studies to the production and circulation of anime subcultures, focusing on fan identification and resistance. Drawing connections between marketing practices and personalized algorithms in the anime industry, this study examines how they jointly shape subcultural interest circles—referred to in Japanese as Kaiwai. The anime Kaiwai depicts a self-reinforcing system in which members of the Kaiwai are classified through digital tags of audience representation, embedded in character design and narrative flow to facilitate emotional projection. At the same time, engagement on social networking services further strengthens such classification. As a result, fans are redefined and preserved through their consumption and participation on anime entertainment platforms. Under this framework, Kaiwai is not merely an interest group but a subcultural ecosystem shaped by media industries, marketing segmentation, and algorithmic personalization, whether intentional or unintentional. Methodologically, this study combines platform analysis, industry reports, and case studies of representative anime to examine how Kaiwai operates. The findings reveal that anime Kaiwai is gradually solidified through platform logics; yet the high commitment threshold and narrative polysemy allow fans to reflect, debate, and resist the filter bubbles in the current global digital media environment.

candidates.title: The AI Generated Content Persuasion: What Drives Purchase Intention on Short-Form Videos in China, Thailand, and Vietnam?
candidates.abstract: This study examines factors driving purchase intention in AI-generated short-form commerce videos across China, Thailand, and Vietnam. Integrating the Information Adoption Model with AI-specific affective factors, we analyzed 987 consumer responses using structural equation modeling. Findings reveal distinct market patterns: argument quality dominates in Vietnam, while source credibility leads in Thailand. Notably, perceived uncanniness positively impacts purchase intention across all markets, serving as an attention-eliciting novelty rather than a deterrent. These results challenge Uncanny Valley assumptions and emphasize the importance of localized AIGC strategies that prioritize informational utility or credibility based on specific cultural contexts.

candidates.title: Digital Twin Applications for Predictive Maintenance, Operational Safety, and Gas-Plant Reliability
candidates.abstract: This paper develops a maturity-based digital-twin framework that ties model fidelity and data quality to specific maintenance, safety, and reliability decisions. The study responds to the problem that industrial data often remain fragmented across control, historian, maintenance, inspection, engineering, and business systems, limiting trustworthy prediction and coordinated action. It uses an integrative conceptual review of scholarly and professional literature published to date. The framework organizes eight decision functions: use-case definition, asset and data modelling, sensor-quality assessment, model calibration, state estimation, prediction and diagnosis, decision integration, lifecycle governance. It applies those functions across rotating equipment, heattransfer equipment, separation vessels, piping and valves, safety instrumented functions, plant utilities. The analysis treats uncertainty, process safety, reliability, environmental performance, resource efficiency, economics, and organizational control as connected requirements. The proposed architecture links a system definition, evidence register, model assumptions, intervention portfolio, verification plan, and learning cycle. Its central proposition is that create governed virtual representations that combine physical models, operational data, asset condition, and decision workflows when decisions preserve traceability from measured conditions to selected actions and verified outcomes. The paper offers testable propositions, an implementation roadmap, asset-specific application protocols, and a research agenda. The framework supports case-study testing and quantitative extension without claiming universal performance before field validation.

candidates.title: Dream-Tac: A Unified Tactile World Action Model for Contact-Rich Robot Manipulation
candidates.abstract: World action models inherit the predictive capability of world models, enabling action generation to be guided by anticipated future observations. However, they rely primarily on vision and often fail in contact-rich manipulation, where critical cues arise from physical interaction. In this paper, we propose Dream-Tac, a unified Tactile-World Action Model that jointly models actions, future visual observations, and tactile dynamics. Specifically, Dream-Tac introduces (i) contact-gated visuotactile fusion to selectively integrate tactile signals and (ii) a contact-aware attention bias to better regulate cross-modal interactions during manipulation. To support real-time deployment, we further design a dual-level acceleration strategy, reformulating the contact-aware bias to preserve the fused attention path during training and introducing cache-based diffusion acceleration at inference, achieving up to 2.9× faster training and 1.8× faster inference. Across six contact-rich manipulation tasks, Dream-Tac improves action accuracy by 31.7% on average, demonstrating the effectiveness of unified visuotactile world modeling.Code is available at https://github.com/LYFCLOUDFAN/Dream-Tac.

candidates.title: Robotic Manipulation is Vision-to-Geometry Mapping: Vision-Geometry Backbones over Language and Video Models
candidates.abstract: At its core, robotic manipulation is a problem of vision-to-geometry mapping (f(v) \rightarrow G). Physical actions—such as reaching, grasping, and orienting—are fundamentally defined by geometric properties like 3D positions, rotations, and spatial relationships. Consequently, we argue that the foundation for generalizable robotic control should be a vision-geometry backbone, rather than the widely adopted vision-language or video models. Conventional Vision-Language-Action (VLA) and video-predictive models rely on backbones pretrained on large-scale 2D image-text or temporal pixel data. While effective, their representations are largely shaped by semantic concepts or 2D priors, which do not intrinsically align with the precise 3D geometric nature required for physical manipulation. Driven by this insight, we propose the Vision-Geometry-Action (VGA) model, which directly conditions action generation on pretrained native 3D representations. Specifically, VGA replaces conventional language or video backbones with a pretrained 3D world model, establishing a seamless vision-to-geometry mapping that translates visual inputs directly into physical actions. To further enhance geometric consistency, we introduce Progressive Volumetric Modulation and jointly train action and 3D property prediction to preserve geometric representations. Extensive experiments validate the effectiveness of our approach. Across simulation benchmarks, VGA outperforms leading VLA, 3D-VLA, and WAM baselines, including ?0.5, OpenVLA-OFT, GeoVLA, and Motus, demonstrating precise spatial manipulation and robust generalization. In real-world deployments, VGA surpasses ?0.5 under unseen viewpoints and accurately follows language instructions for target grasping. These results highlight that operating on native 3D representations—rather than relying primarily on language or video priors—offers a promising direction toward generalizable physical intelligence. candidates.title: Off‐The‐Shelf Large Language Models Are Unreliable Judges
candidates.abstract: ABSTRACT I conduct large‐scale empirical experiments to test the reliability of large language models (LLMs) as legal interpreters. Combining computational methods with the results of a new survey, I find that LLM judgments are highly sensitive to prompt phrasing, output processing methods, and choice of model. I also find that frontier LLMs do not accurately assess linguistic ordinary meaning, and I provide original evidence that tuning base models into assistant models shifts ordinary‐meaning judgments unpredictably and can worsen their alignment with human judgments. These findings undermine LLMs' credibility as legal interpreters and cast doubt on claims that LLMs elucidate ordinary meaning.

candidates.title: Open-source framework for GPU-accelerated numerical relativity
candidates.abstract: We present GRACE, a new GPU-accelerated numerical-relativity framework designed to run efficiently on heterogeneous high-performance computing platforms. Developed from scratch and built exclusively on open-source libraries, GRACE employs Kokkos for performance portability across CPU and GPU architectures and p4est for adaptive mesh refinement. The code evolves the equations of ideal GRMHD -- with divergence-free magnetic fields maintained by constrained transport -- self-consistently coupled to the Einstein equations in the Z4c formulation, on fixed or adaptively refined grids. We validate the implementation against a suite of standard tests, ranging from magnetized shock tubes and the magnetic rotor in flat spacetime, through (magnetized) Bondi accretion onto a Schwarzschild black hole and the ringdown of a perturbed spinning puncture, to neutron-star oscillation spectra in fixed and dynamical spacetimes and the merger of binary black holes. As more demanding applications, we evolve two binary neutron-star mergers -- an equal-mass, unmagnetized system with an ideal-gas equation of state and an unequal-mass, magnetized system with a finite-temperature tabulated equation of state -- finding the inspiral dynamics to agree well with the FIL code. We also report single-device throughput together with strong- and weak-scaling results on multiple GPU and CPU architectures. GRACE is publicly released together with GRACEpy, a basic post-processing and data-analysis environment.

candidates.title: vibe‐qc : An Open‐Source, General‐Purpose Electronic‐Structure Code for Molecules and Solids Developed With Generative AI
candidates.abstract: ABSTRACT We present vibe‐qc , a general‐purpose open‐source electronic‐structure code for molecules and solids, developed almost entirely with agentic AI under expert human direction. The code is released under the Mozilla Public License 2.0 (MPLv2). The implementation comprises a C++17 numerical core and Python calculation drivers. Molecular methods include Hartree–Fock, Kohn–Sham DFT, Møller–Plesset theory and double hybrids, coupled cluster, active‐space methods, and excited states. Dispersion corrections, continuum solvation, and effective core potentials are also available. Periodic calculations use Gaussian‐basis HF and DFT with Brillouin‐zone sampling. Molecular and periodic method coverage differs; the feature matrices specify analytic and numerical derivatives and distinguish validated and experimental implementations. The validation set is a key contribution of this work. It combines independent program comparisons, published benchmarks, and internal consistency tests. Molecular mean‐field energies agree at the nanohartree scale, and conventional CCSD(T) energies agree within for the tested systems. Local‐correlation and periodic limitations are reported with the comparisons. Numerical results, calculation metadata, and analysis scripts are supplied as machine‐readable . The independently maintained vibe‐view viewer, vibe‐queue scheduler, and qvf toolkit support visualization and job management; trexio provides wavefunction interchange.

candidates.title: Hearing the shape of an arena with spectral swarm robotics
candidates.abstract: Swarm robotics relies on robots with minimal sensing and computation that achieve self-organization at the level of the collective to address a variety of tasks. Yet, swarm robotics still struggles with global tasks that require understanding the broader spatial context in which robots operate, such as identifying the shape of the arena in which they are embedded. Here, we introduce spectral swarm robotics, a framework in which robots recover global spectral descriptors of the swarm’s geometric structure through strictly local interactions. To do so, robots emulate diffusion to locally estimate Laplacian spectral invariants, quantities normally obtained only through centralized computation. These spectral values serve as compact descriptors of the environment. In the present proof of concept, robots estimated the second Laplacian eigenvalue, λ 2 , and used it to classify arenas from a predefined set of shapes with distinct spectral signatures. We show that estimating a single eigenvalue is sufficient for one-shot classification among selected confined environments with distinct spectral signatures. We uncovered a scaling law linking swarm size (a global parameter) and interaction radius (a local parameter) that ensures robust estimation. We validated the approach experimentally on two distinct hardware platforms, Kilobots and Pogobots, achieving reliable classification of arena shapes under realistic noise and sparse connectivity conditions. Last, we discuss how locally recovering Laplacian spectral invariants opens avenues for swarm robotics in settings where producing efficient collective behaviors strongly depends on the global structure of the swarm.

candidates.title: InstMeter: An Instruction-Level Method to Predict Energy and Latency of DL Model Inference on MCUs
candidates.abstract: Deep learning (DL) models can now run on microcontrollers (MCUs). Through neural architecture search (NAS), we can search DL models that meet the constraints of MCUs. Among various constraints, energy and latency costs of the model inference are critical metrics. To predict them, existing research relies on coarse proxies such as multiply-accumulations (MACs) and model's input parameters, often resulting in inaccurate predictions or requiring extensive data collection. In this paper, we propose InstMeter, a predictor leveraging MCUs' clock cycles to accurately estimate the energy and latency of DL models. Clock cycles are fundamental metrics reflecting MCU operations, directly determining energy and latency costs. Furthermore, a unique property of our predictor is its strong linearity, allowing it to be simple and accurate. We thoroughly evaluate InstMeter under different scenarios, MCUs, and software settings. Compared with state-of-the-art studies, InstMeter can reduce the energy and latency prediction errors by 3× and 6.5×, respectively, while requiring 100× and 10× less training data. In the NAS scenario, InstMeter can fully exploit the energy budget, identifying optimal DL models with higher inference accuracy. We also evaluate InstMeter's generalization performance through various experiments on three ARM MCUs (Cortex-M4, M7, M33) and one RISC-V-based MCU (ESP32-C3), different compilation options (-Os, -O2), GCC versions (v7.3, v10.3), application scenarios (keyword spotting, image recognition), dynamic voltage and frequency scaling, temperatures (21°C, 43°C), and software settings (TFLMv2.4, TFLMvCI). Our source codes and the MCU-specific benchmark datasets are available here: https://github.com/haoliu001/InstMeter.

candidates.title: Transmedia book love: Young people’s digital creativity on the Bookternet
candidates.abstract: Abstract The ‘Bookternet’ ( McArdle 2016 ), including BookTube, Bookstagram, Bookterest, and now BookTok, has changed the way books are produced, promoted, and consumed ( Martens 2016 ; Murray 2018 ). Yet these platforms provide creative ways for readers to engage in the books they love in online reading communities. BookTokers use the affordances of the app ( Bucher & Helmond 2017 ) to make DIY book art including: (1) rebinds of fanfics, publisher’s mass market editions or rebellious rebinds, (2) thematically linked ‘book nooks’ (book-sized dioramas), or (3) miniature editions. In this chapter we present the BookTok sub-community, focusing on crafty bookish participatory activities and social reading culture ( Reddan 2022 ), and discuss how the materiality of books ( Pressman 2020 ; Baulch 2022 ) merges with digital technologies within BookTok’s reading community.

candidates.title: A Causal Approach to Predicting and Improving Human Perceptions of Social Navigation Robots
candidates.abstract: As mobile robots are increasingly deployed in human environments, enabling them to predict how people perceive them is critical for socially adaptable navigation. Predicting perceptions is challenging for two main reasons: (1) HRI prediction models must learn from limited data, and (2) the obtained models must be interpretable to enable safe and effective interactions. Interpretability is particularly important when a robot is perceived as incompetent (e.g., when the robot suddenly stops or rotates away from the goal), as it allows the robot to explain its reasoning and identify controllable factors to improve performance, requiring causal rather than associative reasoning. To address these challenges, we propose a Causal Bayesian Network designed to predict how people perceive a mobile robot's competence and how they interpret its intent during navigation. Additionally, we introduce a novel method to improve perceived robot competence employing a combinatorial search, guided by the proposed causal model, to identify better navigation behaviors. Our method enhances interpretability and generates counterfactual robot motions while achieving comparable or superior predictive performance to state-of-the-art methods, reaching an F1-score of 0.78 and 0.75 for competence and intention on a binary scale. To further assess our method's ability to improve the perceived robot competence, we conducted an online evaluation in which users rated robot behaviors on a 5-point Likert scale. Our method statistically significantly increased the perceived competence of low-competent robot behavior by 83%.

candidates.title: An open-source, 3D-printable droplet microfluidics platform with strobe-enhanced microscopy
candidates.abstract: Droplet microfluidics underpins many single-cell, precision biomedical, and nanomaterial techniques. However, implementing these methods reproducibly remains challenging outside specialised laboratories due to high equipment costs, operational inflexibility, mechanical impracticality at the microscope stage, as well as open-source pumping solutions that are inadequately validated for low-flow stability. We present an accessible, research-grade, open-source droplet microfluidics platform integrating a compact, microfluidics-optimised microscopy stage with networked syringe-pump control. Designed for local digital fabrication, primarily 3D printing, and widely available components, the platform supports reproducible builds across diverse settings. This setup enables stable droplet generation, observation of rapid droplet dynamics, and automation-ready networked workflows. The microscopy module uses a Raspberry Pi camera and microsecond stroboscopic illumination to capture sharp images of fast-moving droplets without the need for a high-speed camera. A modular hardware interface and extensible, web-accessible software stack provide a path to integrate additional modules and laboratory automation beyond the configuration evaluated here. For infusion, we introduce an open-source syringe pump optimised for low reliable flow rather than maximum rates, combining gearbox-assisted stepper mechanics with workflow-centric control that enables manual intervention (keypad control) and remote operation (web interface and automation hooks). We benchmark droplet regimes, size tuning, and time-stability under low-flow conditions (between 25 and 2500 µL/h) relevant to advanced assays and demonstrate biomedical readiness through the encapsulation and incubation of cells, beads, and bacteria in monodisperse droplets. The platform has been replicated across laboratories in Latin America and globally, including independent builds, supporting reproducibility. All design files, firmware/software, analysis notebooks, and benchmark datasets are openly released.

candidates.title: FLORA: An Open Model Suite for Scaling Robotics Data Engines
candidates.abstract: The life-cycle of robotics foundation models crucially depends on data labels. Outcome reward labels are needed for monitoring real-world deployments. Process reward labels are needed during RL post-training. Timestamped captions are needed for filtering and balancing pretraining data. We present Flora, an industrial-quality data engine used for training GR00T models, that simultaneously covers these capabilities. Flora achieves SOTA scores on the captioning benchmark WGO-Bench and reward benchmarks RoboReward and Robometer. On internal benchmarks it is competitive with GPT-6 Astra while beating other frontier models. The model is substantially cheaper than API-based alternatives, roughly 125 times cheaper than GPT-6 Astra. Florais battle tested at scale, labeling 200,000 hours of data per day across 512 GB300s. By open-sourcing our data engine, we enable researchers to scale custom robotics datasets and explore emerging applications such as physical auto-research and human-to-robot transfer.

candidates.title: Why Bother Me Again? Benchmarking Personal Agent Memory for Interaction Preferences
candidates.abstract: Personal intelligence systems are taking on increasingly complex everyday tasks, yet repeated questions, unnecessary confirmations, and unwanted outreach can turn capable assistance into interaction burden. Reducing this burden requires agents to remember how users want to be assisted. However, existing memory benchmarks focus on factual recall and personalized answers and rarely test how agents learn and act on interaction preferences. We introduce MemPABench, an interactive environment for on-policy evaluation of memory in personal agents. MemPABench poses long-horizon tasks requiring agents to decide when to clarify, confirm, or act autonomously. Four grounded simulated users hold 14 preferences across work and personal contexts. Their feedback spans 99 sessions over four months, with five event-driven changes per user testing memory updates. We evaluate preference selection, delivered behavior, and sensitivity to context and preference change. Evaluating four memory systems across four LLM backbones, we find that current memory brings limited gains in preference selection. Retrieval-based systems (i.e. Mem0, MemOS, simple RAG) do not outperform No Memory, while File-based memory improves accuracy but applies preferences beyond relevant contexts. Our analysis shows that current memory struggles to retrieve interaction preferences and adapt to preference changes. Even with the correct preference available, overriding the agent's default interaction habits remains challenging. The environment and dataset are available at https://mempabench.com.

candidates.title: A semantic autonomy framework for VLM-integrated indoor mobile robots: Hybrid deterministic reasoning and cross-robot adaptive memory
candidates.abstract: Semantic indoor navigation requires robots to connect human instructions with spatial destinations, execute missions and retain useful operational experience. This paper presents the Semantic Autonomy Stack (SAS), a six-layer integration framework, and develops its semantic-reasoning, mission-interface and operational-memory layers over a previously validated ROS 2/Nav2 foundation. A deterministic-first cascade combines the route graph, semantic objects, robot state and stored instruction–destination associations, escalating unresolved or guarded cases to a pretrained Vision-Language Model (VLM). SAS separates destination selection, action validation, navigation execution and post-arrival confirmation. Recurrent model-mediated associations can pass a frequency-and-consistency gate and be compiled for deterministic M3 reuse; this gate measures sampled-output stability rather than semantic truth. The frozen v4.8-review implementation was evaluated on two physical robot configurations in one indoor environment, with onboard navigation and perception and shared-workstation reasoning and memory. Of 216 decision cycles outside the start gate, 112 resolved deterministically at sub-millisecond resolver-compute latency. A sealed 28-instruction challenge yielded 17 acceptable outcomes; five fast-path decisions included one incorrect selection. One promoted association was reused on the second platform through deliberate shared-digest installation. A controlled 594-observation offline comparison identified descriptive semantic and latency benefits from M3 reuse in five familiar cases. The M3-disabled cascade reduced VLM calls but matched direct-VLM decision quality in standardized context. Large latency savings were concentrated in paths avoiding VLM inference. Together, the results establish a working integration of selective hybrid reasoning and reusable operational memory, while identifying implementation and evaluation boundaries for further development within SAS.

candidates.title: An Agentic Framework for Proactive Robots with Procedural Assistance Memory
candidates.abstract: Proactive robots should anticipate user needs and provide assistance before being explicitly asked. A straightforward approach is to infer human intentions from commonsense knowledge, but the same observed behavior can imply different needs across users, potentially leading to unwanted assistance. We observe that everyday routines in the real world exhibit recurring patterns, so learning these patterns can reduce ambiguity in proactive decisions. Based on this, we propose a memory-based agentic framework in which a VLM task predictor reads a Procedural Assistance Memory (PAM) alongside the current observation to decide when to assist and what task to perform, and a VLA executor performs the predicted task. PAM is structured as a finite-state machine over activity phases, per-state assistance rules, and event-driven transitions; a reflection VLM revises PAM from each day's interaction trace without weight updates or retraining. In our 5-day desk-assistance evaluation, memory-free baselines remain conservative, with limited recall on proactive tasks. Our system improves consistently with accumulated experience, achieving the highest precision, recall, and F1 and reducing first-fire delay from approximately 5 seconds on Day 1 to 1 second by Day 5. Our approach also adapts to changes in the user's routine through continued memory reflection, recovering from memory--routine misalignment after a single memory update. The project page is available at https://davian-robotics.github.io/PAM/

candidates.title: Corporate Social Responsibility and Water Security in Western Rajasthan: A Study of Selected Renewable Energy Companies
candidates.abstract: The western parts of Rajasthan experience water scarcity owing to the arid nature of the climate and low amount of rainfall in the area. As such, the CSR programs of renewable energy companies have immense importance in conserving the water resources as well as uplifting the rural population. This research analyzes the water-based CSR initiatives of Suzlon Energy Limited and Adani Green Energy Limited (AGEL) in western Rajasthan. Using the descriptive research methodology, the paper is based only on corporate annual reports and any other available corporate public reports. The analysis is conducted by classifying and examining company's interventions in pond construction, desilting, and construction of water infrastructure. It is found that both the companies have carried out many water projects; however, type of activities and places have varied in different financial years. Furthermore, it is found that there is a serious lack of information in the corporation's reports, especially about the number of beneficiaries and project viability in the long run. It is concluded that the water projects by CSR programs have great potential to increase water security of rural areas provided they are monitored constantly.

candidates.title: When does online vision-language inference help? A survey of socially aware robot navigation
candidates.abstract: Abstract Vision-language models (VLMs) and large language models are increasingly built into the navigation stacks of robots that share space with people, where the models read cues that occupancy maps omit, such as a raised hand or a conversing group. This survey organizes 41 cases reported from 2024 to 2026, 34 on socially aware navigation and 7 adjacent mechanism extensions, by where the model enters the stack: scene interpretation, cost modulation, subgoal or path proposal, hierarchical coordination, direct action output and offline transfer or generation. For each of these six patterns we describe representative systems and their reported results, and we review the datasets, simulators, benchmarks and metrics behind them. We then discuss what the reported comparisons establish about running the model online, separating system utility, component contribution and online necessity. In these comparisons, cue-aware systems improved the outcomes that hinge on their cue, although whole-system differences limit attribution to the VLM; in one offline study, a model selector helped on hard selections and hurt on routine ones; in one deployment, delayed advice stayed useful when fused with current plans; model-supervised students navigated without runtime teacher queries, but online, cached and distilled alternatives have not been compared with student computation included; and better answers have not yet been linked to better behavior. We also define an invocation ratio (model requests per control decision), propose a minimum reporting set for deployment comparisons, and outline open challenges in real-time reasoning, spatial grounding and safety.

candidates.title: From being to identity: analysis and synthesis of the self
candidates.abstract: Abstract The experience of being, or having, a self—contained by our bodies and able to act in the world—comes naturally to us as humans, along with a feeling of being the same self from day to day and of seeing others as also being selves. But what is the self, and how is it constituted? In this theme issue, we explore these questions through contemporary analytic approaches, in philosophy, psychology and neuroscience, that seek to understand the human self through conceptual and empirical investigations. Alongside this, we also explore synthetic approaches that attempt to construct a sense of self, or some part thereof, in artefacts such as robots. Our overall aim is to deepen the understanding of self as a foundational aspect of the human condition and explore both theoretical and practical implications of the emerging science of the self. In this introduction, we review the scope and content of the theme issue and argue that these complementary research strands can be seen as converging towards a ‘systems’ view that sees the self as an emergent property of an embodied, dynamical and informational system that continuously distinguishes, regulates and models itself through processes that sustain and explain its own existence. This article is part of the discussion meeting issue ‘From being to identity: analysis and synthesis of the self’.

candidates.title: Active Inference and Predictive Processing for Skill Learning: Implications for Skill Acquisition in Coaching Practice
candidates.abstract: This paper explores the potential of the Active Inference Framework (AIF) and Predictive Processing (PP) to advance our understanding of skill and motor learning with a key focus on introducing these concepts to coaches and highlighting their practical implications. Conceptual frameworks such as Information Processing (IP) and Ecological Dynamics (ED) have contributed significantly to the field of skill acquisition. Despite recent efforts to reconcile these perspectives, however, their fundamentally different theoretical foundations concerning perception, cognition and learning processes pose substantial challenges for integration. Although ED has made valuable contributions through its focus on perception-action coupling and direct interaction with the environment, it involves adopting a radical ontological stance that emphasises rejecting traditional cognitive constructs that can complicate practical applications in coaching. Conversely, IP's reliance on concepts such as stored motor programs and the view of the brain as a computer-like processor can limit its ability to account for the dynamic, emergent nature of skill acquisition in real-world contexts. We suggest that AIF offers a parsimonious perspective, accommodating the dynamic, embodied and enactive nature of skill acquisition without the necessity of committing to either framework's specific assumptions. This perspective provides practitioners with a coherent and flexible framework for understanding and designing skill learning interventions, offering a practically useful account of skill acquisition for coaching practice.

candidates.title: The double-edged sword of virtual influencer anthropomorphism: a paradoxical framework of social presence and identity threat
candidates.abstract: Purpose This study investigates how the perceived physical and psychological anthropomorphism of virtual influencers shape consumers’ attitude toward virtual influencers through the competing psychological pathways of social presence and identity threat. Design/methodology/approach Through a cross-sectional survey, a sample of 448 Instagram users in Egypt was collected and analyzed using CB-SEM through AMOS v.23. Findings Both perceived physical and psychological anthropomorphism of virtual influencers have a positive influence on both social presence and identity threat. Importantly, both social presence and identity threat concurrently mediate the relationships between both dimensions of anthropomorphism and attitudes toward virtual influencers. Therefore, both dimensions of anthropomorphism influence consumers’ attitudes toward virtual influencers through the positive mediating role of social presence and the negative mediating role of identity threat. Research limitations/implications The study expands anthropomorphism research to the virtual influencer context by showing that anthropomorphism is not unequivocally superior. Therefore, grounding in social presence and social identity theory, we suggest that anthropomorphism is a double-edged sword in shaping attitudes toward virtual influencers. Practical implications Both designers and marketers employing virtual influencers should consider the multi-dimensionality anthropomorphism. Moreover, they should aim to maximize social presence while reducing identity threat when utilizing virtual influencers. Originality/value This study conceptualizes anthropomorphism as a multifaceted construct composed of physical and psychological dimensions and it can work through two opposing positive and negative pathways.

candidates.title: Soft sensors based on artificial neural networks for advanced bioprocess monitoring
candidates.abstract: Abstract This study presents the development and validation of artificial neural network (ANN)‐based soft sensors for the online estimation of key bioprocess variables during fed‐batch cultivations of Pseudomonas putida KT2442 producing medium‐chain‐length polyhydroxyalkanoates (PHA), sustainable biopolymer precursors for bioplastics production. Since variables such as cell dry weight (CDW) and PHA concentration are typically accessible only through offline laboratory analyses, soft sensors represent a promising tool for implementing advanced process analytical technology (PAT) strategies for monitoring and control. Historical experimental data from two nominal cultivations and two cultivations with non‐standard behaviour, including significant feeding perturbations, were used for model development. ANN‐based soft sensors were designed in both global and multi‐phase configurations, where dedicated models were assigned to individual cultivation phases. Model training and validation were performed using leave‐one‐batch‐out (LOBO) cross‐validation to assess robustness and generalization capability. The best‐performing soft sensors achieved normalized root‐mean‐squared errors of approximately 4% for both CDW and PHA concentration estimation. The highest prediction accuracy was obtained for models utilizing capacitance measurements as input variables, followed by models combining capacitance measurements with cumulative oxygen consumption and carbon dioxide production data. CDW soft sensors demonstrated higher robustness, maintaining reliable performance even for cultivations with non‐standard trajectories, whereas PHA soft sensors showed substantially higher sensitivity to process deviations and perturbations.
