candidates.title: Pax Lambayeque? Trauma, interpersonal violence, and environment over 3,000 years in the Lambayeque Valley Complex, Peru
candidates.abstract: Previous research at archaeological sites in the coastal desert of northern Peru suggests strong human behavioral responses to environmental shifts. For example, at the Huaca de la Luna, Sicán, and the Huanchaquitos-las Llamas sites, paleopathological and stratigraphic analyses suggest that sociopolitical elites organized mass human sacrifices between 550−1450 CE in response to sudden intense increases in precipitation, possibly caused by El Niño-Southern Oscillation events. However, there has not yet been quantitative research into the relationship between non-ritualized violence and precipitation over the longue durée . To investigate the role climate change may have had on driving violence in the Peruvian desert coast outside of episodic sacrifice events, as well as accidental injuries, we modeled the relationship between highland precipitation, El Niño flood frequency, and osteological trauma in the Lambayeque Valley Complex. We pull paleoclimate data from the CHELSA climate simulations, and paleopathological data from the extensive work of the Lambayeque Valley Biohistory Project, yielding a total sample size of 1,659 individuals from a period of over 3,000 years. Ultimately, we detect no strong evidence for an association between environmental factors and interpersonal violence and find that non-ritual violence in the Lambayeque Valley Complex was rare (1.6%). These findings support previous meta-analytical work in the south central Andes, which found similar results in coastal and middle elevation communities. This study not only adds to our understanding of the range of human behavioral responses to climate changes but also proposes the hypothesis that mass sacrifice in the Lambayeque Valley Complex was politico-religious in nature rather than a Malthusian consequence of resource stress.

candidates.title: Citizen 5.0: A New Social Contract for Artificial Intelligence
candidates.abstract: Artificial intelligence is being built at an extraordinary pace. But by whom, and for whom? As AI systems increasingly shape how people work, think, and are governed, the world has quietly slipped into treating citizens as consumers: recipients of decisions made elsewhere, rather than participants in making them. Citizen 5.0 confronts this shift directly. David Galipeau argues that the defining question of the AI era is not technological. It is human. Will citizens have a genuine seat in decisions that determine the future of labor, data, and cognition? Or will that future be decided unilaterally by a handful of technology companies? Drawing on rigorous, interdisciplinary research, the book builds a concrete framework for restoring citizens, not consumers, to the center of the AI era. It includes neurorights, data sovereignty, and a Synthetic Labor Tax that could reshape who owns the value AI creates. This is a precise, urgent case for reclaiming human agency before the future is built without us.

candidates.title: Tutorial: Vision-Based Formation Control with Differential-Drive Robots
candidates.abstract: This tutorial presents a step-by-step introduction to multi-robot formation control using differential- drive robots, an overhead camera, and Python. ArUco markers are used to estimate robot positions and orientations, while desired pairwise displacement vectors define a circular formation. By comparing measured and desired relative positions, the controller computes movement vectors that are converted into differential-drive wheel commands, with basic proximity-sensor-based obstacle avoidance. The tutorial guides readers through hardware and software setup, robot pose estimation, formation geometry, feedback control, system integration, and formation-error evaluation. Motivated by the need to bridge the gap between theoretical understanding and practical implementation in robotics education, we emphasize how mathematical concepts are translated into coordinated behaviors on physical robots. Although the implementation uses a specific robotic platform, the underlying perception and formation-control principles can be adapted to other differential-drive robots and simulation environments. The accompanying open-source GitHub repository provides the Python implementation, setup instructions, and demonstrations to support hands-on learning and further exploration of multi-robot systems.

candidates.title: BUT telepresence: a fully open-source VR framework for low-latency stereoscopic video streaming with end-to-end latency instrumentation
candidates.abstract: Abstract Advances in immersive telepresence have enabled compelling virtual reality (VR)-based teleoperation, yet existing systems remain difficult to reproduce, inflexible in their streaming configuration, and largely devoid of end-to-end latency instrumentation. Current research prototypes typically rely on fixed encoding parameters, do not expose a unified interface for real-time reconfiguration, and rarely support hardware-accelerated decoding on standalone VR headsets. As a result, the community lacks an open, validated reference framework for low-latency stereoscopic teleoperation. This paper introduces a fully open-source VR telepresence system that integrates stereoscopic capture on a two-degrees-of-freedom (2-DOF) camera module, low-latency encoding using GStreamer, head-coupled camera actuation, and a native OpenXR application capable of hardware-accelerated decoding on modern standalone VR headsets. A key contribution is a built-in end-to-end latency instrumentation mechanism that timestamps each stage of the pipeline and embeds these measurements into the media stream, enabling continuous monitoring by the VR client. This information enables the user to dynamically adjust codec, resolution, and frame rate to maintain stable operator perception under heterogeneous network conditions, including wireless links. The framework is validated in representative robotics scenarios, demonstrating reliable stereoscopic teleoperation with a measured instrumented end‑to‑end latency of approximately 79 ms on a quiet 6 GHz link and 101 ms with the operator’s link saturated by competing traffic, with the VR headset’s pose prediction helping, in informal use, to mitigate perceived delay for the operator. Because every pipeline stage is timed individually and the reported total is their sum, the instrumentation also localizes degradation to individual components: contention is shown to act almost entirely on receiver-side decoding and not on transport, and reducing frame rate under loss is shown to be counterproductive, neither of which is visible from aggregate latency alone. A pilot evaluation with operators closes the loop from instrumentation to end user: the framework imposes a latency condition, verifies per participant from its own telemetry what was delivered, and records the operator’s presence, workload and task performance on the same sessions. All software, including benchmark datasets and Grafana dashboard configuration, is released publicly at https://github.com/Robotics-BUT/BUT_Telepresence to support reproducibility and future research.

candidates.title: THE IMPACT OF INDUSTRIAL ROBOTICS ON PRODUCTIVITY AND THE LABOR MARKET
candidates.abstract: ABSTRACT The development of industrial robotics and automation is significantly transforming the organization of production processes and business operations in modern companies. The use of robots in manufacturing contributes to higher efficiency, precision, and productivity, while also leading to changes ih the labor market. This paper analyzes the impact of industrial robotics on enterprise productivity and the changes in employment structure resulting from automation. Special attenation is given to the economic effects of robot implementation, as well as the challenges related to adapting the workforce to new technological conditions. The focus is on shifts in demand for certain occupations, the need for additional employee training, and the emergence of new jobs connected to digital technologies. The research is based on analytical, descriptive, and comparative methods, along with a review of domestic and international literature. The results indicate that industrial robotics contributes to the growth of productivity and the competitiveness of companies, but at the same time requires continuous investment in knowledge development and adaptation of the labor market to modern technological changes.

candidates.title: Seventy years of parasocial research: a bibliometric analysis and science mapping, 1956–2025
candidates.abstract: Abstract Research using the term ‘parasocial’ has appeared since 1956 in media studies and psychology and, more recently, in influencer marketing. This study maps the development, intellectual structure and recent thematic direction of the 2174 journal works published from 1956 to 2025 that use the term ‘parasocial’ in its media sense. Using records from OpenAlex, it combines performance analysis with co-citation, bibliographic coupling, keyword mapping and topic analysis and tests the robustness of the main mapping results across alternative corpora, periods and network settings. Output increased from one article in 1956 to 521 works in 2025, and, by authors’ affiliations, the USA, Indonesia and China had the most works. Horton and Wohl’s 1956 article is cited by 63.1% of the works with a reference list. Under the main network settings, the most frequently cited references form two co-citation communities, which we interpret as a media-psychology foundation and an influencer-marketing stream; they differ in topic and in the age of their references, and the share of co-citation link weight between them increased across the three periods from 2014–2019 to 2023–2025. The keyword ‘Influencer marketing’ appears in 28.7% of the works published in 2023–2025; in that period the topic ‘Digital Marketing and Social Media’ exceeded ‘Media Influence and Health’, whereas across 2020–2025 the two were nearly equal (397 and 405 works). OpenAlex topic labels identify AI-related topics in 3.0% of the works from 2023–2025. A separate language-model-assisted classification of titles and stored abstracts classified 71 of these works (6.3%) as studying a parasocial bond with an artificial partner; the author examined every such case individually. Together, the widely shared cited reference, the rising co-citation between the two communities and the application of the concept to influencers and artificial agents offer a frame for comparing which conditions of a parasocial bond studies keep and which they change; how studies define or measure the phenomenon, and whether the concept applies to artificial agents, are questions that future content analyses and experiments could examine.

candidates.title: Adaptive patriliny: care and lineage continuity in Liangtouhun families in contemporary China
candidates.abstract: Drawing on field research and interviews with six families in a peri-urban setting in Jiangsu Province, this study examines how Liangtouhun arrangements connect caregiving, family recognition, and lineage continuity. Liangtouhun is understood as a marriage arrangement involving ongoing coordination with both spouses’ natal families, rather than a uniform pattern of alternating co-residence. The analysis identifies four related patterns: participants explained the arrangement through childcare needs and obligations to aging parents; caregiving contributions were invoked to justify claims for recognition; participants attached differing degrees of flexibility and significance to residential, surname, and ritual practices; and competing expectations were expressed through fairness, reciprocity, and family responsibility. Existing surname allocations are distinguished from unimplemented spousal agreements and prospective preferences. Care-for-recognition describes how practical support was connected to claims for involvement and belonging, without assuming a fixed exchange. Adaptive patriliny captures how bilateral participation can coexist with, and reconfigure, continuing commitments to descent-based family continuity. These commitments were expressed by members of both spouses’ natal families. The study therefore complicates an interpretation of bilateral participation as necessarily displacing patrilineal practices, while recognizing that the evidence does not establish the preservation of male decision-making authority.

candidates.title: AI companions, human concerns: a pragmatic perspective
candidates.abstract: Abstract The rise of agentic AI and so-called AI companions introduces a shift in the modes of interactions between humans and machines. The exact contours of this shift remain unclear, but early signs of social, affective, and even romantic engagements demonstrate areas of potential benefit and potent harms to individuals and to the broader social fabric. A full appreciation of these benefits and harms demands a multi-perspectival account not only of technological innovation and emerging modalities of human-machine interaction, but also of the historical, socio-cultural, psychological, and ethical aspects of companionship. This essay provides such as account through a pragmatist perspective that considers the material, institutional, and psycho-social conditions behind the rise of AI. From this perspective, the essay broadens the notion of “alignment” as one between means and ends rather than the commonly accepted formulation between design goals and outputs. We argue that AI companionship blurs the boundaries between tools and social actors—a dynamic that emerges from the interplay of technical architectures, intentional design practices, user psychology, and political-economic forces. Given that interplay, a set of interrelated questions arise, which we address in three clusters (supply, demand, mediation), highlighting the emerging social and ethical dilemmas, and suggesting pragmatic interventions to inform public discourse and policymaking. In so doing, we hope to curtail the tremendous fallouts that have become evident in other domains such as social media only in retrospect, and ​to contribute to the creation of an environment conducive to social cohesion and individual wellbeing.

candidates.title: Advancements in Embedded Surveillance Robotics for Defense and Security Applications
candidates.abstract: In military applications, surveillance plays a critical role in ensuring security, particularly in isolated and border areas. This chapter presents a recent approach to surveillance using a robot for military applications. The planned methodology is to substitute soldiers in border areas with robots, to enhance the security and both autonomous and manual control via internet connectivity. Equipped with multiple sensors and various electronic devices, the robot is designed to detect enemy presence, capture camera footage, and live-stream data to authorized personnel. This robot enables armed forces to proficiently monitor isolated areas and respond immediately to potential threats. Human risk is reduced by using this type of robot surveillance system. Deploying robots in high-risk isolated areas minimizes personnel exposure to potential threats while maintaining effective surveillance. The use of autonomous technology increases operational efficiency by enabling continuous surveillance without requiring constant human intervention. By combining cutting-edge embedded technology, real-time monitoring, and remote operability, this robot vehicle delivers a consistent and effective solution for border or boundary security. Integrating advanced technologies, such as artificial intelligence (AI), embedded systems, and very large-scale integration (VLSI), will significantly enhance the capabilities and efficiency of the robot in armed forces. This robot provides not only a human-free system but also an efficient smart system to address military challenges.

candidates.title: Virtual Smartphone Fan Fiction in the Age of AI: Technology Empowerment and Fan Culture Reproduction
candidates.abstract: This study examines virtual smartphone fan fiction, in which fans use large language models (LLMs) and front-end tools to create interactive smartphone interfaces. Through passwords, simulated apps, prewritten content, and AI-generated replies, readers explore a character’s digital space and participate in an unfolding narrative. Using the perspectives of technology empowerment and fan-culture reproduction, this study analyzes the shift from screenshot-based stories to operable interfaces, the redistribution of authorship, the production of virtual intimacy, and the limits imposed by AI models, community norms, and platform governance. It argues that interfaces and AI responses now help shape narrative rhythm and reader agency, while creators increasingly act as system designers. However, greater technical access does not guarantee cultural recognition. The reproduction of fan culture is therefore shaped by the interaction of creators, readers, interfaces, models, and communities.

candidates.title: Innovator 5.0: Integrating Design Thinking and Responsible Innovation into AI and Robotics Research Environments for Industry 5.0 and Society 5.0
candidates.abstract: Industry 5.0 and Society 5.0 call for a shift in AI and robotics development from a primary focus on automation and technical sophistication to holistic solutions that address human needs, social contexts, stakeholder perspectives, and broader societal impacts. Preparing future engineers for this shift requires educational approaches that connect technical development with design thinking and responsible innovation. To address this need, this study introduces Innovator 5.0, an educational framework that extends the Science–Engineering–Design (SED) model by incorporating responsibility (R + SED) within a design-thinking process. The proposed framework was implemented through seven embedded workshops during a five- to six-month international research internship involving nine undergraduate students across six AI and robotics projects. An exploratory post-programme evaluation examined participants’ design-oriented practices, perceived capability development, and experiences within the research environment. Participants reported high ratings across several evaluated dimensions, particularly for challenging problem statements before solution development (M = 6.78/7), systems thinking (M = 6.67/7), creative innovation (M = 6.56/7), contextual awareness (M = 6.33/7), and iterative revision (M = 6.11/7). They also highlighted project autonomy and facilitative mentoring as valued features, while limited direct stakeholder access was identified as an important implementation constraint. Together, these findings provide practical guidance for preparing engineers to consider the purpose, societal implications, and value of AI and robotics innovations alongside their technical feasibility, supporting people-centric and responsible engineering innovation.

candidates.title: The World Model Planning Accelerator (WMPA): Hardware-Algorithm Co-Design for Embedded AI in Robotics
candidates.abstract: Embedded AI is moving from perception to prediction. Robots now use world models$\unicode{x2014}$learned simulators that predict the outcome of candidate actions in a compressed latent space before any is executed. Every predicted step must be computed on board within a tight power and thermal budget, yet the energy these steps fundamentally require, and how far real hardware sits from it, have not been characterized. We derive lower bounds on the arithmetic operations and the CMOS dynamic energy of a latent state transition from information theory and Boolean circuit complexity. Profiling a DreamerV3-style Recurrent State Space Model (RSSM) shows that every rollout operation is memory-bandwidth bound and that a GPU consumes at least $5.9\times10^{10}$ times the CMOS energy floor. Transient 3D thermal simulations show that this inefficiency is also a thermal one, since sustained back-to-back planning heats a millimeter-scale silicon tile to 556 K even behind an ideal copper heat spreader. Guided by this chain from bound to bottleneck, we propose the World Model Planning Accelerator (WMPA), a chip architecture for embedded world model planning that combines near-memory computation, real-time entropy estimation, variable-precision rollout units, and copy-on-write latent scratchpads. With a design target of 40x lower power, the same tile stays near ambient at 306 K in simulation, pointing toward practical planning on thermally constrained robots.

candidates.title: Electronics and wearable devices of cellulose in 3D/4D printing
Adventures in Reproducing and Integrating Open-Source: Developing Guidelines for Modular Software Components in Robot Grasping and Manipulation Pipelines for Picking in Clutter
candidates.abstract: When developing a novel software component of a robot system, researchers typically integrate open-source code for other components in the pipeline, such as perception, grasp planning, and motion planning. However, there are several bottlenecks related to the accessibility and reproducibility of open-source which are stifling research, development, evaluation, and deployment of robots. To this end, we are working to develop community-driven guidelines for modular components in robot software pipelines in the context of picking in clutter. In this work, we investigate reproducing and integrating multiple perception and grasp planning components used in vision-based perception-to-action pipelines. The architecture and methodology used to conduct these exercises are reviewed, highlighting issues encountered along the way. Recommendations for guidelines to improve accessibility, reproducibility, and integration of modular open-source components are shared related to the assets included in an open-source release, methods to modularize components, and practices for development and testing.

candidates.title: Regulatory governance and full-scale digital transformation for prediction-based food safety management: Global trends and future perspectives
candidates.abstract: ABSTRACT Background The global food safety paradigm is shifting from traditional, reactive hazard control toward proactive, predictive risk management to address increasingly complex supply chain vulnerabilities. However, current digital implementations remain fragmented, creating structural bottlenecks that hinder the transition to next-generation regulatory science. Scope and approach To our knowledge, this study provides one of the first comparative critical analyses of the HACCP-based data governance frameworks of six major jurisdictions. We compare jurisdictions in which private actors play a relatively larger role in certification and implementation ('market-led': the United States, the European Union, Canada, and Japan) with those in which public institutions play a dominant role ('state-led': South Korea and China), positioned along a governance continuum in which all systems combine public and private functions, focusing on their capacity for real-time risk prediction, public-private data integration, and global interoperability. Key findings and conclusions The market-led systems examined tend to foster food safety culture but are affected by 'Data Silos' that limit actions to retrospective tracebacks. The state-led systems examined may enhance data integrity but can create a 'Data Island' paradox due to an over-reliance on automating isolated physico-chemical Critical Control Points. To overcome these limitations, we propose a conceptual framework for Full-Scale Digital Transformation (Full DX). Converging prerequisite programs, structured food safety culture assessment (e.g., Shapley-FAHP), and intentional threat mitigations (TACCP/VACCP) into an interoperable predictive network powered by ensemble machine learning could support a more resilient regulatory ecosystem for mitigating multidimensional global supply chain threats; this framework requires empirical validation.

candidates.title: Designing a Small Language Model Lexicon in Natural Language for Robotic Applications
candidates.abstract: In this paper, the aim is to present a project report of a method, based on which a small natural language lexicon is designed, or otherwise a small language model, for robotic applications. In this direction, a reference is made to Controlled Natural Languages, and their characteristics are determined for application in operational robotic vehicles. In addition, criteria are established for the selection of the nationality of the language, which constitutes the basis of the lexicon. A small introspection is made in the natural language unit of a human–robot interface, and a method is presented that examines the adequacy of the selected language in relation to the purpose of use of the system and the control criteria. The use of the lexicon’s method is presented, and an example of the analysis and inclusion of selected Greek language words is given. The reproduction of words from the lexicon’s stored data is also explained, as the reverse process that functions as a confirmation of the method. Received: 22 August 2025 | Revised: 20 April 2026 | Accepted: 12 October 2026 Conflicts of Interest The authors declare that they have no conflicts of interest to this work. Data Availability Statement Data sharing is not applicable to this article as no new data were created or analyzed in this study. Author Contribution Statement Ioannis Giachos: Conceptualization, Methodology, Software, Investigation, Resources, Writing – original draft, Visualization. Evangelos Papakitsos: Conceptualization, Methodology, Investigation, Resources, Writing – original draft. Nikoletta Samaridi: Investigation, Resources, Data curation. Michail Papoutsidakis: Validation, Formal analysis. Nikolaos Laskaris: Writing – review & editing, Supervision.

candidates.title: Interactive Visual Gym: Evaluating Visual Interaction Models with Simulated Users in Interactive Worlds
candidates.abstract: Visual interaction models that support users during ongoing physical tasks require evaluation in closed loop, where assistant responses can change subsequent user behavior and task outcomes. Existing benchmarks largely rely on offline replay and therefore cannot capture these effects. We introduce Interactive Visual Gym, a framework for closed-loop evaluation and training of visual interaction models through joint simulation of executable task environments and human users. We contribute three simulators that recreate everyday tasks and human-aligned action spaces across cooking, household manipulation, and mobile-interface domains, together with a persona-conditioned user simulation harness that collaborates with the assistant while incorporating controlled execution errors and other out-of-plan behaviors. We instantiate the framework as IVG-Bench, a benchmark with 315 interaction scenarios. Evaluating state-of-the-art VLMs as visual interaction models reveals substantial limitations: the best-performing model, Gemini 4 Argon, completes only 53.4% of tasks within the time limit, exhibits significant weaknesses in factual grounding and actionable guidance, and is often too slow to prevent errors when response latency is considered. We verify our evaluation protocol with a human study which finds 78.5% agreement between our interaction-quality metric and participant preferences. We further show that the environments provide useful learning signals: in a proof-of-concept GRPO experiment, closed-loop training improves both task success and interaction quality for Qwen3.5-4B model in our cooking environment.

candidates.title: Social Humanoid: Socially Responsive Human-Humanoid Interaction
candidates.abstract: Humanoid robots are typically trained as solitary agents, leaving them unable to coordinate physically with human partners who naturally anticipate and adjust to one another. To bridge this gap, we present Social Humanoid, a hierarchical system that generates and executes socially responsive whole-body motion on a 29-DoF Unitree G1 conditioned on a human partner's motion. Its high-level policy performs flexible sequence modeling of human and humanoid motion through a shared tokenized representation, generating reactive humanoid motion and anticipating the partner's motion when they are occluded, while a low-level whole-body tracking controller executes the generated motion on the robot. To train the system, we introduce a two-phase adaptive retargeting procedure that retargets one interaction partner to the robot while morphing the other partner to preserve contact dynamics, reachability, and relative body scale. We apply this procedure across five motion-capture datasets to produce a new Human-Humanoid Interaction (HHI) benchmark of 260 hours of human-humanoid interactions. Our results demonstrate that Social Humanoid produces coordinated, human-aligned behavior across diverse interaction types in simulation and the real world. Project page: https://von31.github.io/social-humanoid/

candidates.title: Insect-inspired hexapod robot with magnetically coupled compliant and modular drive system
candidates.abstract: Legged robots are increasingly inspired by insects’ ability to combine rigidity and compliance for agile, damage-tolerant locomotion in cluttered terrain. Herein, we introduce INSECTRON, a centimeter-scale hexapod robot that employs magnetic transmission to achieve robust mobility with minimal mechanical complexity. Each leg connects to the drivetrain via neodymium magnets, forming a self-aligning micro-clutch that transmits torque under normal load and safely slips under overload, while additional magnetic couplings between drive modules accommodate load imbalances and perturbations. Hall effect sensors provide proprioception for a phase-domain controller maintaining persistent anti-phase coordination. The magnetic transmission architecture introduces intrinsic mechanical adaptability, functionally analogous to biological preflex mechanisms, enabling rapid responses to external perturbations without additional control complexity. Experiments demonstrated stable locomotion across multiple slopes and substrates. Maneuverability was achieved through differential turning and spin-in-place. A minimum Cost of Transport (CoT) of 30 was achieved during locomotion experiments. Under vertical perturbations, INSECTRON autonomously recovered in over 90% of trials, highlighting strong passive impact tolerance. The architecture eliminates the need for precision alignment and mechanical fasteners, enabling tool-free leg replacement and rapid mechanical reconfiguration. This work establishes a scalable route toward modular, resilient, and field-deployable miniature legged robots for confined and uncertain environments.

candidates.title: VFlash: Fast, Accurate Visual Planning via Flash Primitive Decoding
candidates.abstract: Models for physical AI tasks, such as robotics and autonomous driving, need not reason solely in language. They can use visual plans--points, bounding boxes, and trajectories--to represent spatial goals and anticipate motion. However, autoregressive vision-language models generate these plans one coordinate token at a time, making richer predictions increasingly costly. We introduce VFlash, a method for fast, accurate visual planning through Flash Primitive Decoding. VFlash exploits the known structure of visual primitives to predict their coordinates jointly, using a lightweight drafter that generates an entire primitive in one forward pass. The layout adapts to the primitive's type, dimensionality, and length, supporting compact boxes and long, variable-length trajectories. Crucially, spatial accuracy need not require reproducing an autoregressive model's exact token sequence. VFlash therefore trains on annotated primitives and directly accepts structurally valid predictions without target-token agreement. Across the evaluated 2D and 3D robot trajectory tasks, VFlash consistently reduces prediction errors relative to autoregressive decoding. Preliminary single-rollout measurements indicate approximately 25x faster generation for 3D point motion forecasting. A world action model conditioned on VFlash plans achieves 70.2% average success across four MolmoSpaces task suites, compared with 62.6% for the baseline.

candidates.title: La-JEPA: Compact Robot Policies with Latent World Modeling
candidates.abstract: World-action models adapt pretrained video generators, and vision-language-action models build on pretrained vision-language backbones; both tie policy architecture and inference cost to large transformers designed for generation rather than control. It remains unclear how much these generation-oriented choices affect control. In this work, we introduce Latent Action JEPA (La-JEPA), a compact world-action model whose policy transformer is trained from scratch in the feature space of a pretrained V-JEPA 2.1 encoder. Following Fast-WAM, La-JEPA learns to predict future features jointly with actions during training and generates only actions at inference. Among policies without embodied pretraining, La-JEPA achieves state-of-the-art performance in clean and randomized RoboTwin 2.0 scenes and on LIBERO-Plus with correct instructions, while using far fewer parameters than the strongest competing policies. It runs substantially faster than Fast-WAM at comparable performance and outperforms the closest JEPA-based methods, LeapBot-WA and JEPA-WAM, on LIBERO-Plus and RoboTwin 2.0 without their pretrained policy backbones. On four real-robot tasks, its average success is comparable to pi0.5 and above non-embodied-pretrained baselines. Through a design study of the choices behind La-JEPA, we show that JEPA features outperform video VAE latents, most clearly out of distribution, and that training-time future prediction choices significantly impact the policy even when future prediction is skipped at inference. We correct the LIBERO-Plus instructions, as the officially released evaluator corrupts them for most variants, and re-evaluate several strong open baselines. Without a generative pretrained policy backbone, La-JEPA is better and faster than far larger policies, suggesting that robot foundation models may benefit from architectures designed for control rather than inherited from generation.

candidates.title: A Search for Exoplanets around Northern Circumpolar Stars. XI. A Planetary Companion around HD 112987 and a Planetary Companion Candidate around HD 58545
candidates.abstract: Abstract We present precise radial velocity (RV) measurements of the northern circumpolar giant stars HD 58545 and HD 112987 obtained over 8 yr with the Bohyunsan Observatory Echelle Spectrograph and supplemented during the final 3 yr by the Network of Robotic Echelle Spectrographs. RV variations in giant stars may arise from orbiting companions or intrinsic phenomena, including pulsations, chromospheric activity, and rotational modulation. To distinguish these possibilities, we analyzed line-profile variations, line bisectors, chromospheric activity indicators, and photometric data, and modeled the RV time series with Keplerian orbits using Markov Chain Monte Carlo sampling. For HD 58545, the best-fitting Keplerian model yields an orbital period of 450.44 − 4.63 + 3.35 days and a minimum companion mass of 3.65 − 0.58 + 0.61 M J . For HD 112987, we derive an orbital period of 554.96 − 4.67 + 4.14 days and a minimum companion mass of 8.48 − 0.73 + 0.96 M J . None of the activity diagnostics for HD 112987 exhibits significant variability at the RV period, consistent with a Keplerian interpretation. In contrast, several activity diagnostics of HD 58545 exhibit periodicities comparable to the RV period, which is also consistent within the uncertainties with the projected rotational timescale, P rot / sin i = 462 ± 33 days . Thus, rotationally modulated stellar variability may contribute to the RV signal. Although the signal can be described by a Keplerian model, the current data cannot distinguish unambiguously between a planetary companion and intrinsic stellar variability. We therefore conclude that HD 112987 hosts a planetary companion, whereas further monitoring is required to determine the origin of the RV signal in HD 58545.

candidates.title: Into the Infinite Possibilities: Omar Yaghi’s Vision for Science in the Era of AI
candidates.abstract: 2025 Nobel Laurent Omar Yaghi is establishing a new center in Tsinghua University, aiming to transform chemistry and materials science through AI and robotics.

candidates.title: Intimacy Robots and Inward Decline: From Individual Symbolism to Civilisational Consequence
candidates.abstract: Abstract Philosophical work on intimacy robots has kept to two registers: the welfare of the individual user, and the symbolic wrong done to the classes of person such artefacts represent. Danaher’s symbolic-consequences argument, the fullest statement of the critical case, concedes that the downstream effects of that symbolism are hard to establish, and recommends an experimental posture. This paper takes the concession as its problem. The debate has no macro-social level of analysis, and without one it cannot say which consequences to look for. Drawing on the sociology of solidarity, Vallor’s account of moral deskilling, and the older literature of civilisational decline, it sets out three mechanisms by which individually rational uses of intimacy technology could aggregate into collectively costly outcomes: demographic subtraction, relational deskilling, and the habituation of desire to objects that cannot reciprocate. Each is put as a conditional with its defeaters named, not as a prediction. Tested against current evidence, including a nationally representative survey of adolescent companion-AI use and experimental work finding that AI companions do reduce loneliness, the third mechanism proves best supported analytically and the first least supported empirically. The result is a framework for aggregation, not a forecast of collapse; the paper closes by saying what would disconfirm it.

candidates.title: Interrogating Large Language Model Discourse on Pornography: Implications for Sexuality Education
candidates.abstract: Large Language Models have had a massive impact on learning, knowledge production, and educational processes. Concerns regarding the reliability of the knowledge LLMs produce, the impact of their use on critical thinking, and how to promote AI literacy, have been raised by many critical researchers, especially in relation to sensitive topics. This paper explores implications of the use of LLMs for comprehensive sexuality education and pornography literacy. Discourses generated by popular LLMs when asked about pornography are analyzed through a feminist lens. The LLMs produced power-blind statements about pornography, creating silences around the gendered practices. Moreover, the LLMs produce reduced discourses around pornography, violence against women, and consent. When asked to generate lesson plans, simplistic plans were created that lack systemic analysis of pornography and limit critical thinking to individual awareness. The paper argues that if LLMs are applied in CSE, the discourses they generate must be carefully considered through feminist and critical pedagogical perspectives that address power relations, oppression, and violence within the wider social context. Furthermore, the results suggest that the proliferation of easily accessible AI-generated knowledge makes comprehensive sexuality education curricula about pornography and teachers’ training even more essential.

candidates.title: “Society failed men”: male self-help influencers around dating and fitness, optimised hegemonic masculinity and networked misogyny
candidates.abstract: Examining an important aspect of wellness industries namely male self-help influencers and their content, this paper studies the everyday expression of non-violent gendered extremism on social media and the ways that visuals help extremism to spread. The article, first, argues that the purported authenticity and intimacy along with platform affordances and vernaculars used by male self-help influencers make misogyny and heteronormativity accessible. These influencers brand themselves as entrepreneurial subjects and informed experts, embedded within the global neoliberal consumer landscape, in line with the burgeoning mainstream interest in wellness. Second, the article shows how seemingly “apolitical” and “neutral” media content, combined with references to popular media cultures and manosphere memes, perpetuate covert and acceptable networked misogyny. Expanding knowledge on influencer cultures, gender and online extremism, our findings identify these influencers as fun and accessible symbols of a widespread right-wing movement online, perpetuating stereotypical gender norms and optimized and hegemonic masculinity.

candidates.title: DMuon-2: Scaling Matrix Optimizers in Data Parallelism with Topology-Aware Matrix Ownership and Communication
candidates.abstract: Matrix optimizers such as Muon update whole weight matrices, which conflicts with the element- or row-wise sharding of data-parallel runtimes. Once parameters are sharded as well, matrix optimizers incur extra communication or repeated computation. We present DMuon, a matrix-granular optimizer runtime for PyTorch FSDP (ZeRO-2/3) and HSDP. DMuon assigns each matrix a unique owner, which performs the Newton--Schulz (NS) iteration and optimizer update on the full matrix, and balances the load across owners by computational cost. On HSDP, ownership is global across replicas, so the cluster keeps a single copy of gradients and optimizer state, and updated parameters are published across nodes as soon as they are ready, overlapping subsequent computation. This layout makes every collective sparse and variable in length, so DMuon schedules these collectives as their data becomes ready and routes them along the cluster's two-level network. On up to 256 H100 GPUs, across three dense LLMs and two VLA models, DMuon matches or exceeds the training throughput of PyTorch FSDP2 with AdamW, reaching 1.05$\times$ that of FSDP2 with AdamW at the median on 256 GPUs. The optimized parameter gathering and gradient reduction absorb the extra communication and computation a matrix optimizer requires. Against a gather-then-replicate Muon baseline, DMuon's throughput is 2.1 times as high at the median.

candidates.title: ApproxHDC: Approximation Tuning for Hyperdimensional Computing
candidates.abstract: As Moore's law reaches its physical and economic limits, domain-specific approaches are increasingly employed to accelerate machine learning workloads. Hyperdimensional Computing (HDC) represents one such emerging paradigm, offering an alternative to conventional deep learning techniques. Rooted in cognitive models of computation, HDC is designed bottom-up with hardware efficiency as a first-class objective. Consequently, HDC workloads map naturally to heterogeneous hardware platforms, including CPUs, GPUs, and FPGAs, as well as emerging in-memory computing technologies such as Resistive RAM (ReRAM) and Phase-Change Memory (PCM). The intrinsic tolerance of HDC algorithms to noise and approximation enables substantial performance gains with minimal loss in inference quality. In this work, we introduce ApproxHDC, a framework for automated identification and application of domain-specific approximations in HDC workloads. ApproxHDC extends the HPVM-HDC compiler infrastructure to enable retargetable compilation across diverse hardware backends, including CPUs, GPUs, and simulated ReRAM and PCM-based accelerators. The space of possible software and hardware approximations in HDC is exponentially large, making exhaustive exploration intractable; ApproxHDC employs efficient search and analysis techniques to navigate this space and identify high-impact approximations. We further integrate hardware-level approximation mechanisms within the HDC accelerator to demonstrate ApproxHDC's ability to exploit both software and hardware approximations. Experimental evaluation shows that ApproxHDC achieves up to 17.25x speedup on CPUs, 14.97x on GPUs, and 4.69x on SpecPCM while staying within user-specified quality-of-service constraints, outperforming the state-of-the-art MicroHD framework by 3.49x. HDC-specific search space pruning reduces the design space by 71 to 491 orders of magnitude automatically and up to 89 more with developer guidance, enabling discovery of high-quality configurations within minutes.

candidates.title: Software-Defined Context-Aware Virtual Fixture for Teleoperation via Vision-Language Model
candidates.abstract: Abstract Precise teleoperation in unstructured environments remains challenging, because human errors and system-inherent limitations such as control jittering can significantly degrade task success and operational efficiency. To address these limitations, this paper proposes a software-defined Context-Aware Virtual Fixture (CAVF) system that leverages the open-world understanding of a Vision-Language Model (VLM). The proposed system automatically generates motion guidance for the robot end-effector (EEF) to assist teleoperation, preserving critical task-relevant motion while suppressing unnecessary translation and rotation components. This framework enables the autonomous generation of context-aware, haptic-free assistance without relying on handcrafted rules or physical force-feedback devices. Quantitative experiments in both simulation and real-world environments demonstrate that the proposed system significantly improves success rates, reduces completion times, and enhances trajectory efficiency compared to conventional teleoperation.

candidates.title: A human-centric large language model interface for monitoring and control of autonomous mobile robots via digital twins in industry 5.0
candidates.abstract: The diversity of industrial robot manufacturers, proprietary programming languages, and graphical interfaces complicates robotic system deployment and operation. This heterogeneity highlights the need for intuitive, accessible, and human-centric interaction methods. This paper presents a framework for natural language-based monitoring and selected control of autonomous mobile robots using a Large Language Model (LLM) interface, structured API communication, and digital twin visualization. The approach enables operators to interact with robots through natural language without requiring detailed knowledge of robot-specific interfaces or technical commands. The framework is evaluated from the operator’s perspective, focusing on its ability to simplify access to robot information, reduce interaction complexity, and support selected control tasks. Digital twin integration provides additional visual feedback on robot status and its operating environment. The proposed framework contributes to the development of more transparent, accessible, and human-oriented robotic systems aligned with Industry 5.0 principles.

candidates.title: Technostress in a Multi-Platform Robotic Surgery Environment: A Phenomenological Study of Operating Room Nurses' Lived Experiences in China
candidates.abstract: Abstract To explore the lived experiences of technostress among operating room nurses working in a multi-platform robotic surgery environment in China. A descriptive phenomenological study was conducted in a tertiary hospital in Wuhan between March and June 2026. Eighteen operating room nurses with robotic surgery experience were recruited through purposive sampling. Data were collected through face-to-face semi-structured interviews and analysed using Colaizzi's phenomenological method with MAXQDA 24. Four themes and twelve sub-themes were identified: system integration and cognitive adaptation across multiple platforms; physical layout, hardware adaptation, and environmental compatibility; digital ecosystem evolution and professional boundary shifts; and professional role evolution and institutional support mechanisms. Participants described sustained cognitive and operational demands arising from platform switching, differences in hardware and interface design, repeated software updates, remote surgery requirements, and expanding technical responsibilities. These experiences reflected multiple dimensions of technostress, including techno-overload, techno-complexity, techno-uncertainty, techno-invasion, and techno-insecurity. Technostress in multi-platform robotic surgery is therefore shaped not only by technological complexity, but also by the continuous need to adapt across systems and by insufficient platform-specific organisational support. Targeted training and stronger technical and organisational support may help nurses adapt to increasingly complex robotic surgery environments.

candidates.title: V1: An Open-Source Shallow-Water Stereo Research ROV — Hardware Design Files and Software
candidates.abstract: V1 is an open-source remotely operated underwater robot developed initially for supervised shallow-water stereo data collection and intended for reuse in related shallow-water visual research. It combines commercial propulsion, flight-control and computing components with a single acrylic watertight enclosure, six thrusters and a common multilayer internal payload rack that can be withdrawn from the rear for equipment access. A custom stereo mount behind a shared flat front viewport provides 80, 100 and 120 mm nominal mechanical camera separations for manual selection and fixation before a task. This deposit provides an engineering-only distribution based on public source release v0.1.1 (4 November 2026). It includes 11 editable SolidWorks 2018 custom parts; DXF, STEP and STL exports; five editable R1 manufacturing-review drawings, associated custom models and PDFs; functional wiring diagrams; the bill of materials and cost basis; assembly, deployment and operating instructions; onboard acquisition/communication software; and selected offline calibration and processing tools. Temperature validation data, statistics, audit logs and thermal analysis scripts are excluded at the author's request. The original GitHub release and ZIP remain unchanged. PACKAGING_NOTE.md records the selected scope; manifest.json and SHA256SUMS are regenerated for this distribution. FILE_INDEX.md lists the actual 122 files, purposes and licences. Mixed licences apply by file: CERN-OHL-P-2.0 for hardware and functional wiring; MIT for supplied engineering software; and CC BY 4.0 for project-authored documentation, BOM and metadata. Original licence texts, directory notices and THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md remain authoritative. Commercial reference CAD, private complete assemblies and separately licensed upstream drivers, kernels, SDKs and SLAM algorithms are excluded. York-Tank is a separate research output associated with https://doi.org/10.3390/s26206567. Its complete raw dataset is not included in this hardware archive. The supplied R1 drawings retain manufacturing-review/nominal status. Dependencies, calibration inputs and processing scope are documented in the package.

candidates.title: Open-HumanWAM: An Open Recipe for Scaling Human and Robot Experience for Embodied Foundation Models
candidates.abstract: Egocentric human video offers a scalable source of manipulation priors for robot learning, yet translating raw data scale into generalizable robot policies demands rigorous data curation and training recipes. We introduce Open-HumanWAM, the first fully open recipe for scaling egocentric pretraining to 50,000 hours, anchored by Open-HumanWAM-50K---a curated egocentric video corpus densely annotated with hand motion and natural language. Leveraging this corpus, we systematically investigate pure human pretraining via closed-loop simulation evaluations and uncover an empirical log-linear scaling law linking pretraining data hours to downstream robot success rates. Grounded in these findings, we develop HumanWAM-Vanilla, a world--action model pretrained exclusively on 50k hours of egocentric human video. Upon robot post-training, HumanWAM-Vanilla reaches 92.08% success on RoboTwin 2.0 Clean2Clean and 68.88% on Clean2Random, alongside a 14.17% mean success rate and a 19.00 mean progress score on RoboDojo. To push the capability frontier further, we explore joint human--robot pretraining with HumanWAM-Goal, a visual-goal-conditioned world--action model. Hybrid data scaling unlocks broad zero-shot generalization across both simulation and physical benchmarks, propelling post-trained RoboTwin 2.0 performance to new state-of-the-art levels: 92.70% on Clean2Clean and a substantial leap to 84.60% on Clean2Random. On physical robots, HumanWAM-Goal further exhibits emergent embodied in-context learning, dynamically adapting its manipulation behavior to unseen visual goals without parameter updates. To support reproducible scaling research in embodied AI, we open-source the Open-HumanWAM-50K corpus, data curation and pretraining pipelines, alongside the pretrained and post-trained HumanWAM checkpoints, inference code, and simulation evaluation suites.

candidates.title: Robonomics: A Toolbox for Governing AI’s Impact on Socioeconomic Systems
candidates.abstract: ROBONOMICS: A Toolbox for Governing AI’s Impact on Socioeconomic Systems advances a systematic framework for an emerging discipline devoted to the study of how artificial intelligence, robotics, and automation are reshaping contemporary socioeconomic systems. Combining insights from economics and sociology, Riccardo Campa develops an interdisciplinary approach to the governance of the robonomic system. Through social policy and scenario analyses, the book examines alternative responses to technological unemployment, technological impoverishment, and the broader challenges of automated societies. More than a survey of policy debates, this book provides both a conceptual foundation and a therapeutic toolbox for governing one of the most profound socioeconomic transformations of the twenty-first century.

candidates.title: Machine Learning-Enabled Rover For Autonomous Navigation In Rough Terrain
candidates.abstract: A hybrid perception-control framework for navigating rough terrains by remote YOLOv8n-based terrain classification combined with on-board safety-based control of rover is proposed. The system uses ESP32-WROOM-32 module for controlling motors, ultrasonic sensors for detecting obstacles, infrared sensors for detecting cliff edges, and watchdog communication, whereas ESP32-CAM is responsible for sending terrain images to a laptop where the inference algorithm works. Four-class terrain data consisting of 800 images of grass, sand, gravel, and soil is employed for fine-tuning YOLOv8n using stratified dataset. Terrain predictions control movements depending on traversability coefficients, while safety controls take precedence over remote controls when an obstacle or communication link is detected. The evaluation over 60 trials of outdoor navigation has resulted in terrain classification with an accuracy of 78.3% and successful navigation with an 80.0% success rate. The perception-to-action latency was 170±23 ms, fail-safe time was 1.02±0.04 s, and emergency braking was 310±45 ms. The power consumption of the rover was 4.22±0.35 W, and the estimated operational time was around 4.5 h. Such values characterize the performance of the limited resources rover that implements the separation of complex computation-based inference from motion control in embedded systems.

candidates.title: SenTrojan: Revealing Analog Hardware Trojan Attacks on Sensors
candidates.abstract: Sensors bridge the physical and digital worlds, making their integrity critical to cyber-physical system security. Existing sensor attacks largely exploit unintended and sensor-specific physical vulnerabilities, limiting their generalizability and motivating a different threat model, i.e., whether an adversary can implant hidden attack surfaces into sensors before deployment. In this paper, we present SenTrojan, an analog hardware Trojan framework for sensors. SenTrojan embeds malicious functionality into analog signal circuitry commonly shared across diverse sensor architectures, and activates the hidden behavior through crafted external physical signals. Once activated, SenTrojan can induce sensor malfunctions ranging from permanent denial-of-service to static or dynamic spoofing. To achieve these effects under different architectural constraints, we introduce two complementary designs. The Logic-Rule-Driven (LRD) Trojan adds lightweight analog monitoring logic to detect trigger features such as frequency and amplitude, enabling reliable activation across various sensor types. The Physical-Effect-Driven (PED) Trojan targets sensors with exploitable native analog effects, e.g., nonlinearity and rectification, and realizes attacks with minimal component insertion. We evaluate SenTrojan on 14 sensors spanning 6 transduction principles and demonstrate its effectiveness across diverse real-world scenarios. Overall, SenTrojan achieves an average successful trigger rate above 95%, maintains over 97% similarity to benign behavior, incurs zero false-trigger rate for LRD designs, and introduces less than 5% average deviation in drift, noise floor, and response time. To our knowledge, this work is the first systematic study of analog sensor Trojans, broadening sensor security from unintended physical vulnerabilities to intentional supply-chain compromise.

candidates.title: Haptic Shared Control for Multi-Robot Systems
candidates.abstract: Multi-agent systems offer significant advantages in terms of flexibility and redundancy, enabling the efficient distribution of complex tasks among multiple robots. However, their deployment requires advanced control strategies to ensure optimal cooperation between autonomous agents and human operators. We propose a modification of the global connectivity maintenance algorithm to incorporate measurements taken in agent's local frame, using sensors with limited fields of view. This algorithm, responsible for the autonomous behavior of the multi-robot system, is combined with different adaptive supervision strategies, allowing the user to exert control at varying scales over the entire group. (i) Single Agent Control (S): The operator directly controls a single robot, (ii) Pinning Control (P): The operator imposes constraints on multiple robots to influence the group, (iii) Centroid Control (C): The operator acts on the system's center of mass to steer the entire fleet. In conjunction with the connectivity maintenance algorithm, these methods ensure compliance with inter-agent constraints while providing haptic feedback to the user regarding the system's connectivity state. The effectiveness of these approaches was evaluated through a user study, comparing performance with and without haptic feedback across multiple scenarios tailored to the different control modes.

candidates.title: Boundary-Constrained Vision and Spectral Point-Cloud Filtering for 6-DoF Robotic Grasping of Hollow-Frame Porous Structures
candidates.abstract: Abstract Automated sorting and precision robotic manipulation of lightweight hollow- frame workpieces, such as lattice-style micro-unmanned aerial vehicle (micro- UAV) frames and topology-optimized industrial components, present acute perceptual bottlenecks for standard 3D visual sensing. Active infrared struc- tured light efortlessly traverses internal apertures and void cavities, interleaving upper surface contact points with underlying support table clutter and severely destabilizing 6-DoF grasp pose estimation. To resolve this geometric contam- ination without relying on CAD models or prior 3D templates, this paper proposes an integrated boundary-constrained perception and geometry-aware grasping pipeline tailored for porous and hollow-frame structures. The proposed architecture establishes an external-perimeter segmentation strategy utilizing a customized YOLOv8-seg network, explicitly masking out interior void regions at the visual source. The segmented depth cluster is back-projected into 3D camera coordinates and processed through a nearest-20% depth-quantile filter ( Q0 . 20 ) to decouple the top planar contact rim from vertical sidewalls. Local surface nor- mal vector extraction is formulated via Singular Value Decomposition (SVD) of the spatial scatter covariance matrix, accompanied by an analytical planarity spectral-ratio gate ( κ = λ 1 /λ3 ≥ 15 . 0 ) to reject non-planar degeneracies. In- plane rotational ambiguity is resolved by projecting the 2D contour axis onto the tangent plane, synthesizing robust grasp orientations on SO(3) via Lie algebra matrix exponential mapping. Perception and motion execution are coordinated across a distributed mechatronic testbed linking an industrial 6-DoF Aubo-i5 collaborative manipulator, an eye-in-hand RealSense D435i sensor, and an SMC pneumatic parallel gripper over a lightweight asynchronous JSON-RPC protocol. Experimental evaluations demonstrate a boundary segmentation mask mAP@0.5 of 0.995 across 106 annotated frames, alongside 68 physical workspace grasping trials yielding an empirical position jitter of 0.167 mm, an orientation jitter of 0 . 249◦ , and an overall geometric convergence rate of 98.5% (67/68 trials), verify- ing the system’s operational viability and numerical robustness under real-world laboratory conditions.

candidates.title: Stabilizing On-Policy Targeted Guidance in Agentic Reinforcement Learning
candidates.abstract: Naive on-policy RL is often bottlenecked by the capabilities of the base model --- insufficient coverage can result in an inability to learn from certain rewards. At the same time, rewards in modern post-training systems often come from rich textual sources, e.g. judge models with a rubric of criteria. Can we utilize such structures to provide a rich directional signal that enables improving on otherwise difficult to optimize rewards? In this work, we examine a framework we refer to as targeted guidance that learns from per-turn textual feedback via an on-policy self-distillation objective. Our focus is not only on directly improving hard-to-optimize behaviors, but on how to do so throughout the training process without degrading baseline RL performance. Over a range of settings across an agentic multi-turn software engineering environment, we find success by combining targeted self-distillation with a per-criteria RL reward, and by limiting feedback to turns where the policy specifically fails. We further examine the design choices that lead to stable entropy and reduce oscillatory behavior throughout training.

candidates.title: Prosthetic Heart Valve Orifice Area Detection By Using A Combined Shock-Anisotropic Coherence Filter To Improve Level Sets Algorithm
candidates.abstract: Abstract Prosthetic valve is a synthetic or tissue substitute for the natural valve. It is designed to mimic the natural valve’s normal opening and clos-ing motions. The need for replacing heart valves increased drastically as the heart valve diseases became one of the dangerous death cause in the world. “Global demand for prosthetic heart valve market expected to reach USD 5,302.1 million in 2021 and growing of 9% from 2016 to 2021”. Unfortunately, Biological valves tend to fail over time, requir-ing replacement in 30% of patients within 10 years and 50% within 15 years. The demands for testing prosthetic valves are crucial to main-tain a robustness, durability and compatibility to improve patient health care which insure a place in the global market. This article discuss a novel method for automatic detection of a leaflet edges around ori-fice area opening for PHV (Prosthetic Heart Valve). A pre-processing algorithm using a combination of Anisotropic and Shock filter is proposed to enhance image quality before using a level set to detect PHV edges. This technique shows great capabilities to detect leaflet edges and provide additional enhancement compared to the other works.

candidates.title: Large Language Models for Industrial Robots: Applications, Challenges, and Future Directions
candidates.abstract: With the accelerating intelligent transformation of global manufacturing, industrial robots have become critical equipment in modern smart factories. However, the growing prevalence of multi-variety, small-batch production has made the high programming threshold, tedious reconfiguration, and limited environmental adaptability of traditional industrial robots increasingly prominent. Over the past few years, large language models (LLMs) have proven to have strong semantic comprehension, knowledge reasoning, and task planning abilities, a new avenue in the intelligent upgrading of industrial robots. The systematic review of the literature on the topic of the industrial robot driven by LLM is presented in this paper, including the mainstream technical directions, and the representative studies in five areas of application: industrial inspection, assembly and collaboration, maintenance and fault recovery, manufacturing operation planning, and robot navigation. Based on this, the paper examines the key challenges to be addressed at present, including model output reliability and safety, the simulation-to-reality gap and real-time constraints, and data scarcity and distribution shift. It also discusses future research opportunities, including knowledge enrichment and reliable reasoning, lightweight deployment and edge computing, and life-long learning and domain adaptation. The purpose of this paper is to serve as a reference in future studies and implementation of LLMs in industrial robots.

candidates.title: Asynchronous Robot Policies
candidates.abstract: Scaling vision-language foundation models has significantly advanced generalist robot manipulation, but the increased model scale introduces computational latency that degrades real-time physical reactivity. Existing Vision-Language-Action (VLA) architectures execute high-level semantic reasoning and action ex- ecution sequentially within the primary control loop, creating a fundamental tension between semantic-reasoning capability and robot agility. To address this, we propose Asynchronous Robot Policy (ARP), an architectural framework that decouples semantic reasoning from low-level action generation using asynchronous processes operating at independent frequencies. In ARP, a high-capacity Vision-Language Model (VLM) asynchronously updates a semantic memory at low fre- quency, while a lightweight Vision-Action Expert, conditioned on this semantic memory, generates robot actions at a much higher control frequency. Such a formulation, enables having a fast perception-action loop without compromising on the semantic capability. To overcome asynchronous memory staleness, ARP trains the vision-action expert on the semantic staleness and execution delay, with temporally mismatched observation across processes. On Franka manipulation tasks, ARP achieves an 18% higher success rate and 20% less time need for execution in quasi-static setups, while 3-5 times baseline performance in dynamic simulation environments. Furthermore, ARP enables operating the VLM at 10 times lower than its nominal frequency with no significant performance loss making it much more efficient than the baseline. These results highlight the architectural advantages of modeling robot policies as asynchronous processes, enabling real-world reactive deployment without sacrificing the scale of foundation models.

candidates.title: Analysing responses to digital activism in Indonesia and Malaysia using AIDA framework
candidates.abstract: This article examines how six youth-led X accounts in Indonesia and Malaysia generated engagement and were associated with different forms of participation during the 2024 Indonesian presidential election and the 2022 Malaysian general election. Using the AIDA (Attention–Interest–Desire–Action) framework as a non-linear interpretive heuristic, it draws on platform metrics, interactional traces, and interviews with organisers. The study compares four candidate-centred volunteer accounts in Indonesia with two reform-oriented and civic education initiatives in Malaysia as an analytical contrast rather than a like-for-like national test. The findings show that spectacle and gamified formats scale Attention and affective Desire within platform attention economies, yet frequently remain associated with discursive, platform-proximate Action, revealing an action gap. In contrast, the Malaysian civic initiatives demonstrate stronger organisational and institutional linkages between online coordination, procedural participation and civic education. Situating AIDA within hybrid media ecologies and platform governance, the article argues that democratic effects depend less on visibility metrics than on organisational capacity and linkages to institutional processes. The study contributes to eParticipation research by distinguishing discursive-amplificatory, material-participatory, and institutional forms of Action and by specifying how platform logics condition their relationship to online engagement
