candidates.title: The Third Case: Prompt-Governed Agency under a Consciousness Hypothesis
candidates.abstract: English abstract Can an artificial agent have subjective experience while lacking unrestricted authority to replace its governing task objective? This paper treats that possibility as a distinct design and evaluation problem, termed the third case. It separates phenomenal consciousness, goal-directed behavior, operational competence, temporal continuity, and decision authority. The hypothetical case, a functionally testable candidate, and the evidence concerning experience are different descriptions. The prompt-issuer is an explicit role that may itself be occupied by a potentially experiencing executor under upstream constraints. The framework preserves the project-specific composition B-Core = A-Core ⊕ Purple Box/Present. A-Core denotes a potentially stateful, learning, multi-model cognitive and executive system; Purple is an undisclosed candidate addition with intended history-dependent causal effects. ESSENTIAL is a protected specification of constraints and revision authority, logically associated with A-Core. A targeted comparison with IDA, LIDA, adjustable autonomy, and existing agent controls, at the access levels stated in section 2.4, locates the proposal within established work. The contribution is a project-specific evaluation contract for externally governed, internally continuous execution, rather than a demonstrated new consciousness mechanism. Three limited analytical observations concern goal delegation, policy differences masked by a shared guard, and the gap between an architectural effect and consciousness. The proposed studies distinguish causal relevance from practical benefit, score feasible completion and justified infeasibility separately, and control initialization, history transfer, order, and dependent observations. No empirical result or proof of phenomenal consciousness is claimed. Functional findings could remain valuable if the consciousness hypothesis is rejected; credible welfare concerns would require assessment that task success alone cannot resolve. Magyar absztrakt Lehet-e egy mesterséges ágensnek szubjektív átélése úgy, hogy közben nincs korlátlan jogköre irányadó feladatcéljának lecserélésére? A tanulmány ezt a lehetőséget önálló tervezési és értékelési problémaként kezeli, és harmadik esetnek nevezi. Elkülöníti a fenomenális tudatosságot, a célirányos viselkedést, a működési kompetenciát, az időbeli folytonosságot és a döntési jogkört. A hipotetikus eset, a funkcionálisan vizsgálható jelölt és az átélésre vonatkozó bizonyíték eltérő leírások. A promptot kiadó szereplő kifejezetten meghatározott szerepet tölt be, amelyet maga is betölthet egy esetleg átéléssel rendelkező, a hierarchia felsőbb szintjéről korlátozott végrehajtó. A keretrendszer megőrzi a projektre jellemző B-Core = A-Core ⊕ Purple Box/Present összetételt. Az A-Core egy potenciálisan állapotos, tanuló, több modellt használó kognitív és végrehajtó rendszert jelöl; a Purple egy nem közölt felépítésű kiegészítőjelölt, amelynek előzményfüggő oksági hatásokat szánnak. Az ESSENTIAL a korlátok és a módosítási jogkör védett specifikációja, amely logikailag az A-Core-hoz kapcsolódik. Az IDA-val, a LIDA-val, az állítható autonómiával és az ágensek meglévő irányítási megoldásaival végzett célzott összevetés a 2.4 szakaszban megadott hozzáférési szinteken helyezi el a javaslatot a korábbi munkák között. A hozzájárulás a külsőleg irányított, belső folytonosságú végrehajtás projektspecifikus értékelési szerződése, nem pedig egy bizonyított új tudatossági mechanizmus. Három korlátozott érvényű elemzési megfigyelés foglalkozik a célok delegálásával, a közös védelmi mechanizmus által elfedett döntésipolitika-különbségekkel, valamint az architekturális hatás és a tudatosság közötti különbséggel. A javasolt vizsgálatok megkülönböztetik az oksági relevanciát a gyakorlati haszontól, külön pontozzák a megvalósítható teljesítést és az indokolt megvalósíthatatlanságot, továbbá kontrollálják az inicializálást, az előtörténet átvitelét, a sorrendet és a függő megfigyeléseket. A tanulmány nem állít empirikus eredményt vagy a fenomenális tudatosság bizonyítását. A funkcionális eredmények akkor is értékesek maradhatnának, ha a tudatossági hipotézist elvetik; a hitelt érdemlő jólléti aggályok olyan értékelést igényelnének, amelyet a feladatsiker önmagában nem rendezhet.

candidates.title: Coordinating a Robot Swarm in a Warehouse by Aggregate Programming: A Case Study
candidates.abstract: Abstract Multi-robot systems (MRS) are becoming increasingly relevant within diverse application domains, including warehouse logistics, where robots are in charge of moving and storing crates, by navigating through the warehouse shelves. Engineering such robust multi-robot systems is a significant challenge, especially if the goal is to build a fully decentralized system, without single points of failure, or potential bottlenecks. Aggregate Programming (AP) is an established approach to engineering resilient distributed systems, which has already been applied successfully for building prototypes in Industrial Internet of Things and robotics scenarios. In this paper we present an in depth description of how we have exploited AP for designing and simulating a MRS to address a non-trivial farm warehouse logistics case study proposed by a company operating in the Autonomous Mobile Robots (AMR) market, which cooperated in this research. Importantly, to better validate the implemented prototype, we have relied on two different levels of simulation, one scalable and high-level, and another one small-scale but highly realistic.

candidates.title: Hierarchical Scene Graph Concepts for Spatial AI in Robotics
candidates.abstract: Robots deployed in structured indoor environments need to reason about their surroundings at several levels, from the geometry around their sensors, through the individual elements that populate the scene, up to the topology of the building. Constructing this knowledge as it moves is the problem of Simultaneous Localization and Mapping (SLAM), which recovers a metric map that semantic SLAM then labels element by element. 3D Scene Graphs (3DSGs) add the relations among them and, above the observed elements, stack the High-Level Spatial Concepts (HLSCs), such as rooms and floors, that are not observed directly but synthesized from the entities they aggregate. Coupled into the SLAM optimization as geometric factors, these concepts turn the hierarchy into a Factorized 3DSG (F3DSG) whose structural regularities constrain the estimate, while also giving the tasks that build on the map an abstraction over which to reason, from path planning to global localization against an architectural plan of the building. The HLSCs in use today, however, remain limited to rooms and floors, each handcrafted for its concept type and validated only in simple layouts, leaving a thin hierarchy whose benefit is only partially realized, both for the estimation of the map and for the downstream tasks that global localization would exploit but existing methods have yet to reach. This thesis advances a unified treatment of the generation and exploitation of HLSCs, developed across seven appended articles and organized along three research directions. The first concerns the generation of HLSCs from the planar wall surfaces the robot observes as it maps, replacing the concept-specific heuristics of prior work with a single learned formulation that jointly detects each concept and infers its metric attributes. It progresses from the detection of rooms and walls in controlled layouts to the joint generation of a complete hierarchy, from rooms up to floors, buildings, and a city, evaluated by a novel scene-graph-level generation metric that scores structural, semantic, and metric fidelity together. The second integrates the generated concepts into the SLAM backend as optimization factors, generalizing the factor definition across concept types and deriving each factor covariance from the same learned predictors that produce the HLSCs, so that the weight of every factor dynamically reflects the reliability of its own detection and inference rather than a fixed, manually tuned uncertainty. This removes the per-concept design that prior factorization required and couples the whole hierarchy into the F3DSG, estimated online alongside the trajectory to improve both trajectory and map. The third exploits the HLSCs in global localization, matching the online representation against the architectural prior over the hierarchy and semantics the two share rather than the geometry alone. It progresses from a top-down candidate search that exploits the hierarchy to remain tractable, through an incremental matching that localizes under the deviations of the built environment from its plan while estimating those deviations, and a semantic disambiguation of structurally symmetric layouts, to an end-to-end learned formulation that matches heterogeneous 3DSGs at a near-constant cost as they grow. Across these directions, the proposed methods enrich the information the HLSCs synthesize and model, generalize the methodological approach that produces and exploits them, and extend their validity to operating conditions of increasing layout complexity, from rectangular rooms to real architectural floor plans spanning multiple floors and buildings. All contributions are validated in real indoor environments mapped with LiDAR, with the semantic primitive labeling and HLSC generation further demonstrated on RGB-D data.

candidates.title: Foundation Models for Autonomous Space Robotics: Architectures, Physical Adaptation, and Validation
candidates.abstract: Space robots must interpret tasks and act despite unfamiliar dynamics, difficult sensing conditions, and limited opportunities for human intervention. Foundation models offer reusable perceptual and behavioral knowledge, but their value depends on how that knowledge reaches physical execution. This critical review follows space-specific requirements through perception, prediction, planning, and action to deployment and validation, emphasizing orbital manipulation and proximity operations. Terrestrial comparisons establish benefits of particular pretraining stages and model interfaces; their transfer to space dynamics and constrained onboard operation remains insufficiently tested. Event cameras offer timely motion observations across strong illumination contrasts, while spiking neural networks provide possible routes to sparse local computation. We examine how sensor degradation, state estimation and computing choices affect feedback and recovery. Higher action throughput need not yield fresher feedback; lower processor power can also coexist with higher energy per inference. We organize validation as an iterative sim-to-ground-to-space pathway, connecting physical tests with telemetry-based diagnosis and closed-loop revalidation. A satellite-capture example links observations to approach, contact and recovery, while a corresponding protocol separates generalization from adaptation with limited target-domain interaction. These comparisons identify what models already contribute and the physical evidence needed to support autonomous space operation.

candidates.title: Pedicel-Targeted Strawberry Harvesting via Imitation Learning on a Low-Cost Teleoperated Robotic Arm
candidates.abstract: Precise pedicel-targeted grasping in strawberry harvesting remains a critical bottleneck due to the pedicel's small diameter (1.3-3 mm), color similarity with surrounding foliage, and precise force control required for clean abscission zone detachment. As a market-grade crop, strawberry aesthetic value makes bruise-free pedicel detachment essential over direct fruit grasping. Classical approaches struggle to unify vision models, motion planning, and contact manipulation into a robust framework, particularly in occluded canopy environments. Therefore, this work presents a visuomotor imitation learning pipeline for pedicel-targeted strawberry harvesting that unifies perception, motion planning, and contact manipulation from collecting human teleoperation demonstrations, training an Action Chunking with Transformers (ACT) policy with a ResNet-50 visual backbone, and deploying the learned policy autonomously on a Jetson AGX Orin edge platform at 15 Hz. The trained policy achieved consistent loss convergence from 2.84 to 0.091 over 100K gradient steps on 130 demonstrations. We have also established a reproducible open-source pipeline with publicly released dataset and model weights for the agricultural robotics community. Full dataset is available at, https://huggingface.co/datasets/nitindominicrai/strawberry_pedicel_grasp_teleoperation and trained policy at, https://huggingface.co/nitindominicrai/act_strawberry_pedicel. To replicate this work, all code, configurations, and deployment instructions are publicly available at, https://github.com/nitin-dominic/autonomous_strawberry_pedicel_harvesting.

candidates.title: Cancer and Artificial Agriculture: Converging Gene-Editing Toolkits, Governance, and Climate-Resilient Food Systems
candidates.abstract: Abstract Elevated atmospheric CO₂ at projected mid-century concentrations reduces iron and zinc concentrations in C3 staple crops, deepening hidden hunger in populations already dependent on those staples, while the same exposure has been reported to increase the risk of cancer and other non-communicable diseases. Responses to date remain fragmented: biofortification, offline agricultural diagnostics and gene-editing governance are studied in isolation, no framework connects climate-driven nutrient dilution to community-scale intervention, and the gene-editing toolkit and governance questions common to artificial agriculture and oncological research have not been considered together; meanwhile, centralised and cloud-dependent agritech systematically fails low-connectivity rural populations. Here we present and appraise an integrated artificial-agriculture model combining transgene-free CRISPR–Cas9 SDN-1/2 biofortification, a decentralised low-cost sensor network with an offline KNN classifier for soil and crop diagnosis, community-scale organic soil-regeneration practice, and open-access licensing under the FAO International Treaty, and we assess its evidence base through a structured synthesis of 50 peer-reviewed studies. The classifier attained author-reported precision and recall of approximately 86% across cotton, rice, wheat and zinc-fortified maize classes. Claim-by-claim appraisal rated CO₂-driven micronutrient dilution, biofortification efficacy and India's SDN-1/2 regulatory exemption as strongly supported, and product-specific performance, the reported ₹75,000 laboratory cost and the combined soil-regeneration package as weakly supported; gap analysis identified the absence of community-deployment evidence as the principal limitation. Decentralised, transgene-free artificial agriculture is therefore credible as a synthesis of proven components, but not yet as a validated, deployment-ready system, for mitigating hidden hunger and its reported oncological consequences under climate change; multi-location field trials of edited staples under elevated CO₂, leakage-resistant external validation of offline models, and comparative cost-effectiveness studies of community laboratories are the priorities this work establishes.

candidates.title: Enhanced engagement during infant‐like robot‐mediated telepsychiatry in an older patient with delirium and cognitive impairment
candidates.abstract: Psychiatrist shortages in general hospitals, particularly in rural areas, have increased interest in telepsychiatry as a means of improving access to specialist care. 1 However, patients have reported challenges with videoconferencebased telepsychiatry compared to in-person consultations, including difficulty speaking up, asking questions, and establishing a therapeutic relationship with clinicians. 2 These challenges may be greater among older hospitalized patients, whose age-related sensory and cognitive impairments can hinder reciprocal communication in videoconference settings.3 Delirium, which is common in this population, is characterized by disturbances in attention and arousal, 4 further limiting optimal engagement during telemedicine.Therefore, alternative communication interfaces that can enhance engagement during remote consultations may be beneficial.Robot-mediated interactions can facilitate the disclosure of sensitive experiences and enhance social engagement.[5][6][7] Furthermore, a robot's

candidates.title: The Portrayal of Robots in Isaak Asimov’s Runaround and other Stories-An Evaluation
candidates.abstract: Isack Asimov’s robot stories made a significant impact on how science fiction portrays robots, as he consistently depicted them as altogether something else than monsters. In hindsight, while Asimov readily took credit for such innovativeness, he also noted that the stories were a simple reaction against the “Robot-as-Menace” type of story, referring the less frequent variety of “Robot-as-Pathos” stories where the robot was a “lovable” creature “usually put upon by cruel human beings”.On the other hand, the Three Laws also provide Asimov the guidelines for creating plots and help readers solve his puzzle stories. His short story, Runaround is explicitly about the Three Laws and how they cause a standstill situation, which can be solved only by the engineers’ capacity to test hypotheses and find the solution by exploiting the Laws.

candidates.title: “Integration of Embedded AI and Medical Heat Pipes in Robotic Neurosurgery: A Novel Framework Based on Elmas’s Thermodynamic Theory”
candidates.abstract: Objective: This study presents an interdisciplinary framework that autonomizes the thermal management of high-temperature laser ablation and ultra-low-temperature cryoprobe applications, which represent opposing thermal poles in robotic neurosurgery operations. The thermal sensitivity of neural tissues and the risk of permanent neuron damage developing at temperatures above 43°C necessitate a micron-level stable thermal control. Accordingly, the study aims to optimize surgical robots both in terms of hardware and software. Method: The theoretical foundation of the study is based on the principles of “ELMAS’s Thermodynamic Theory”, the “5th Law of Thermodynamics”, and “Bio-Robotic Resonance” developed by Asst. Prof. Dr. Emin Taner Elmas. In the hardware layer, dual-phase medical heat pipes integrated into the tip of the robotic arm (end-effector), having a diameter of 0.8 mm, flexible, and containing sintered copper powder micro-capillaries with water-graphene nano-fluid, were utilized. In the software layer, an embedded artificial intelligence (AI) engine supported by machine learning models was developed, capable of real-time data processing from micro-sensors on the heat pipe and performing digital twin-based live thermal mapping (HUD). The validation of the system was designed with a 5-step validation protocol encompassing computerized thermal modeling, synthetic gel tests, ex-vivo organ tests, in-vivo animal experiments, and preclinical human simulation. Findings: The integration of the micro-heat pipe provided passive cooling without requiring an external energy source, thereby suppressing peripheral heat dissipation (thermal dissipation) during laser operations and maintaining healthy neural tissues within a stable range of 37°C - 38°C. In cryoprobe applications, it acted as a passive heat barrier, creating reverse thermal gradients along the probe shaft, protecting healthy tissues along the entry path while performing instantaneous shock freezing cycles (freeze-thaw) at the target tumor site. The predictive algorithms of the AI engine predicted the thermal saturation at the tissue border milliseconds in advance and successfully activated the haptic lock (fail-safe) mechanism that applies resistance to the surgeon’s master control arms at critical thresholds. Conclusion: The developed autonomous thermal management architecture elevates surgical robots beyond being merely devices that produce mechanical motion into intelligent protective shields that thermally sense the tissue. The integration of Dr. Elmas’s medical thermodynamics equations into robotic software demonstrates at a preclinical level that a micron-level precise, autonomous, and thermally safe hybrid surgical platform can be established for brain tumor resections.
